10. Nichole Grzych | From Creative Expression to a Life of Purpose

An evolving journey shaped by creativity, motherhood, faith, and the determination to keep moving forward.

Some journeys are defined by the things people create, while others are shaped by the experiences that change how they see the world. For Nichole Grzych, both have played an important role. Her journey has moved through poetry, art, writing, modelling, and entrepreneurship, while personal experiences have influenced the values and beliefs she carries into everyday life.

In 2005, Nichole founded Code Break Services, beginning a creative journey that has continued to evolve over the years. From publishing poetry and articles online to contributing to books and magazines, creating music, and maintaining an active presence across social media, she has explored different ways of expressing herself and connecting with others.

Beyond her creative pursuits, Nichole’s story is also shaped by motherhood, faith, personal resilience, and a commitment to self-improvement. In this conversation, she reflects on the experiences that have influenced her, the importance of staying connected to her beliefs, and the principles that continue to guide her life.

A Creative Journey Shaped by Experience

We wanted to understand how Nichole’s creative journey began and how it has developed over the years.

In 2005, she started her own business, Code Break Services, as its founder. She began by publishing articles and poems online and getting published in poetry books. She also gave away her handmade art and poetry books in exchange for donations and published a few songs on CD and MP3. Today, she models and writes for WordPress, Fashion Republic, Lure, and Influential Women magazines, while maintaining an ongoing Facebook presence that she considers her journal.

Family and motherhood can change the way people understand responsibility, relationships, and their priorities. For Nichole, these roles have taught her the importance of selfless love and responsibility.

Finding Purpose Through Faith and Personal Growth

Personal experiences can have a lasting influence on a person’s relationship with faith. Nichole shares that her past experiences with abuse and trafficking shaped her spiritual journey and continue to motivate her to better herself and succeed.

Living with purpose, according to Nichole, also means setting daily goals, building healthy habits, taking care of one’s body and health, and maintaining a relationship with faith. She believes in studying the Bible, following the teachings of Jesus Christ, and sharing His love.

Staying connected with others is another important part of her life. Through her writing and publications, social media presence on Facebook, Instagram, and LinkedIn, and everyday interactions at gyms, coffee shops, restaurants, stores, family gatherings, and church, she continues to build connections with people around her.

When it comes to navigating difficult times, Nichole relies on her faith and focuses on balance. She also prioritises her health through medication, vitamins, herbs, supplements, and exercise.

Her advice to others is to become independent, find answers for themselves, and build a support system along the way. She encourages people to read the Bible and daily devotionals, pray, attend church, and treat others as they would like to be treated.

A Journey Guided by Creativity and Faith

Nichole Grzych’s journey brings together creative expression, personal experiences, family, and faith. From starting Code Break Services in 2005 to exploring writing, poetry, music, and modelling, she has continued to find different ways to express herself and share her experiences.

Her reflections highlight the importance of the values that guide her: independence, self-care, faith, and responsibility towards others. While her creative pursuits continue to evolve, these principles remain central to how she approaches life.

For Nichole, personal growth is an ongoing process, shaped by everyday choices, meaningful relationships, and the determination to keep moving forward.

LinkedIn 

Conclusion

The future of business will be shaped by those willing to think differently and act with purpose. The leaders featured in this edition demonstrate how fresh perspectives, calculated risks, and a commitment to progress can influence entire industries.

Their journeys reflect the changing nature of leadership, where adaptability and the willingness to explore uncharted territory are increasingly valuable. Each brings a distinct perspective to the challenges and opportunities ahead.

As new possibilities emerge, their contributions serve as a reminder that the future is not simply something to anticipate. It is something that determined leaders have the opportunity to create.

On Tuesday nite, Talarico’s supporters celebrated his victory on enormous television screens at a watch party in Austin, the state capital. title: Anthony Zurcher: On This Historic Nite, Democrats Advance Well Into Trump’s Heartland
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: On a nite that will rock American politics for years to come, Democrats tore up Donald Trump’s political blueprint. Republicans were swept out of power by a blue tidal wave that swept over the country following a series of significant Senate victories in states that had been consistently Republican for decades, and in Kansas’ case, almost a century. The Democrats have regained a majority in the Senate and are now firmly in charge of the House of Representatives halfway through President Donald Trump’s second term. They will have the power to thwart Trump’s plans and start looking into his administration. There may possibly be a historic third attempt at impeachment. In the months following Trump’s return to the White House in January 2025 with united Republican control of Congress, few thought such a result was conceivable. Democrats hoped to retake the House as public opinion shifted against him and his party. However, they considered an unfriendly Senate map made up of states Trump had easily carried just two years prior. Rather, Democrats changed the political landscape by winning in North and South Carolina, Texas, Maine, Kansas, Ohio, and Iowa. Trump promised to reach agreements with congressional Democrats in remarks to CBS, the BBC’s US partner, adding that he didn’t want to have to spend his last two years in office opposing their policies. Later, he posted a photo of his signature red baseball cap with the word “veto” printed on it to Truth Social, somewhat undermining that statement. The president continued by saying that although his name was not on the ballot this year, Republicans would have won handily if it had been. However, Trump had encouraged people to act as though he was running for reelection and had assisted in elevating several of those Republican candidates. title: Canva Announces Significant Layoffs Following “Our Hardest Year Yet”
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: One of Australia’s most well-known start-ups, Canva, has announced a reorganisation that would impact 22% of its employees, including layoffs. According to co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins, it was “without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history” and 1,271 employees will either lose their jobs, be asked to relocate, or change responsibilities. Concerns over how artificial intelligence (AI) would affect the company’s operations and the expense of integrating the technology into its platforms have reportedly caused the firm’s value to decline in the last year. Perkins wrote to employees that it had been “our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade.” According to Perkins, the “incredibly hard decision” resulted in “significant changes.”For some, this will entail being asked to move to centralised hubs or having their roles changed. Unfortunately, it will also mean bidding farewell to friends and comrades who have contributed to Canva’s current state. The company, which employs people in 37 countries, announced that starting next year, hybrid workers will be expected to spend two to three days in the office and that Sydney would become the “primary home” for more of its product teams. Blackbird Ventures and Airtree, two of its backers, reportedly reduced its valuation earlier this year from A$60 billion ($41.8 billion; £31.1 billion) at the end of the previous year to roughly A$49 billion. title: Two Helicopters Collide Close to Everest Base Camp, Killing an Indian Visitor
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Two officials have verified to the BBC that an Indian tourist died when two helicopters collided while trying to land close to Mount Everest’s base camp. At roughly 08:15 local time (02:30 GMT) at Pheriche, around 12 kilometres (7 miles) south of Mount Everest Base Camp, verified video of the collision showed the two aircraft’s chopper blades striking each other as they came into land. Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu was identified by helicopter business Fishtail Air as the victim of the collision. The helicopter firm reported that the pilot and another passenger were hurt in the crash, which included one of its vehicles. According to a statement from Fishtail Air, the injured passengers and crew members on board were saved and transported to Kathmandu. Bhupendra Thapa, a Solukhumbu district administrator, informed BBC Nepal that the injured passenger was a visitor from New Zealand. According to the company, Air Dynasty operated the other chopper that was involved and had been transporting cargo. It further stated that only one crew member operated it and was unharmed. Gyanendra Bhul, a spokesman for the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, stated: “It appears the accident happened when two helicopters… attempted to land at the same spot.” The weather appears to be clear and there are no noticeable severe wind impacts in the incident’s video footage. It looks like one helicopter is descending faster than the other. title: Voters Will Cast Ballots in Elections That Might Determine Trump’s Final Chapter
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Donald Trump, who has dominated American politics for the past 10 years and drastically changed it, faces potentially crucial elections with two years left in his presidency. Additionally, his Republican Party is facing a challenging time ahead of the midterm elections on Tuesday that will determine control of Congress. The majority of voters claim that the cost of living is their top worry. The president’s harsh tariffs and unpopular conflict with Iran have contributed to the surge in food and fuel prices, which will be a major concern for many voters as they cast their ballots. Trump has been actively campaigning, leading dozens of rallies around the nation despite facing record low support ratings in recent months. On Monday, he delivered his final speech in front of the controversially renovated Reflecting Pool in Washington, DC. He claimed that Republicans “gave this a very strong shot” during the midterm campaign. However, people on all sides are concerned about rising costs ahead of the election, which helps to explain why he has been campaigning in formerly strong Republican territory, making appearances in Iowa and Kansas during a final weekend blitz. Additionally, his party has invested hundreds of millions of dollars in campaign advertising in these historically secure elections, like the Kansas Senate contest. title: Officials Claim That the Jet May Have Torn Apart Before to the Florida Disaster, with a Family Listed Among the Deceased
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Parts of a private jet that crashed in Florida and killed all nine people on board may have come off while it was in the air, according to investigators. When the Learjet 60 crashed into a multi-lane highway and detonated upon impact, it was travelling from Austin, Texas to the Bahamas. The 20-year-old co-pilot and a digital entrepreneur and his young family were among those who passed away on Sunday. The massive hole the jet left on the Palm Beach road made it difficult for the US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) to retrieve the debris, but it stated that meteorological conditions would be a primary focus of the investigation. At approximately 12:50 local time (17:50 GMT), the jet crashed on Military Trail, a six-lane road with shops and eateries.”Recovering the major wreckage from the impacted crater on the roadway will be our biggest challenge,” lead investigator Tim Monville stated during a press briefing on Monday. According to the NTSB, strong storms caused the crater, which is next to a mobile home park entrance, to partially fill with water. At the time of the collision, there had been reports of thunderstorms and heavy rain in the vicinity. The area’s homes, businesses, and sports grounds were all littered with debris. title: Before the Midterm Elections, the US Bombs an Iranian Island
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: US officials have informed CBS, the BBC’s US partner, that the US has launched strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of Iran fired on a US aircraft, prompting the government to describe the strikes as limited and defensive. Explosions on Qeshm were reported on Monday by Iran’s official news agency, Irna. The IRGC reported that its forces had shot down a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait of Hormuz and two US MQM-170 drones south of the island, but they did not comment. The strikes, which occurred as negotiators increased their efforts to avert a return to full-scale conflict following Tuesday’s US midterm elections, have not been addressed by the US military. Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February, Trump has been under pressure to stop the war from both his Republican Party and declining poll numbers. The president told reporters earlier on Monday that there was “no rush” to increase the number of strikes against Iran.We’ll take action in one way or another, but there’s no rush. We financially ruined them,” he said to news agency Axios. “They have no money, no petrol and their people are getting very tired of it.” In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, he also stated that the US “might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain],” an underground location connected to Iran’s nuclear program. title: Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar: Building Technology for a More Inclusive Global Economy
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar is the Chairman and Founder of EST Group and a global technology strategist working across financial services, digital transformation and inclusive innovation. With around three decades of experience in banking, fintech and emerging technologies, he has focused his work on using digital systems to address economic and social challenges. Based within the Cambridge Innovation Center in the MIT ecosystem, EST Group brings together initiatives across fintech, agritech, healthcare, education, deeptech and sustainability. Rather than developing these areas in isolation, Dr. Sindhu is building an interconnected ecosystem designed to connect technology with practical needs, particularly in rural communities and underserved markets. We spoke with him about his journey, the thinking behind EST Group, financial inclusion, emerging technologies and his vision for sustainable development. A Career Shaped by Financial Transformation We began by asking, “You have spent around three decades working across banking, financial services and emerging technology. What first drew you towards transforming the financial ecosystem, and how has your thinking changed over the years?” Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar explained, “My journey has been shaped by a belief that finance should serve as an engine of economic development. Banking has traditionally been built around established systems, processes and institutions. But as I worked across financial services and technology, I began to see how much more could be achieved by connecting these systems with emerging digital capabilities. The financial sector is not just about transactions. It influences how people build businesses, access opportunities and participate in economic growth. Yet large sections of the population, particularly in rural and underserved communities, continue to face barriers to financial services. Over the years, my thinking has moved beyond digital banking as a technology upgrade. I see it as an opportunity to redesign how financial services connect with people, businesses and communities. This requires combining banking principles with technologies such as AI, blockchain, digital identity and connected platforms. For me, the real measure of transformation is not how advanced a system appears. It is whether it makes financial services more accessible, useful and responsive to the needs of the people who depend on them.” Building an Interconnected Ecosystem Through EST Group EST Group brings together ventures across several sectors, including fintech, agritech, healthcare, education and deeptech. We asked, “What led you to build EST Group as an interconnected ecosystem rather than a collection of separate technology businesses?” Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar shared, “I have always believed that many of the challenges facing communities cannot be solved through one product or one sector. Financial inclusion, agriculture, healthcare and education are closely connected. If we address one area without considering the others, the impact can remain limited. This thinking led us to build EST Group as an interconnected ecosystem. For example, a farmer’s agricultural and carbon data can support access to financial products. A remote healthcare service can connect with a digital wallet. Students who gain technology skills through our education initiatives can also contribute to projects within the wider ecosystem.” “Each vertical has its own purpose, but the larger value comes from how they work together. Our initiatives span fintech and digital inclusion, agritech and carbon credits, healthcare, edtech, deeptech and the space economy. We also believe that building an ecosystem requires collaboration. We work with startups, universities, researchers, governments, financial institutions and entrepreneurs. The aim is to bring different capabilities together and create solutions that can respond to real needs across markets.” Dr Sindhu further added. Rethinking Banking and Financial Inclusion Digital banking and financial inclusion remain central to Dr. Sindhu’s work. His vision is to make banking as intuitive as unlocking a phone with a fingerprint. We asked, “What needs to change in the traditional banking model to make financial services more accessible, particularly for people in rural and underserved communities?” Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar noted, “Banking needs to become easier to access and simpler to use. For many people, particularly in rural communities, the challenge is not only the availability of financial services. It is also the complexity of accessing them and the distance between traditional banking institutions and everyday needs. I believe banking should become as intuitive as unlocking your phone with a fingerprint. People should not have to navigate complicated processes to access basic financial services. Technology can help make this possible through digital banking, wallets, payment gateways, lending systems and secure digital identities. However, digital development banking must retain the principles of classical banking. Trust, security, accountability and sound financial practices remain essential. Emerging technology should strengthen these principles rather than replace them. Our work through initiatives such as BranchX, Ezipay Global and other fintech ventures is connected to this wider vision. We want to help create financial systems that reach more people and support economic participation across different communities.” Connecting Agriculture With Digital Finance One of EST Group’s major areas of work is agritech, with initiatives focused on rural ecosystems, carbon assessment and digital financial access. We asked, “Why has agriculture become such an important part of your work, and how can technology improve the economic opportunities available to farmers?” “Agriculture is central to the livelihoods of a large part of the world’s population. Yet farmers often face challenges at different stages of their work, from accessing resources before cultivation to managing production and reaching markets after harvesting. We need to look at agriculture as a complete economic ecosystem. Technology can help connect these stages through better information, digital systems and access to financial services. Through EST AgrX and related initiatives, we are working on decentralised rural ecosystems that link pre-farming, farming and post-farming activities. Our work also includes AI-driven soil and carbon assessment, which can help connect agricultural activity with sustainability and carbon-credit opportunities. The larger objective is to improve the way rural economies function. Agriculture and finance should not operate as separate worlds.” Dr Sindhu Bhaskas added. Bringing Healthcare

Rather than developing these areas in isolation, Dr. Sindhu is building an interconnected ecosystem designed to connect technology with practical needs, particularly in rural communities and underserved markets.

We spoke with him about his journey, the thinking behind EST Group, financial inclusion, emerging technologies and his vision for sustainable development.

A Career Shaped by Financial Transformation

We began by asking, “You have spent around three decades working across banking, financial services and emerging technology. What first drew you towards transforming the financial ecosystem, and how has your thinking changed over the years?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar explained, “My journey has been shaped by a belief that finance should serve as an engine of economic development. But as I worked across financial services and technology, I began to see how much more could be achieved by connecting these systems with emerging digital capabilities.

The financial sector is not just about transactions. It influences how people build businesses, access opportunities and participate in economic growth. Yet large sections of the population, particularly in rural and underserved communities, continue to face barriers to financial services.

Over the years, my thinking has moved beyond digital banking as a technology upgrade. I see it as an opportunity to redesign how financial services connect with people, businesses and communities. This requires combining banking principles with technologies such as AI, blockchain, digital identity and connected platforms.

For me, the real measure of transformation is not how advanced a system appears. It is whether it makes financial services more accessible, useful and responsive to the needs of the people who depend on them.”

Building an Interconnected Ecosystem Through EST Group

EST Group brings together ventures across several sectors, including fintech, agritech, healthcare, education and deeptech. We asked, “What led you to build EST Group as an interconnected ecosystem rather than a collection of separate technology businesses?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar shared, “I have always believed that many of the challenges facing communities cannot be solved through one product or one sector. Financial inclusion, agriculture, healthcare and education are closely connected. If we address one area without considering the others, the impact can remain limited.

This thinking led us to build EST Group as an interconnected ecosystem. For example, a farmer’s agricultural and carbon data can support access to financial products. A remote healthcare service can connect with a digital wallet. Students who gain technology skills through our education initiatives can also contribute to projects within the wider ecosystem.”

“Each vertical has its own purpose, but the larger value comes from how they work together. Our initiatives span fintech and digital inclusion, agritech and carbon credits, healthcare, edtech, deeptech and the space economy.

We also believe that building an ecosystem requires collaboration. We work with startups, universities, researchers, governments, financial institutions and entrepreneurs. The aim is to bring different capabilities together and create solutions that can respond to real needs across markets.” Dr Sindhu further added.

Rethinking Banking and Financial Inclusion

Digital banking and financial inclusion remain central to Dr. Sindhu’s work. His vision is to make banking as intuitive as unlocking a phone with a fingerprint. We asked, “What needs to change in the traditional banking model to make financial services more accessible, particularly for people in rural and underserved communities?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar noted, “Banking needs to become easier to access and simpler to use. For many people, particularly in rural communities, the challenge is not only the availability of financial services. It is also the complexity of accessing them and the distance between traditional banking institutions and everyday needs.

I believe banking should become as intuitive as unlocking your phone with a fingerprint. People should not have to navigate complicated processes to access basic financial services. Technology can help make this possible through digital banking, wallets, payment gateways, lending systems and secure digital identities.

However, digital development banking must retain the principles of classical banking. Trust, security, accountability and sound financial practices remain essential. Emerging technology should strengthen these principles rather than replace them.

Our work through initiatives such as BranchX, Ezipay Global and other fintech ventures is connected to this wider vision. We want to help create financial systems that reach more people and support economic participation across different communities.”

Connecting Agriculture With Digital Finance

One of EST Group’s major areas of work is agritech, with initiatives focused on rural ecosystems, carbon assessment and digital financial access. We asked, “Why has agriculture become such an important part of your work, and how can technology improve the economic opportunities available to farmers?”

“Agriculture is central to the livelihoods of a large part of the world’s population. Yet farmers often face challenges at different stages of their work, from accessing resources before cultivation to managing production and reaching markets after harvesting.

We need to look at agriculture as a complete economic ecosystem. Technology can help connect these stages through better information, digital systems and access to financial services.

Through EST AgrX and related initiatives, we are working on decentralised rural ecosystems that link pre-farming, farming and post-farming activities. Our work also includes AI-driven soil and carbon assessment, which can help connect agricultural activity with sustainability and carbon-credit opportunities.

The larger objective is to improve the way rural economies function. Farmers should be able to participate in more structured systems, access relevant services and create greater value from their work. This is also where financial inclusion becomes important. Agriculture and finance should not operate as separate worlds.” Dr Sindhu Bhaskas added.

Bringing Healthcare Closer to Underserved Communities

Healthcare is another part of EST Group’s ecosystem, with initiatives focused on remote diagnostics and access to primary care. We asked, “What role can technology play in improving healthcare access in regions where medical facilities and resources remain limited?”

According to Dr Sindhu Bhaskar, “Access to healthcare remains uneven across many regions. People in remote communities may have to travel long distances to reach medical facilities, and this can delay diagnosis and treatment.

Technology can help reduce some of these barriers. Remote diagnostics, AI and robotics can support healthcare delivery in areas where access to medical professionals and facilities is limited. The aim is to make primary healthcare more accessible and connect people with services that may otherwise be difficult to reach.

Through EST RAHA and EST Healthcare, we are working towards this direction. These initiatives are part of a wider approach in which healthcare connects with other parts of the ecosystem, including digital identity and financial services.

I believe technology should help bring essential services closer to people. Its value should be measured by the difference it makes in access, delivery and the everyday lives of communities.”

AI, Blockchain and the Next Phase of Digital Infrastructure

Dr. Sindhu’s work also extends into agentic AI, blockchain, digital identity, quantum technologies and industrial applications. We asked, “As these technologies develop, where do you see their greatest potential, and what should organisations consider before adopting them?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar shared, “AI, blockchain and other emerging technologies are creating new possibilities for how organisations operate and how services are delivered. But adopting technology simply because it is new is not enough. We need to understand the problem first and then identify the right technology to address it.

AI can support analysis, automation and decision-making. Blockchain can contribute to secure digital infrastructure and identity systems. Agentic AI introduces another dimension by allowing systems to carry out tasks towards defined goals. Each of these developments has potential, but they also require careful consideration of governance, security and accountability.”

He further added, “Organisations should look at how these technologies fit into their existing systems and what outcomes they are expected to deliver. They must also consider the people affected by these changes.

At EST Group, our approach is to explore technology across practical applications, including digital finance, agriculture, healthcare and manufacturing. We are interested in solutions that can work across different environments and contribute to long-term development.”

Knowledge Sharing and the Next Generation of Innovators

Alongside his commercial ventures, Dr. Sindhu leads EST FAB, a knowledge-empowerment initiative with 35 global chapters. Its programmes include webinars, international internships and mentoring, conducted on a pro bono basis. We asked, “Why is knowledge sharing such an important part of your work, and what do you hope to achieve through EST FAB?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar reflected, “Knowledge should not be restricted by geography or economic background. There are talented students and young entrepreneurs across the world who have the ability to contribute, but they may not always have access to the right networks, practical learning opportunities or industry exposure.

EST FAB was developed to help address this gap. Through our global chapters, we organise webinars, knowledge exchanges, technology forums and internship programmes. These initiatives give students opportunities to learn from professionals and gain exposure to projects across areas such as fintech, blockchain, agritech and healthcare.

The programme is conducted pro bono because I believe access to knowledge should not depend on a person’s financial circumstances. We also encourage young people to become active contributors rather than simply recipients of information.

My aim is to build a network of creators and carriers of change. Young people should have the opportunity to develop ideas, work with experienced professionals and take part in solving real-world challenges.”

Leadership, Collaboration and Global Partnerships

With initiatives and partnerships spanning multiple countries, Dr. Sindhu’s work depends on collaboration across institutions, industries and regions. We asked, “How do you approach building partnerships across different markets, and what have you learned about leading an ecosystem with such a wide range of stakeholders?”

“Building across different markets requires an understanding of local needs. A solution that works in one country may need a different approach in another because the financial systems, regulations, infrastructure and community requirements can vary.

I believe partnerships are essential because no single organisation can build everything independently. We bring together financial institutions, technology companies, universities, researchers, investors and entrepreneurs to complement one another’s capabilities.

Our presence across multiple countries has reinforced the importance of understanding these differences. It is not enough to introduce a technology and expect it to work everywhere. We need local knowledge, trusted partners and the ability to adapt to the environment.

My approach to leadership is therefore collaborative. I value people who bring different experiences and perspectives. The strongest ecosystems are built when participants have a shared purpose and can contribute their expertise towards a wider goal.” Dr Sindhu explained.

Looking Ahead: Technology With a Human Purpose

As EST Group continues to expand across sectors, Dr. Sindhu remains focused on connecting technology with sustainable development and human progress. Lastly, we asked, “What is your long-term vision for EST Group, and what would you like its work to achieve for communities and economies around the world?”

Dr. Sindhu Bhaskar concluded, “My long-term vision is to build an ecosystem where technology, finance, sustainability and knowledge work together to improve human lives. We are working across several sectors, but the underlying purpose remains consistent: to create systems that support economic participation and make essential services more accessible.

I see significant opportunities in rural development, financial inclusion, sustainable agriculture, healthcare and digital education. These areas need solutions that are connected rather than isolated. When financial services support farmers, when healthcare reaches remote communities and when young people gain access to technology education, the impact can extend across generations.

We will continue to develop our initiatives, strengthen partnerships and explore emerging technologies. But growth alone is not the objective. What matters is whether the work creates lasting value for people and communities.

I often return to the belief that real transformation occurs when technology, sustainability, knowledge and humanity evolve together. That is the direction I want EST Group to continue pursuing.”

title: Noelene Buckrell | Building Technology That Keeps People in Control
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Noelene Buckrell is the Founder and CEO of Techlani Group, a New Zealand technology company developing AI-enabled products across safety, intelligence and accessibility. With a background in biomedical science and experience in emergency communications, financial management, operations and language services, she brings a different perspective to technology. Her work is guided by a consistent belief: AI should increase human capability without removing human authority. Through products such as Screengnie, Northern Intelligence and Arabic Lens, Noelene is exploring how technology can make information more useful, improve safety and address practical challenges. We spoke with her about her journey, the ideas behind her ventures and her views on the future of AI. A Journey Into Technology We began by asking, “Your professional journey has taken you through biomedical science, emergency communications, financial management, operations and language services. How did these experiences lead you towards building technology products?” Noelene explained, “My route into technology was not planned in the traditional sense. I came from a biomedical science background and worked across several different fields, including emergency communications, financial management, operations and language services. What connected these experiences was the need to understand information and make decisions in situations where the consequences mattered. In emergency communications and high-stakes operational environments, having more information does not always make a situation easier to manage. You need to recognise what is important, understand the risks and know what requires attention. Over time, I became increasingly interested in how technology could help solve these problems. Our work sits at the intersection of technology, cybersecurity and human behaviour. We are interested in how technology can help families, communities and organisations understand digital risks, reduce exposure and respond with greater confidence. At this stage, we are focused on building and testing structured systems that prioritise prevention, clarity and ethical design. We also work through workshops and advisory sessions to help non-technical decision-makers understand the digital challenges they face. Parents can receive large amounts of information and alerts, but that does not always help them understand what is serious or what needs their attention. Our approach is built around identifying meaningful communication threats without overwhelming parents with unnecessary notifications. We want to help people recognise the signals that matter rather than adding more noise to an already difficult digital environment. The philosophy behind Screengnie is ‘less noise, only signals.’ It is about making online safety information more useful and helping parents focus on situations that may require attention. Northern Intelligence focuses on helping organisations turn expanding volumes of information into intelligence they can actually use. The goal is to make complex information easier to understand and more useful for decision-making. I believe AI can help people work through complexity, but the responsibility for decisions should remain with the people who understand the context and consequences. Intelligence is valuable when it improves understanding and supports sound judgment.” Making Arabic Content More Accessible Another product in Noelene’s portfolio is Arabic Lens, which focuses on language accessibility. We asked, “What inspired the development of Arabic Lens, and why is making Arabic video content more accessible important?” Noelene Buckrell shared, “Arabic Lens is another example of how technology can address a practical problem. Arabic Lens is being developed to make Arabic video content more accessible through transliteration and English translation. It brings together language technology and accessibility to help more people understand and engage with content.” “Although this product addresses a different need from Screengnie and Northern Intelligence, the thinking is similar. Keeping Human Judgment at the Centre of AI

As AI becomes more involved in everyday decisions, questions around trust, responsibility and governance are becoming increasingly important. We asked, “You believe AI should increase human capability without removing human authority. How should businesses approach this balance as they introduce intelligent systems?”

Noelene noted, “I believe AI should increase what people are capable of doing, not remove their authority to make decisions. Technology can help process information, identify patterns and support faster responses, but it does not always understand the full human context behind a situation.

Businesses need to think carefully about where AI is being used, what decisions it influences and who remains responsible for the outcomes. Trust cannot come from technology alone. It also depends on transparency, appropriate safeguards and clear accountability.

Human discretion matters, particularly in situations involving safety, risk or personal consequences. People need to understand when to rely on a system, when to question it and when a decision requires human judgment.

As AI becomes more embedded in organisations, I believe responsible design and governance will become increasingly important. The aim should be to build systems that help people make better decisions while keeping them involved in the process.”

Building Through an Unconventional Path

Noelene’s journey into technology did not follow the traditional route through a computer science degree or established technology companies. We asked, “You have described your journey as an unconventional route into technology. What has this taught you about entrepreneurship, and why do you believe proof of work is becoming more important than traditional qualifications?”

“I did not enter technology through the usual route. My background is different, and I had to learn what was required by identifying problems, finding ways to solve them and building the knowledge needed along the way.

That experience has shaped my belief that proof of work is the new résumé. What matters is not only what someone has studied or where they have worked. It is also what they can demonstrate, build and bring into the world.

AI is lowering some of the technical barriers that previously made it difficult for people to create products. This creates opportunities for people with different professional backgrounds and experiences to contribute to technology.

I think we will see more founders who come from outside the traditional technology industry. They may understand a particular problem through their own experience and then use the tools available to build a solution. The ability to learn, test ideas and demonstrate real progress will matter enormously.” Noelene Buckrell added.

Looking Ahead: Building With Purpose

Lastly, we asked Noelene about the direction of Techlani Group and what she hopes to achieve through its growing portfolio: “As you continue developing Screengnie, Northern Intelligence and Arabic Lens, what are your priorities for the future?”

She concluded, “We are still early in the journey, and that is a deliberate position. We are building, testing and learning as we develop products that address different needs across safety, intelligence and accessibility.

Our priority is to build deliberately and make sure the products have a clear purpose. That means understanding the problems they are designed to solve, testing the systems and maintaining a strong focus on responsible development.

Each product has its own direction, but they are connected by a wider belief that technology should filter complexity, strengthen human judgment and keep people in control of important decisions.

I am also interested in the opportunities to work with organisations and partners that share this approach to responsible technology and human-centred safety.

title: A Well-Known Australian Children’s Novelist was Imprisoned for Charges Involving Child Exploitation
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Craig Silvey, an Australian children’s novelist, was given a seven-month prison sentence for having and disseminating content that exploits minors. Judge Hayley Cormann described Silvey’s behaviour as “repulsive” and “degrading” when imposing her punishment. Police raided Silvey’s Western Australian house in January and confiscated a number of electronic devices, leading to his arrest. The 44-year-old was imprisoned in October while awaiting sentencing after entering a guilty plea to possessing and distributing child exploitation material in May. The father of three is most renowned for his children’s book Runt and his critically acclaimed young adult novel Jasper Jones, both of which were later adapted into motion pictures.According to WA Today, Cormann remarked on Monday, “You have devastated and betrayed the trust of thousands of people, and you have let entire communities down.” Police claimed that when they arrived to raid Silvey’s home, he had open online discussions in which he talked about child exploitation. Silvey had called himself “extremely open minded” and “obsessed with taboos” in them, the court heard. Detectives discovered pictures and films of other adults assaulting children on his devices, and he had talked to another member of a pornographic website about his sexual interest in youngsters as young as five. title: After the Biggest Cryptocurrency Hack Ever, Binance Users Took out $3.6 Billion
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Customers withdrew $3.6 billion (£2.7 billion) from Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, when it reopened on Sunday after what is thought to be the worst hack in history. Following the incident, which affected $6.3 billion worth of digital assets, the company halted all transactions. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other prominent organisations have accused North Korea of being behind the cyberattack. About 95% of the assets taken in the incident have been covered, according to the company, but it might take longer to find the remaining amount. Binance has stated time and again that it will pay for all losses associated with the hack. Binance stated on X: “Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion.” Withdrawals “are stabilising as expected” after a “initial spike” and subsequent fall. According to Binance, Sunday’s net withdrawals make up slightly more than 2% of the $171 billion in assets it manages. The company announced last week that it has set aside almost $6.3 billion to deal with the attack’s aftermath. Samira staged a spectacular foot escape from Iran by negotiating perilous mountainous terrain. She describes herself as a “one-woman army fighting the regime” and currently resides in hiding overseas. She is determined to identify the security personnel and officials she believes fired lethal bullets during the protests in an effort to find justice and accountability following the loss of her daughter.Finding me won’t be simple, but they’ll take me to the edge of death before killing me. Go back to your regular life? “There’s no turning back,” she declares. Since the beginning of the year, the BBC has spoken with a number of Iranians, including Samira. title: A Small Jet Crashes on a Florida Street, Killing Nine People
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: According to the US Transport Secretary, nine persons were killed when a business plane crashed in a Florida area on Sunday. Around 12:50 EST (17:50 GMT), the collision occurred close to Cresthaven, around nine miles (14 km) from Mar-a-Lago, President Donald Trump’s resort in the affluent Palm Beach County neighbourhood. No one on the ground was harmed, but photos show a sizable hole in the midst of a multi-lane road with flames and Learjet 60 aircraft debris strewn across it. According to a statement from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the plane had taken off from Austin, Texas, and was en route to the Bahamas. Before crashing, the jet was falling hundreds of feet per second, according to flight analysis. Someone in the aircraft can be heard reporting “moderate turbulence” and the crew was “managing the ice” in air traffic control audio that was captured just prior to the collision. The statement that the plane was “picking up precipitation” and “we need to climb” is then audible. Shortly after, the same voice reported that the plane was falling at a speed of 10,000 feet per minute (3,048 meters per minute). At a press conference in Atlanta, Georgia, where he was hosting G20 foreign ministers for a two-day meeting, Rubio stated, “We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. However, Rubio stated that Trump “hasn’t made a decision” regarding more military action, despite rumours that the US president may launch an assault following Tuesday’s crucial midterm elections. Rubio stated that Trump would prefer a diplomatic option to stop the war with Iran, even as he denounced Tehran for “actively and openly” attacking commercial vessels. However, he did not promise a timeframe for negotiations. Other than to say that we would be open to a diplomatic solution, I won’t describe the state of those negotiations or provide a timeline,” Rubio stated. title: Before a Major Opposition march in Delhi, Indian Authorities Increase Security
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The location of a planned opposition protest in Delhi on Sunday, which is expected to call for the resignation of the nation’s election chief over a contentious modification of voter lists, was encircled by Indian security forces armed with batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles. Prior to the protest march and rally, which Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi would lead, authorities issued a warning about traffic delays. Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to participate in what the opposition claims would be a significant challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Since last month, opposition parties, student organisations, and the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party have staged almost daily protests calling for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign due to the voter list alteration, which they claim favours the BJP. Senior police officer Rohit Rajbir told ANI, “People have begun to come to participate in this rally. We have ensured proper arrangements at the venue, and arrangements are also planned on the route of the march that will happen in a few hours.” The Indian Express newspaper revealed in September that Kumar’s two deputies had voiced multiple internal concerns regarding voter list modifications, registration procedures, and digital systems, which sparked the protests calling for Kumar’s resignation. title: Xi Promotes “Party Discipline” at a Political Gathering in China, Resulting in a Record Number of Purges
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As China’s Communist Party wrapped off a significant annual political meeting with the highest number of empty seats ever recorded, a record 33 members were dismissed. There were 279 Central Committee members present at the fifth plenum, compared to 315 at the fourth in October 2025 and 364 at the third in July 2024. Party discipline took center stage during this week’s meeting, in contrast to previous plenums that concentrated on social and development issues or economic reforms. Since assuming power in 2012, Xi Jinping has made combating corruption a top priority, referring to it as the “biggest threat” to the party. Following a four-day closed-door meeting at a Beijing hotel, a statement was released on Thursday stating that sixteen of the thirty-three individuals removed are from the military. Beyond “serious disciplinary and legal violations,” it’s unclear what precise allegations these members are facing. Under Xi’s anti-corruption effort, such general accusations have become commonplace. According to Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar at Carnegie China, it is now “an effort to consolidate and maintain authority”In this instance, the campaign will go on and grow based more on Xi’s sense of security than any actual corruption problem. The party declared that it will “enforce strict party self-governance, including turning the knife inwards to… curb disorder” and that it had “squarely confronted the grim reality that party leadership had at times weakened or hollowed out” in its statement. title: Days After Announcing Thousands of Layoffs, Microsoft’s Revenues Rise
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Just days after announcing intentions to reduce its employment by more than a quarter, IT giant Microsoft reports that its profits for the three months ending in September surged to more than $36.6 billion (£27.5 billion). The Windows creator announced on Monday that it would provide buyouts to some 60,000 employees in order to reduce expenses while investing billions of dollars in artificial intelligence (AI). Microsoft, like many other large tech companies, is making significant investments in the infrastructure that underpins artificial intelligence, even though it is yet unclear if these expenditures will be profitable. In New York’s after-hours trade on Wednesday, Microsoft shares increased by over 2.9%. Investors have been keeping a careful eye on tech companies’ recent financial performance in order to determine whether the significant expenditure on AI is sustainable. It is anticipated that major internet firms like Amazon, Meta, and Alphabet will spend over $700 billion on AI processors and data center infrastructure this year. Due to robust growth in its cloud computing sector, Microsoft reported on Wednesday that its quarterly revenue increased to $92.3 billion, up 19% over the same period last year. A 30% increase in sales for Microsoft Cloud, its suite of enterprise technology services, boosted the company’s earnings. title: Partial Results Indicate That Netanyahu’s Bloc is Dominating the Israeli Election But Does not Have a Majority
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is leading his opponent, former military leader Gadi Eisenkot, according to partial results of Israel’s general election, although he still lacks a majority in parliament. Netanyahu’s Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish partners were on course to secure 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset with 85% of the votes counted. Three additional Jewish opposition groups in Eisenkot’s coalition, together with his Yashar party, were scheduled for 48. The two leaders have declared that they will attempt to establish a coalition for governance. All but one of the Jewish parties have promised not to cooperate with Arab-led parties, who are expected to win an unprecedented 19 seats and potentially become kingmakers. It may yet take a day or two for the final election results to be announced because between 430,000 and 480,000 absentee ballots from military and diplomats have not yet been counted. Following their confirmation, President Isaac Herzog will speak with all political parties and invite the leader he thinks has the best chance of forming a cabinet. This process may take weeks. There would eventually need to be another election if they are unsuccessful. title: If Democrats Take Over Congress, They Might Start Four Probes
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In the event that they win a majority in either the House or the Senate in next week’s midterm elections, Democrats in the US Congress are already preparing how they would exercise their authority. Even while midterm elections can occasionally be nasty for the current party holding the White House, success is by no means assured. However, control of the chamber would grant the party the authority to issue subpoenas, which are summonses to testify or produce documents, as well as increased funding to begin investigations early in the next year. Democrats are debating whether to look into the president and other high-ranking Trump administration officials. According to those familiar with the conversations, staff members have started compiling a list of potential probes and witnesses. These are some possible Democratic goals in the event that the party wins on November 3. title: Dolores Huerta, a 96-Year-Old American Civil Rights Activist, Dies
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Dolores Huerta, a pioneering US civil rights activist who supported underprivileged farm labourers, passed away at the age of 96, according to her family. In the 1960s and 1970s, the well-known labour organiser fought for the rights of agricultural workers alongside fellow labour leader Cesar Chavez. Together, they founded the revolutionary United agricultural Workers Union (UFW). Through her foundation, Huerta carried on her advocacy efforts on voting and immigration-related issues.Family spokesman Erik Olvera stated on Wednesday, “As you can imagine, this is an extremely difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family.” Huerta’s death from cancer has been confirmed by the BBC. Huerta was raised in Stockton, California, in the center of the state’s significant agricultural sector, despite being born in New Mexico. Her mother, who used to work at a cannery, reared her. After graduating from college, Huerta worked as a teacher before establishing labour unions and leading the Chicano power movement. She became the emotional focal point of a number of revolutionary groups advocating for improved living and working conditions and salaries for the underprivileged. Later, while raising eleven children, she worked on environmental concerns, women’s and civic rights, and gender equality. She carried on with that work far into her 90s.According to several accounts, she once said, “I would like to be remembered as a woman who cares for fellow humans.” “Our life should be used to improve the world, not only to obtain possessions. title: Leading Bahraini Companies Show Interest in Exports of Moscow Technologies
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The Mosprom Export Support Center arranged a series of meetings between Moscow industrial companies and potential clients in Manama. The parties to the talks discussed joint projects in construction, IT and telecoms, as well as supplies of sweet goods to the local market. This was reported by Maksim Liksutov, Deputy Mayor of Moscow for Transport and Industry. “The capital is a confident leader among Russian regions in terms of trade with Arab states. Moscow accounts for over 30 percent of Russia’s total sales with these countries. The Kingdom of Bahrain is one of the promising markets for scaling up Moscow’s high-tech exports. Pharma and medicine, power engineering, robotics, additive technologies, and IIoT projects have great potential for bilateral cooperation,” Maksim Liksutov emphasized. To expand trade and economic ties and scale up the presence of Moscow solutions in the region, the Moscow export support center “Mosprom” organized a business mission to Manama. “The talks in Bahrain were attended by developers of microelectronics and representatives of the food, consumer goods, and construction industries of the capital. In total, they held about 50 meetings with counterparties, including leading players in the local telecoms and construction markets, food distributors, and retail chains that also operate in neighboring countries, for example, in Oman and the UAE,” Anatoly Garbuzov, Minister of the Government of Moscow, Head of the Moscow Department for Investment and Industrial Policy, noted. Neoros, a developer and manufacturer of high-speed optical transceivers based on photonic integrated circuits and a resident of the Technopolis Moscow special economic zone, joined the talks. Its portfolio already covers a joint project with partners from Saudi Arabia. In Bahrain, company representatives met potential clients, including integrators of telecoms, network infrastructure, and data center (DC) solutions, in particular, the operator stc Bahrain and the local IT and telecom provider Almoayed Group. A new line of wavelength division multiplexing equipment was presented for DCs. Another party to the business mission was Moscow-based Invisiline (Nevidimye Reshetki), which manufactures innovative ventilation diffusers. title: Two in Court on a Purported Plot at RAF Fairford Connected to Iran
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Westminster, London resident Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, is accused of aiding a foreign intelligence agency, which police had previously stated they thought was Iran. On August 22, Nouman Essghir, a 24-year-old Westminster resident, was charged with accessing a forbidden area for a purpose detrimental to the United Kingdom. This was just weeks before he and four other men were caught near the Gloucestershire airbase. On Tuesday, the two made their appearance at Westminster Magistrates’ Court. On September 27, three suspicious vans were spotted close to the US-run airbase, prompting the declaration of a serious incident. A massive perimeter was erected around the base, and dozens of locals were evacuated. Police found a lot of petrol in the vans but no explosive materials. Vans with the “Fuel2You” emblem were seen near the base, the court heard. The vans were rerouted when they encountered a Ministry of Defence Police cordon in the early hours of the morning. Five males were taken into custody by the arriving police. They later disclosed that someone had reported what was happening by calling 999. Essghir verified his name and residence while standing in the dock at Westminster Magistrates’ Court while sporting a grey sweater. Abdulkarim is accused of aiding in the scheme. He showed up in court in a wheelchair, dressed in jeans, a baseball cap, and a checked shirt. He verified his residence and name. The 2023 National Security Act is the basis for the charges against both men. They were informed that the case will be heard at the Old Bailey on November 20. title: A Documentary Accusing Modi and Adani of Cronyism is Ordered to be Removed by an Indian Court
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: After Adani Enterprises filed a lawsuit alleging it was defamatory, an Indian court ordered the removal of an online documentary that Hotmail co-founder Sabeer Bhatia had posted accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and billionaire Gautam Adani of cronyism. The High Court in the eastern city of Kolkata was informed by Adani’s flagship company, Adani Enterprises, that the documentary, which received millions of views on social media in recent days, was full of false information and had prompted questions from some of the company’s investors, who were not named in the court order. The documentary “is not an account of proceedings or a news report.” The court’s late-Monday takedown order for YouTube, X, and Meta stated, “It is a dramatised narrative.” Opponents of Modi have frequently claimed that the prime leader has a tight relationship with Adani and that the business magnate has been treated favourably over the years. Both the Adani group and the Indian government have consistently refuted those claims. Adani Enterprises informed the court in its challenge that while it does not aim to limit constructive criticism of corporate concentration or government policy, Bhatia had concealed important information, per the court’s ruling. The US-based Bhatia stated on his X account that the case seeks damages of 500 million rupees ($5.25 million). He wrote “Truth is on my side” in one X post.He stated, “I think the documentary has rattled Adani Enterprises Limited and struck a nerve at the highest levels. title: Due to a Scheme Involving a UK Airbase, Two Men are Accused with National Security Offences
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Following an incident at a British airbase operated by the United States last month, UK anti-terrorism police announced on Tuesday that two men have been charged with national security offences, connecting the fear to Iran. Two 24-year-old British males have been prosecuted, according to Laurence Taylor, chief of National Counter Terrorism Policing: one is accused of aiding a foreign intelligence agency that is thought to be in Iran, while the other is accused of entering a forbidden area with intent “prejudicial” to the United Kingdom. Police detained seven individuals in the days that followed before releasing them on bond, thus this is the first time that anyone has been charged in connection with the incident. Early on September 27, a nearby farmer reported a group of individuals with multiple white vans involved in “suspicious” activities, prompting police to respond to the Royal Air Force’s Fairford airfield in southwest England. The United States immediately removed all of its B-1 bombers from the base a few days later. Two of the suspects were re-arrested, according to police a week ago; one of them has now been charged. Nouman Essghir, 24, was accused by police of going into or near a “prohibited place” for a reason “prejudicial” to the interests of the United Kingdom. Prior to his re-arrest by police a week ago, Essghir was detained at the scene in Gloucestershire and then freed on bail. Without providing any specifics, the police chief stated that the charge against Essghir was related to “suspected activity” on Saturday, August 22, more than a month prior. Mohamed Ahmad Abdulkarim, 24, the second individual charged, was taken into custody following a cautious questioning conducted over the past week, according to the police. title: In a Ukrainian City Where People Had to Eat Weeds to Survive, a Truce has Begun
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where citizens are stranded without access to electricity, water, or food, a ceasefire has been declared. The restricted ceasefire is being observed, according to Ukrainian officials and Russia’s defence ministry. According to the White House, US First Lady Melania Trump negotiated the ceasefire, which will permit relief delivery and a civilian evacuation on Friday. Along the front line in the Kherson region, Oleshky is encircled by Russian forces on one side and Ukrainian positions on the other by the Dnipro River. To survive, several locals have turned to cooking yard weeds. They have told the BBC that they are really hungry and wish to leave. One local expressed anxiety that the ceasefire would not last, stating, I don’t believe in Russia’s humanity.” Kyiv estimates that only 1,700 people are currently residing in Oleshky, but up to 6,000 individuals—including 200 children remain in the city and its environs. 24,000 people lived there before to the conflict, but Russia took control of it in the early stages of its full-scale invasion in February 2022. The situation has gotten so bad that not only is it very hard to bring supplies into the city, but it’s also quite risky to flee because the routes out of Oleshky are mined and vulnerable to drone attacks. title: Investors Who Deny Fraud Allegations and Mislead Authorities are Fined $210,000 by Dubai
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: An investor who denied prior fraud charges and provided false information to the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) was fined more than $210,000 (Dh771,330). In addition to failing to produce documentation, the investor, Gary Joseph Peters, misled the authorities by giving incorrect and misleading information about his work and criminal past. The regulator claims that from November 2020 to June 2022, Peters worked for a company that was licensed by DFSA. According to the employment contract, he served as the company’s chief operational officer, managing partner, and public relations officer. The DFSA discovered that Peters gave “misleading and deceptive” information during a mandatory interview by falsely denying that he had previously been found guilty of crimes involving fraud or other dishonest behaviour. According to DFSA, Peters was charged with and entered a guilty plea in three different incidents involving fraudulent and criminal activity in another jurisdiction, with his actions violating Article 66 of the Regulatory Law 2004. In addition to the penalties, the DFSA, the independent regulator of financial services at the Dubai International Financial Center (DIFC), has banned Peters from working for a company that is authorised by the DFSA and limited his ability to conduct business with DIFC. According to a statement from the DFSA, “Mr. Peters was not and has never been a DFSA Authorised Individual.” Also Read: Stablecoin Payments Could be Made by AI Agents as Early as 2027 On the Basis of Energy Security, the UK Permits the Long-Delayed Jackdaw Gas Field

title: Xi Might “Tighten Discipline” Within the Party During China’s Major Political Gathering
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: A significant political event is taking place in the Chinese capital, including a private meeting of high-ranking officials that may influence the future direction of the ruling Communist Party. The Fifth Plenum, which brings together some 300 Central Committee members, is expected to lead to a “tightening of discipline” among Party members, according to official media. After recent purges, Xi Jinping will have a chance to further solidify his hold on power at the four-day session that began on Monday. Although the yearly plenums are often quite confidential, a more comprehensive paper and a summary of conclusions will be released afterward. At least once a year, the Party’s central committee meets behind closed doors. Each five-year term of the Central Committee typically consists of seven plenums, which are seen from a distance since they are intended to convey the goals of the leadership. The date of this year’s meeting is significant since the next Party Congress is one year away, at which time a new central committee will be selected and a new set of priorities will be established. Although the Party’s top leadership is officially chosen by the Central Committee, the actual selection procedures are kept under wraps within the Party elite. After term restrictions are eliminated, Xi will most likely be reappointed as the nation’s leader by the upcoming Party Congress. title: Families of Palestinians Are Uprooted as Israeli Troops Demolish Homes in Hebron
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: According to local reports, the Israeli force has begun a massive crackdown in the occupied West Bank, destroying houses and businesses in Hebron and uprooting hundreds of families. Israeli bulldozers were seen wreaking havoc in footage that was circulated online; at least one street appeared to have been completely destroyed. Additionally, the military has sealed off the city, severely limiting the 200,000 citizens’ freedom of movement. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced the operation on Friday in reaction to two Palestinian militants attacking a checkpoint and murdering two Israeli troops. The shooters were killed, and three additional Israeli soldiers were hurt. Netanyahu declared on Friday that the two gunmen’s home areas and the surrounding structures would be “destroyed” after the attack. title: Meta Deal Helps Zuckerberg Foot bill for Possible Wins California Billionaires’ Tax
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Meta has struck a new deal with its chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, to keep him in California over a planned state tax on billionaires. The deal will give Zuckerberg, who is said to be worth more than $200bn (£149bn), more Meta shares as compensation for the portion of his money he may lose if voters approve the tax in November. The plan would levy a one-time 5% tax on residents with net worth over $1 billion. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay almost $10 billion in increased state taxes. The settlement with a special committee of Meta followed “robust, and at times contentious negotiations,” according to a financial filing Wednesday. Most of the US’s technology giants are based in California, which is home to some 225 billionaires, according to campaign group Americans for Tax Fairness. In recent years, the wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has grown. At the same time, his estimated effective tax rate in California was below 1 percent a year. Last month Zuckerberg informed Meta’s board he was considering transferring his primary residence out of California, and potentially selling his place in the state. His two primary houses in California are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe. title: After Discovering a Cyber-Security Problem, Services are Racing to Upgrade Their Computer Systems
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Organisations and corporations are still trying to upgrade their systems after cyber-security holes were discovered in PHP, a popular programming language. Websites worldwide went offline on Wednesday and Thursday after PHP developers disclosed “critical vulnerabilities” in the back-end language, which has powered online development for decades. Researchers warned that the “severe” faults might expose millions of sites that use it to potential hackers if not patched, prompting the UK government to take some sites offline as a precaution. So yet, no successful attempts have been reported, but experts believe any impact may take weeks or months to become apparent. Downing Street stated on Thursday that “some” limited government services “may be offline” while security measures were being implemented. The information I have is that 32 Government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable,” said technology minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra in the House of Lords. She explained that this “largely resulted from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied”. title: A Famous Shark That was Escorted out of the South Korea Canal Declined to go out to Sea
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: After being led out of a canal on Wednesday, a well-known dusky shark from South Korea is still hanging around. When the shark, known as Bukangi, was seen swimming in a canal in the southeast port city of Busan last month, it caused an unexpected stir. Rescuers used big nets for weeks in an unsuccessful attempt to return it to the open sea. Authorities announced on Thursday that they had strengthened obstacles to stop Bukangi from going back. However, it has not yet ventured out into the open ocean and has been continually returning to the waterway’s entrance. In Busan, opinions on the shark’s rescue were divided; some believed it should remain, while others thought it would be best for it to leave. It took more than eight hours for rescue personnel to carefully steer the three-meter-long (10-foot) shark toward open water in a port during a livestreamed operation on Wednesday. At the park with a view of the canal, hundreds of devoted spectators gathered to cheer and bid the shark farewell. However, Bukangi apparently broke through an official barrier on Thursday morning and swam back into the canal. Bukangi was imprisoned for a while in the canal between two layers of nets. title: Stablecoin Payments Could be Made by AI Agents as Early as 2027
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As autonomous systems increasingly perform purchases and financial transactions on behalf of users, artificial intelligence agents may play a significant role in the adoption of stablecoins as early as 2027, according to digital asset executives at the ADGM Global Media Forum. According to Andrej Majcen, co-founder and group CEO of Bitcoin Suisse, the quick advancement of AI may lead to the emergence of a new class of economic players that can conduct transactions with little assistance from humans.”I anticipate that the proliferation of AI agents will occur in 2027,” Majcen stated. He clarified that AI agents will require quicker and more effective payment methods as they grow more autonomous. Majcen anticipates that these systems will progressively favour stablecoins and other digital assets because to their programmability and efficiency, even though they could still accept conventional payment methods like credit cards. Digital assets known as stablecoins are made to have a comparatively steady value, typically by being connected to a conventional currency like the US dollar. Within the next three to five years, AI bots may start communicating directly with one another, according to Edward Hong, Senior Executive Officer of Hashed Global Management and Chief Platform Officer and Partner of Hashed. He clarified that because these computers might autonomously make purchases, access data, and pay for computer services, there would be a need for quick, programmable payment infrastructure that could facilitate international transactions. title: On the Basis of Energy Security, the UK Permits the Long-Delayed Jackdaw Gas Field
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: LONDON: The Jackdaw North Sea gas field was cleared by Britain on Wednesday, concluding years of legal and political fighting as the Labour administration tries to strike a balance between energy security concerns and climate aspirations. According to Energy Minister Miatta Fahnbulleh, the project will start supplying gas by the end of this month, which will assist reduce energy bills that have increased due to the Iran War. US President Donald Trump has frequently urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to increase North Sea drilling due to the impact of rising energy prices on people and businesses, which has negatively impacted Britain’s economy. The government described Jackdaw as “a source of national strength” during a time of global turmoil, claiming it would increase local gas production by roughly 6% at peak output and run for up to 11 years. According to Reuters calculations based on official statistics, Jackdaw would supply slightly less than 4% of Britain’s daily petrol demand at its anticipated peak production of 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. Burnham stated, “It’s right that we look responsibly at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help at a time when people are really struggling.” Also Read: As Tech Tensions with China Persist, the US Prohibits the Government From Using DeepSeek AI Russia Claims it is Prepared to Start Peace Negotiations With the US and Ukraine

title: Patients with Thalassaemia in the UAE now Have More Options Thanks to Gene Therapy
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: With the help of advanced gene therapy, Yas Clinic and the Abu Dhabi Stem Cells Center (ADSCC) have shown encouraging results in treating thalassaemia. Fahad, a 43-year-old patient, is no longer dependent on frequent blood transfusions to manage his condition. Fahad had transfusion-dependent thalassaemia for a long time; in order to keep his haemoglobin levels steady, he needed blood transfusions every three to four weeks. His general health and quality of life were affected by a number of long-term transfusion-related problems, such as iron overload and the requirement for regular iron chelation therapy, in addition to the continuous burden of treatment. Fahad was referred to Yas Clinic and ADSCC about a year and a half ago, when both organisations were attempting to bring cutting-edge gene therapy therapies to the United Arab Emirates. One of the most important developments in the treatment of inherited blood disorders is gene therapy, which may provide a long-term solution for individuals who might not have access to a suitable donor for bone marrow transplantation. Fahad was determined to be a good candidate for gene therapy after thorough medical evaluations, intensive testing, and thorough interdisciplinary assessments. His course of treatment coincided with national initiatives, backed by the UAE’s government and Department of Health, to bring this cutting-edge therapy to the country, opening up new avenues for patients to receive cutting-edge care nearer to their homes. Fahad’s own stem cells were harvested for the procedure, genetically altered, and then reinfused after preparatory therapy. The method, which is comparable to an autologous transplant, uses the patient’s own genetically altered cells to treat the disease’s root cause.
