title: As Tech Tensions with China Persist, the US Prohibits the Government From Using DeepSeek AI
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The US has mandated that DeepSeek, a Chinese company, remove all artificial intelligence (AI) technology from the majority of government systems. All civilian government entities are prohibited from using DeepSeek or any technology developed using its AI models by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). DeepSeek has been viewed as a disruptive factor in the continuing AI technology race because it is a potent AI model that is open source, which means it is free to access and less expensive to utilise. The White House has blasted Chinese AI companies this year, although the DHS notification did not specify the precise security issues with DeepSeek. We have reached out to DeepSeek, the Chinese embassy in Washington, DC, and the DHS for comment. Although the prohibition went into place at the end of July, the DHS made the directive public on Monday. The Department of the Treasury, the Department of State, and the Department of Justice are among the civilian agencies covered by the directive. Department of Defence agencies are not included, though. The prohibition comes after American companies and the Trump administration criticised Chinese AI. title: Dubai Home Healthcare Services Climb 22.7% in the First Half of 2026
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Home care services in Dubai expanded faster than any other element of the health industry in the first half of 2026, with the number of licensed facilities increasing by 22.7% to 249, up from 203 in the same period last year. The significant increase, disclosed in a recent Dubai Health Authority (DHA) study, indicates a shift in how the emirate delivers care, with more patients receiving treatment at home rather than in a hospital or clinic. The report revealed widespread growth in the sector. The number of licensed health institutions in Dubai increased by 7% to 5,931 in the first half of 2026, compared to 5,541 in the same time of 2025. Licensed health professionals numbered 70,566, up 6.5% from 66,277. Other categories have also grown. The number of pharmacies increased 6.8% to 1,794. Complementary and alternative medicine centers increased by 8.1%, from 99 to 107. Medical complexes and optical centers increased by 9.9 percent, to 1,903 from 1,731 in the first half of 2025. Dr. Alawi Alsheikh-Ali, Director General of the Dubai Health Authority, commented on the report, stating that the expansion reflects the improvement of the emirate’s healthcare system and its capacity to meet community demands.The continued growth of Dubai’s health sector reflects the evolution of the emirate’s healthcare system and its ability to meet the needs of the community. title: Adam Rumanek on Building a YouTube Content Engine Through Licensing, Localization, and Rights Strategy
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: To Adam Rumanek, Founder and CEO of Aux Mode, YouTube is not just a video library. For him, it is a portfolio of various assets that can be programmed, localized, licensed, protected, and monetized in different ways. An effective YouTube strategy is not about finding one video that goes viral. It’s about getting even more commercial value from the content you already have while making smarter decisions about what to acquire next. For media companies, producers, and rights holders, this means they need to bring content strategy and licensing strategy much closer together. Stop Thinking in Videos. Start Thinking in Assets. A complete video may appear to be a single piece of content to benefit from, but it can become several things. Long episode content can anchor a playlist. Chosen scenes can become short clips. Old content can be resurfaced once audience interest picks up again. The catalog could be based on genres, cast, themes, seasons, or recurring viewing habits. The same underlying asset can also be adapted for audiences in other languages. Simply, ask: How many useful opportunities are already inside the assets we have? This also makes planning easier. Content pillars, playlists, release schedules, thumbnails, titles, descriptions, and audience data are no longer separate optimization processes. The Catalog Can Tell You What to License Next Licensing is treated as a negotiation problem. What does the title cost? Which territories are available? How long are the rights? What does the agreement allow you? Those questions are also still important, but YouTube has another layer of evidence. Adam Rumanek has put weight on using analytics for evaluating potential acquisitions through signals, which can include watch time, revenue, average view duration, search traffic, returning viewers, etc. If numerous titles that feature a particular celebrity consistently are being watched more than other comparable titles, that pattern is worth investigating. If one genre is producing fewer views but way more revenue, raw view counts are probably hiding its commercial value. If particular territories are continuously generating unbalanced revenue, they are also deserving of closer attention. The point here is absolutely not to assume that yesterday’s winner will also become tomorrow’s winner. Previous performance can be distorted and changed by thumbnails, promotion, seasonality, competition, or temporary cultural moments, etc. Instead, the data you find should help more in identifying repeatable characteristics. A licensing team that is aware of what their audience is already watching holds a stronger starting point when they’re deciding what to acquire. One Library, More Markets: The Localization Layer Localization is a hidden vault, especially when the stuff has already been produced. In an English catalogue, dubbing videos into Spanish and Portuguese produces more audiences without having to make entirely new content. AI dubbing helps the economics because the marginal cost of making another language version can be significantly lower than traditional voice production. Adam Rumanek suggests using AI dubbing. Take existing libraries and expand their potential instead of just constantly creating new material. It’s also easier since YouTube now supports both automatic dubbing for creators and manually uploaded different-language audio. If one company has produced 500 relevant English videos, the opportunity is not to create another 500 videos. It is to see which of those 500 deserve localization. Which markets justify dedicated channels, and which titles should remain concentrated on a single channel with multiple audio tracks? This is an entire portfolio design. The Real Work Begins After the Upload The problem that results from increased distribution is increased opportunities for content to be stolen, contested, or mismanaged. Here comes the necessity for license management to work side by side with programming. YouTube has the Content ID feature, which can recognize any matching audio or visual material and enable the matched video to be monetized, monitored, or blocked based on the rights holder’s decision. These decisions can even change according to the region. For licensed content, this is really important. A rights agreement can not end with the question of where a video may get published. It also needs to consider who is controlling the Content ID asset, how claims are handled, which territories are covered, what happens when rights expire, and how revenue is reconciled. Adam Rumanek’s insights in this area highlight a mostly overlooked reality that rights management is a significant part of monetization. Video monetization from your own channel could be an option. Similarly, the same video being used somewhere else without permission could also be an option for rights management, as long as there is proper ownership and licensing of the property. Adam Rumanek’s View: Build More Value From What You Already Own Good YouTube strategy should focus on extracting value from every asset possible. This also means having a better release schedule, a long-form title made into several formats, complementary titles licensed after a clear audience pattern, an existing catalog dubbed into new languages, or tighter rights management once the content has left the channel. To Adam Rumanek, this approach is what separates maintaining a YouTube channel from building a YouTube content business. title: In November, US President Trump will Travel to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Next month, US President Donald Trump will go to Manila to attend the 2026 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Meetings. Claire Castro, a spokesperson for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., confirmed the scheduled visit on Wednesday but did not offer any other information. Prior to his journey to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, the White House had previously announced that Trump would be visiting the Philippines. The APEC Summit in China is set for November 18–19, while the ASEAN Summit is set for November 15–17. For the ASEAN conference, Marcos has designated November 16–18 as special non-working days in the National Capital Region. Marcos and Trump last had a face-to-face meeting at the White House in July of last year to talk about trade, defence cooperation, and bilateral relations. On July 23 of this year, they spoke over the phone about regional security issues, particularly the South China Sea, as well as economic developments. In November 2017, Trump made his first trip to the Philippines as president during his first term. There, he met former President Rodrigo Duterte in Manila and attended the ASEAN 50th anniversary banquet. Renato Reyes Jr., president of Bagong Alyansang Makabayan, a left-wing, multi-sectoral political alliance in the Philippines, wrote on Facebook on Wednesday that “Trump’s image and effigy will burn in the streets of Manila the moment he steps foot on Philippine soil. The chief imperialist and fascist will get the fiery welcome he deserves. No red carpet welcome, only red banners of protest for the warmonger who plunged the world deeper in crisis.”Trump would face protests for escalating the global crisis through his assault on Iran, just as he did during his previous trip to the Philippines, Reyes continued. title: Bank of America was Fined $1.2 Billion for Money Laundering Violations
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The US Treasury Department announced on Tuesday that Bank of America had been fined $1.2 billion (£910 million) for failing to identify possible money laundering and other illicit behaviour. According to the Treasury, the banking behemoth neglected to notify the government of over $5 billion in questionable behaviour, of which $1 billion presented concerns to national security and illegal finance. According to the Treasury, these mistakes included failing to identify transactions that might have involved trade-based money laundering “with a substantial nexus to the southwest border” or Chinese money laundering networks.Bank of America told the BBC, “Our team is far along with and committed to finishing the work required to address the issues raised by our regulators.” Less than a day before Bank of America was scheduled to release its quarterly profits on Wednesday morning, the news was made.The bank stated via email, “Our third-quarter results will include a non-tax deductible charge of $1.2 billion impacting net income by approximately 17 cents per share.”It said, “We have already committed a significant amount of staff and resources to our continuing remediation efforts, and those expenses are included in the current expense base. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, “When a bank of this size fails to meet its anti-money laundering and sanctions obligations, the consequences extend far beyond its own walls, exposing the entire US financial system to significant illicit finance risks.” The fine is the third-largest the department has ever imposed. title: Six Flags Closes Nine Coasters Following a “Gruesome” Rider Death Fall
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Following the death of a rider who allegedly fell off a ride at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, the theme park chain is temporarily closing nine more coasters at six of its locations. Local media accounts state that a passenger fell or was thrown from the 200-foot, 70-mph Goliath coaster, though the death’s specifics have not yet been formally confirmed. Witnesses told Atlanta NBC station 11Alive of a “gruesome scene” in which the rider repeatedly struck the coaster while falling. According to one ride, the falling man was even caught in a souvenir photo that was immediately taken and sold in the gift shop. The witness stated, “He was in our pictures.” “He hit the car three times after falling.” Police say several other riders were hurt as well. According to two riders, personnel checked their safety belts in accordance with practice before the ride began. In a statement, a Six Flags representative told the Associated Press, “We have temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks out of an abundance of caution.” “One of our top priorities continues to be the safety of our guests and team members.” Following the incident, riders are seen being escorted off Goliath in the video below. Nine other coasters, including Goliath at Magic Mountain in Valencia, California; Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure in New Jersey; and Orion and Diamondback at Kings Island in Ohio, have been temporarily closed. These rides resemble the Goliath in the Georgia park. The announcement comes after two riders had brain haemorrhages and numerous other riders reported severe problems, leading Six Flags Magic Mountain to permanently close its well-liked X2 ride last month. Due to the ride, three people have sued Six Flags and the coaster’s manufacturer. title: Banking Watchdogs Ratchet up AI Examination as Stability Concerns Increase, Sources Say
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Banking authorities are accelerating efforts to manage rising AI risks, according to six people familiar with the situation, with some citing the possibility of bank cyberattacks or rogue agents that could damage global financial stability. The regulatory review reflects a growing realisation that breakthroughs in frontier AI may require costly cyber recovery, greater reliance on external technology suppliers, and, in some jurisdictions, clearer regulatory guidance, according to sources. Three top US regulators, including the Federal Reserve, are questioning banks about their use of advanced artificial intelligence models, according to two sources, adding to previous scrutiny. Three of the participants questioned whether they use Chinese-developed technology, AI agents in cyber defence, and whether they can control more autonomous systems. Supervisors in Europe, including the Bank of England and the European Central Bank, are pressuring banks to improve recovery plans, concerned that rapid advances in artificial intelligence may cause serious harm and disruption in financial markets sooner than previously thought, according to three people familiar with their thinking. A senior executive at a major European bank expressed concern about the possibility for significant harm to banking and financial markets within the next six months. author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: When an emergency warning is issued, Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence releases safety guidelines advising citizens to stay calm, follow official orders, and take cover in a secure location. Residents have been instructed to move to the nearest secure area as soon as possible, ideally inside a building or a room away from windows, and to stay there until the threat subsides. During the warning, they shouldn’t leave their houses or buildings. Additionally, Civil Defence advised people to avoid standing on rooftops or balconies, as well as in open spaces, near windows, and near glass. Those who are outside should seek cover behind a sturdy barrier or enter the closest building. When an emergency warning is issued while driving, drivers should stop on the side of the road, away from high-rise structures and bridges. Hours after advising civilians to leave the attack area in the Houthi-held capital, the Saudi-led coalition said on Tuesday that it had hit two locations in different provinces and a Yemeni oil company facility in Sanaa. title: Russia, Iran, and AI Pose a Threat to the UK, According to the Head of MI5
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: According to the chief of the intelligence agency, MI5 is investing more resources than it did during the Cold War to combat state threats. According to Sir Ken McCallum, threats from foreign adversaries have increased fourfold over the past ten years, with Russia emerging as “aggressor number one” and increased aggression by Iran-affiliated groups against military installations and Jewish sites. The head of MI5 claimed that Russia was using hybrid warfare while AI was “supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders” during an annual lecture in London. Additionally, he added that MI5 has “caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al,” particularly by integrating the technology with drones, and warned of growing dangers from “extreme right-wing terrorism.” According to him, extremist organisations employing AI to create new and old bioweapons pose the greatest threat from their misuse. He did point out that efforts to combat state threats and terrorism were now “pretty much of equal scale,” which he called a “huge shift” in recent years. Sir Ken stated that while Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has made “minimal and horrifically costly” progress, it has refrained from engaging in “conventional conflict” with NATO and is instead attempting to unnerve European nations. The words “hybrid warfare” and “hybrid attacks” are ambiguous and typically refer to non-military tactics, such as cyberattacks, sabotage, or disinformation, that are intended to put pressure on and destabilise an enemy. title: The Former Top Commander in Kyiv Tells the BBC That Russia’s Offensive Capabilities are Broken
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In an interview with the BBC, Ukraine’s previous commander-in-chief said that by killing so many Russian soldiers, Ukraine had “broken Russia’s ability to advance” and stabilised the front line. In an exclusive interview, Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi made the remarks for the first time since being abruptly removed from his position in the summer. In response to his dismissal, he disagreed with some who said he was too “old school” to lead Ukraine’s new, technologically sophisticated troops. Additionally, he refuted claims made by soldiers who had fought under him in the past, who told the BBC that they were commanded to hold their positions despite being nearly surrounded by Russians, resulting in significant casualties. According to Syrskyi, Moscow’s total combat losses were six times greater than those of Ukraine. “If you count only dead, then it’s up to 11 times,” he said. The death toll is not publicly disclosed by either Russia or Ukraine. Although it cannot be confirmed, the Ukrainian military claims to have inflicted record losses on Russian soldiers in September of this year. Since beginning its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Russia is thought to have lost almost 500,000 men, according to UK intelligence chiefs. According to the US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies, Ukraine may have lost as many as 150,000 soldiers by June 2026. He claims that the current standoff at the front is caused by this disparity in the death toll, technological advancements, and a policy of striking weak locations in Russia’s lines while restricting their advances in other areas. author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As the war in Iran continues to affect energy prices around the world, US President Donald Trump is facing more and more criticism over his plans to buy diesel from Russia. Trump said on Friday that Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to send 300,000 tonnes of diesel right away “to the American and global marketplace.” This would be the first of several shipments. That’s true even though he signed a bill just a few weeks ago that lets the US put new sanctions and tariffs on countries that buy oil and gas from Russia. Some Republicans and Democrats in Congress have said this move is wrong because they think the deal breaks US law. Trump said that Russia would send an extra one million tonnes of diesel after the first 300,000 tonnes. In November, Russia would send another 500,000 tonnes. The next shipment would be three million tonnes, sent “within a short period”, depending on the state of its refineries, which Ukraine has attacked during the war between the two countries. My top priority is lower prices for all Americans, but especially for our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. title: Healey Must Pay £35 Billion. Think Tank: Budgetary Challenge to Fulfilll Spending Commitments
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: An respected think group has cautioned that Chancellor John Healey must find £35 billion to achieve defence commitments in his first Budget without reducing public spending. According to the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS), the government would require a “top-up” of billions of pounds if it hopes to increase health spending and defence spending to 3% of national revenue by 2030 without putting pressure on other departments. Healey will have to decide between cutting expenditure, raising taxes, or doing both, according to the IFS, since higher inflation brought on by the Iran conflict may reduce the amount of money the government intended to spend on public services. The Treasury declined to comment. As borrowing costs increase, the government is under increasing pressure to demonstrate to the financial markets that it has a firm grip on finances. Healey must present “credible” spending plans in the budget, which is scheduled for October 28, according to the IFS.The chancellor cannot choose a “steady-as-she-goes” budget, according to Helen Miller, director of IFS.Maintaining the inherited tax and expenditure plans would mean letting inflation throw departments’ spending projections off track. title: The Second Houthi Attack on Riyadh Airport in Two Days Resulted in One Fatality and Eleven Injuries
author: Entrepreneur Mirror

title: The BBC Discovers That Abramovich Faked Documents to Avoid Paying Taxes on his Wealth
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: According to BBC Panorama, the largest accounting firm in the world assisted in fabricating paperwork to conceal Roman Abramovich’s fortune and avoid paying taxes. Superyachts, residences, and private aircraft valued at $672 million (£508 million) disappeared from Abramovich’s business accounts due to accounting approved by Deloitte in Cyprus. Additionally, it seems that Deloitte offered advice on a plan to use document fraud to avoid paying a significant tax bill on the oligarch’s wealth. Financial services lawyer Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC stated that the scheme was “straightforward” tax evasion and “it couldn’t be more blatant” based on Panorama’s evidence. Roman Abramovich disputes that he concealed his wealth or avoided paying taxes, according to his attorneys. They claimed it was acceptable to depend on expert counsel and that Panorama offered no proof that he was aware of, approved, or directed the falsification of any document. “Acts in compliance with applicable laws” is how Deloitte Cyprus put it.The results are being made public after the Bureau of Investigative Journalism and BBC Panorama conducted a collaborative investigation. Roman Abramovich was the most well-known Russian tycoon in the UK for almost twenty years. He was welcomed to London, where he purchased Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and provided funding for the team’s most prosperous era. However, the UK government sanctioned him as an associate of President Vladimir Putin during Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, forcing him to sell the club. title: US Unveils Sanctions on ICC in Move that Court Condemns as Attack on the Rule of Law
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The Trump administration has announced sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), accelerating its efforts to “dismantle” what it considers a “rogue” institution. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the restrictions, which include a ban on US firms conducting dealings with the ICC, were meant to “defend US sovereignty” and accused the court of attempting to prosecute Americans. The ICC described the measures as an assault on the rule of law and the pillars of the international legal order. The announcement came just hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her work to promote peace and international justice. The US has already sanctioned 17 of the ICC’s judges and executives, but this step targets the court as an institution, threatening its ability to operate financially. However, the US has allowed a six-month grace period before some of the latest penalties take effect, letting member states keep paying for its operations, a move Washington says is meant to give countries time to find a “solution to address” US concerns. title: Top 10 Innovative Leaders Redefining Success
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Success in business rarely follows one fixed path. Some leaders build their reputation by questioning familiar ways of working. Others find new opportunities in difficult markets, introduce fresh ideas to established industries, or take a different approach to challenges that others have accepted as normal. The Top 10 Innovative Leaders featured in this article represent different industries, backgrounds, and experiences. What connects them is the way they approach their work. They look for better answers, stay open to change, and understand that progress often starts with asking a different question. For these Top 10 Innovative Leaders, success is about more than growth or financial results. It can be seen in the businesses they build, the people they influence, the ideas they bring forward, and the standards they set within their fields. Their journeys show why innovative leadership continues to matter in a business environment that is constantly changing. Top 10 Innovative Leaders—Revolutionary Minds Below are the Top 10 Innovative Leaders Redefining Success, each bringing a distinct perspective to their industry. From established sectors to newer fields, these leaders are finding their own ways to create value, solve problems, and build lasting businesses. The stories of these Top 10 Innovative Leaders also show that innovation does not have to mean something completely new. Sometimes, it is about improving an existing idea, approaching a familiar challenge differently, or having the confidence to take an untested path. Ken Thompson | Connecting Global Industry with Innovative Manufacturing Behind every successful industrial project is a network of people and businesses working to find the right components, technologies, and expertise. For Ken Thompson, the challenge of connecting manufacturers with the customers who need their solutions became the foundation for KT Technical Solutions (KTTS), a U.S.-based manufacturers’ sales representative firm serving industrial and technology markets worldwide. Thompson founded KTTS after recognizing the need for a more responsive, technically focused approach to manufacturers’ representation. His customer-first philosophy, summed up in the words “We do whatever it takes,” has shaped the company’s work, particularly when customers need help sourcing hard-to-find components or finding practical solutions to keep critical projects moving. Under his leadership, KTTS has expanded across a broad range of sectors, including electronics, automation, energy storage, robotics, industrial equipment, precision instruments, and advanced manufacturing. The company connects customers with technologies and services that include printed circuit boards, cable assemblies, lithium battery technologies, precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, castings, molding, and engineering support. This breadth allows KTTS to help businesses navigate complex sourcing, manufacturing, and supply chain challenges. Rather than focusing on a single product category, the firm brings together manufacturers and customers across different technical fields, helping them identify suitable solutions for their project needs. Integrity, technical expertise, and long-term partnerships remain central to the company’s approach. Today, KTTS is among the largest independent manufacturers’ sales representative firms in the United States, linking innovative technologies with opportunities across global markets. As KTTS continues to connect manufacturers with customers across industries and markets, its work remains rooted in a practical belief: the right technical solution can help keep business moving. Through its broad network, industry knowledge, and commitment to responsive service, the company aims to make complex sourcing challenges easier to navigate and help innovative manufacturers reach new opportunities worldwide. Finding a route to viewers, securing distribution, and earning revenue can be just as demanding as making the work itself. Bonnie Bruderer encountered that challenge through her own experience in television, and it became the starting point for BINGE Movies + TV, the streaming and distribution company she founded. Bruderer began producing her own television show in New York City in late 2014. The experience gave her a close look at the creative side of the industry, but it also brought a practical question into focus: how could creators get their work in front of an audience beyond the traditional television system? As streaming grew, she saw an opportunity to help independent producers navigate a changing distribution landscape. Today, BINGE Movies + TV works with filmmakers and content owners to distribute films, series, documentaries, and other programming. Its streaming app is one part of the business, while its wider distribution and licensing work helps place projects on other streaming outlets. The company continues to seek placements across platforms and expand the reach of the content it represents. For Bruderer, the work is not simply about getting a title onto a single service. Different projects have different audiences and commercial possibilities, so the route to market may vary. BINGE Movies + TV considers each project individually and looks at a range of options, including major streaming services, niche platforms, cable, and even DVD distribution where it makes sense. The aim is to find a practical path for the particular film or programme, rather than treating one outlet as the only meaningful destination. That approach responds to a common difficulty for independent creators: visibility does not automatically lead to a distribution deal or reliable income. A project may attract attention at festivals and still struggle to reach a wider audience. BINGE Movies + TV’s distribution services are intended to help creators move beyond that bottleneck by handling outreach and pitching to potential licensing partners. Its public materials also emphasize that creators retain ownership of their work, while the company helps them pursue distribution opportunities. The business has also developed a model that connects its own streaming service with the wider licensing market. Content partners can earn through different routes, including revenue from distribution on partner platforms. BINGE Movies + TV’s published agreement outlines quarterly reporting and payment of a share of net proceeds from platform revenue, while its distribution information describes a revenue-sharing option for branded channels. These arrangements place monetization alongside distribution as part of the service offered to content owners.

A New Route to the Screen: Bonnie Bruderer’s BINGE Movies + TV

A finished film is a major achievement, but for many independent creators, completing the project is only the beginning. Finding a route to viewers, securing distribution, and earning revenue can be just as demanding as making the work itself. Bonnie Bruderer encountered that challenge through her own experience in television, and it became the starting point for BINGE Movies + TV, the streaming and distribution company she founded.

Bruderer began producing her own television show in New York City in late 2014. The experience gave her a close look at the creative side of the industry, but it also brought a practical question into focus: how could creators get their work in front of an audience beyond the traditional television system? As streaming grew, she saw an opportunity to help independent producers navigate a changing distribution landscape.

Today, BINGE Movies + TV works with filmmakers and content owners to distribute films, series, documentaries, and other programming. Its streaming app is one part of the business, while its wider distribution and licensing work helps place projects on other streaming outlets. The company continues to seek placements across platforms and expand the reach of the content it represents.

For Bruderer, the work is not simply about getting a title onto a single service. Different projects have different audiences and commercial possibilities, so the route to market may vary. BINGE Movies + TV considers each project individually and looks at a range of options, including major streaming services, niche platforms, cable, and even DVD distribution where it makes sense. The aim is to find a practical path for the particular film or programme, rather than treating one outlet as the only meaningful destination.

That approach responds to a common difficulty for independent creators: visibility does not automatically lead to a distribution deal or reliable income. A project may attract attention at festivals and still struggle to reach a wider audience. BINGE Movies + TV’s distribution services are intended to help creators move beyond that bottleneck by handling outreach and pitching to potential licensing partners. Its public materials also emphasize that creators retain ownership of their work, while the company helps them pursue distribution opportunities.

The business has also developed a model that connects its own streaming service with the wider licensing market. Content partners can earn through different routes, including revenue from distribution on partner platforms. BINGE Movies + TV’s published agreement outlines quarterly reporting and payment of a share of net proceeds from platform revenue, while its distribution information describes a revenue-sharing option for branded channels. These arrangements place monetization alongside distribution as part of the service offered to content owners.

Bruderer’s role has involved building the relationships and operational capacity needed to make that model work. The company has to assess projects, understand where they might fit, coordinate submissions, and maintain connections with platforms and licensing partners. BINGE Movies + TV has a team with experience across different parts of the entertainment business, including cinema and content licensing. That mix of expertise helps the company evaluate opportunities beyond its own streaming app.

BINGE Movies + TV is also focused on growing its direct subscription audience. Bruderer has identified subscriber growth as a key priority and discussed testing different marketing approaches to reach viewers. The company’s subscription model is closely tied to its creator-focused positioning: as the subscriber base expands, a portion of subscription revenue is shared with creators.

After more than a decade in the streaming and distribution business, Bruderer’s work reflects a shift in how independent content can find its audience. BINGE Movies + TV is not only building a place for viewers to watch films and shows; it is also working across the distribution process that can help those projects travel further. For independent filmmakers, that means another potential route from a completed project to a wider market, with distribution and earning opportunities considered together.

Jean-Pierre Cubizolle from Impact2Scale Calls for Anticipatory, Convergent Governance to Advance the UN Sustainable Development Goals

With a career spanning international consulting, corporate leadership, and board-level responsibilities, Jean-Pierre Cubizolle is the Founder and President of CHC Corporate Horizon Consulting, which specializes in dental support services, occupational health, performance and risk management, and emotional intelligence. Since 2025, he has served as a Partner and Board Member of Impact2Scale. From 2020 to 2024, he was regularly invited to speak at Horasis conferences.

His professional experience includes leadership positions across consulting, human resources, and healthcare. From 1992 to 2010, he founded and chaired CCT Management Group SA, a European consulting firm focused on organizational efficiency, performance management, risk management, skills development, and executive compensation. The group operated through subsidiaries in Switzerland, France, Italy, Spain, Luxembourg, Dubai and Egypt. In 2010, it merged with hkp/// Group, where Jean-Pierre served as Senior Partner and Director until 2013.

Earlier in his career, he was Corporate Director of International Human Resources at Motorola Inc. in Chicago from 1979 to 1985, before helping to establish TPF&C Continental Europe. He later co-founded Edenweiss Group SA, serving as Director and CEO from 2013 to 2016.

In early 2026, Jean-Pierre Cubizolle co-authored The Legacy of All with Olivier Ferrari, Founder and CEO of Amberstone Finance SA. This book provides a broader reflection on sustainable development, collective responsibility, and the legacy passed on to future generations.

Jean-Pierre is now developing these reflections through a forthcoming White Paper proposing a model of “anticipatory and convergent governance” for the Sustainable Development Goals. Building on the experience of the first decade of the UN 2030 Agenda, the paper will explore how governance mechanisms could evolve to translate shared commitments into more coherent, measurable and sustainable outcomes.

He argues that, more than a decade after the UN 2030 Agenda established 17 Goals, 169 targets and more than 230 indicators, the central challenge is no longer simply to define additional goals, but to strengthen the governance mechanisms required to transform commitments into measurable results.

Jean-Pierre notes that the global context has shifted markedly since 2015. Armed conflicts, rising geopolitical tensions, persistent poverty, ecosystem degradation, pressure on planetary boundaries, and declining trust in multilateral institutions all point to the same conclusion: ambitious goals alone are not enough without governance that can translate them into effective action.

Two complementary principles should guide this evolution:

Convergent governance: creating the conditions for international organizations, States, businesses, civil society, academia, and citizens to retain their own responsibilities, competencies, and autonomy, while aligning their decisions and actions toward a shared vision and measurable collective outcomes.

Anticipatory governance: developing permanent vigilance capable of identifying situations that may generate future risks, assessing their probable trajectories, and acting early enough to keep those risks under control before they reach critical or irreversible levels.

Jean-Pierre further suggests that international institutions should evolve to better integrate strategic foresight, early warning, mediation, operational coordination, and accountability. This reflection also extends to the governance of the United Nations Security Council, including its composition, decision-making processes, and the implementation of its decisions, to strengthen its contribution to SDG 16 on Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions and, more broadly, to the objectives of the UN 2030 Agenda.

“The SDGs should be regarded not only as a set of objectives, but as the expression of a shared global responsibility. Their success will depend less on the adoption of new goals than on our capacity to anticipate emerging challenges, make autonomous actors converge around a shared vision, and transform that vision into coherent, measurable and collective outcomes.”

Jean-Pierre Cubizolle, President, Corporate Horizon Consulting

Jean-Pierre describes the end of this decade as an important window for reflection. The approaching succession of the UN Secretary-General, changes in political leadership across many Member States and the 2030 deadline are converging at a time when the international community is already considering what should follow the current UN Agenda. Together, these developments provide an opportunity for collective reflection on the future of the SDGs, their governance and the international institutions involved in their implementation.

Jean-Pierre also highlights the role of new tools in supporting this evolution. Artificial intelligence can help analyze complex data, detect emerging risks, and simulate scenarios to support SDG monitoring and decision-making.

He finally emphasizes the importance of giving micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) a more structured role in delivering the Goals. MSMEs account for around 90% of businesses worldwide, generate 60–70% of global employment and contribute approximately 50% of global GDP. MSMEs offer an exceptional capacity to translate the SDGs from international commitments into millions of concrete decisions and actions throughout the global economy.

Krzysztof Dziarmaga | Bringing Digital Intelligence to Maritime Operations

A ship’s condition is often assessed through inspections, reports, and the experience of the people responsible for keeping it running. But as maritime operations become more complex, technology creates new ways to monitor vessels and make decisions using timely information. For Krzysztof Dziarmaga, Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Smart Nautilus Ltd, the opportunity lies in connecting practical maritime knowledge with digital tools that can make operations more efficient, transparent, and sustainable.

Krzysztof is a maritime technology leader whose work spans digital transformation, subsea operations, remote inspection technologies, and the development of solutions for the maritime industry. Throughout his career, spanning roles from seafarer to Technical Superintendent, he maintained a strong interest in emerging technologies. After founding his own company, he focused on helping shipowners, operators, and other maritime stakeholders leverage data and technology to enhance vessel efficiency, ensure regulatory compliance, and optimize asset management.

As CTO and Co-founder of Smart Nautilus, Krzysztof leads the company’s technology strategy, product development, and innovation roadmap. Its solutions bring together technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), underwater robotics, environmental monitoring, AI-driven analytics, digital reporting, and real-time decision-support tools. The aim is to give vessel operators clearer, more continuous insight into their assets, supporting a shift from periodic inspections towards proactive, data-informed management.

A significant part of his work involves remotely operated vehicle (ROV) technologies and underwater inspection systems. These tools can support hull inspections, asset integrity assessments, and condition-based maintenance. Krzysztof’s areas of expertise include monitoring vessel hull conditions, inspecting propellers and rudders, assessing biofouling, managing marine growth, and using digital survey reports to help operators understand the condition of their vessels.

Biofouling has been a particular focus. Marine growth on a vessel’s hull can affect fuel consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, performance, and regulatory compliance. Krzysztof has helped develop technology-based approaches that support ongoing monitoring, earlier detection, and better-informed maintenance decisions. Through Smart Nautilus’ digital ecosystem, operators can gain a clearer picture of hull conditions, plan maintenance, and respond to evolving international requirements related to biofouling management.

His work also reflects the growing role of environmental responsibility in maritime operations. By connecting inspection data, monitoring systems, and digital reporting, technology can help operators understand the effects of their decisions and identify opportunities to improve how vessels are maintained and managed. For Krzysztof, these capabilities are part of a wider shift towards safer and more sustainable operations.

Beyond product and technology development, he has worked to build partnerships across Europe, Australia, New Zealand, the US, and other maritime regions. He supports collaboration among technology providers, vessel operators, regulators, research institutions, and service organizations, recognizing that practical solutions often require expertise from across the industry. These partnerships have been involved in areas such as environmental monitoring, maritime digitalization, smart inspections, asset integrity, and intelligent reporting.

Krzysztof’s approach brings operational experience and emerging digital capabilities together. His focus is on turning complex information into useful insights for people responsible for vessels and marine assets. As the maritime sector continues to adopt automation and real-time intelligence, he remains committed to developing tools that support greater operational transparency and help stakeholders make informed decisions.

Through his role at Smart Nautilus, Krzysztof continues to contribute to the development of intelligent shipping and marine asset management, with an emphasis on connecting technology to the everyday needs of maritime operations.

Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles | A Journey Built on Persistence, Purpose and Global Ambition

Success rarely arrives in a straight line. For some people, it is built through years of steady progress, while for others, the journey is marked by unexpected turns, challenges, and opportunities that gradually shape the person they become. For Sir, Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles, President and CEO of Peebco Energy Group, persistence has remained a central part of that journey.

His recent achievement adds another milestone to an already extensive list of professional and academic accomplishments. Prof. Dr. Peebles has taken part in his second major international business and intellectual competition, competing on a global stage alongside some of the strongest participants in the field. The achievement reflects his continued interest in business, leadership, and intellectual development.

His journey has included recognition from a number of organisations and institutions over the years. On June 13, 2021, Dr. Peebles was among the recipients of the Catholic Man of the Year recognition within the St. Louis Catholic Archdiocese. The recognition marked one of several milestones that would follow in the years ahead.

Education has also remained an important part of his development. On June 25, 2024, he graduated from Harvard University’s two-year H-BAP Leadership Program. Later that year, on September 4, he was accepted into Seton Hall Law School for International Business Compliance and Regulations.

His professional and institutional affiliations continued to grow. On November 10, 2024, Dr. Peebles was inducted into The Royal Society of St. George, followed by his appointment to the United Nations Association on November 26. On January 21, 2025, he was accepted into the American Bar Association.

The academic side of his journey reached another milestone on August 22, 2025, when Dr. Peebles earned his PhD in International Trade & Finance. He later earned a Professorship in International Literature on February 15, 2026, adding another dimension to his academic pursuits.

Alongside these achievements, his work has also received international recognition. On May 19, 2021, Prof. Dr. Joseph Peebles, PhD received an international nomination for an International Peace Ambassador.

The year 2026 brought several significant moments. On May 21, Prof. Dr. Peebles won first place in an international business competition, receiving recognition as the Global Business Innovation & Sustainability Leader of the Year. The achievement placed his work in business and sustainability on an international platform.

Just over a month later, on June 29, 2026, he received the Business Leadership & Excellence Award for Top International Chairman & Chief Executive Officer. On August 31, 2026, he was also awarded an international certificate recognising him among the Global Business Icons to Follow in 2026.

For Dr. Peebles, however, these milestones appear to represent more than a collection of titles and awards. His own reflections place greater emphasis on the resilience required to keep moving forward when the path becomes difficult.

“Over time, hard work does pay off,” Sir Joseph states. “Yes, there will be bumps in the road along the way. There will be failures to launch, and there will be detours within the journey.”

That understanding of perseverance forms an important part of his outlook. He points to versatility, adaptability, and the determination to remain engaged in the competition as qualities that help people navigate difficult periods.

His ambitions also extend beyond personal achievement. Through his work, he says his journey has always been connected to providing for both the planet and the greater good of its inhabitants. That broader purpose gives his business and leadership journey another layer, linking professional ambition with a desire to contribute to something beyond the individual.

The road ahead will undoubtedly bring its own challenges, but Dr. Peebles’ story so far is one of continued movement. From education and professional development to international recognition and business competition, each milestone has added another chapter to his career.

Perhaps the philosophy that best captures his outlook comes from the French saying he uses at the end of his reflection: “Après la pluie, le beau temps”, or, after the rain, the good weather comes. For Dr. Peebles, it is a reminder that difficult periods do not have to define the destination.

Geoffrey Spooner | Turning Field Experience into the Future of Building Intelligence

What if the people who spend years fixing buildings are the ones best placed to rethink how those buildings are understood?

For Geo Spooner, Founder and CEO of CoreTherm Aerial, the answer began long before the idea of a technology company. Nearly three decades spent working across construction, facilities, property operations, and the built environment gave him a close view of how buildings are actually built, operated, repaired, and maintained. His experience was shaped by construction sites, rooftops, mechanical rooms, and job trailers, not by Silicon Valley or a laboratory.

That background became the foundation for a different kind of entrepreneurial journey.

Geo is FAA Part 107 certified and a licensed thermographer, bringing together practical experience with technical knowledge of the built environment. Over the years, he began noticing that some of the biggest opportunities were often hidden inside problems that an industry had simply become accustomed to accepting.

That realization led to CoreTherm Aerial.

The company was founded around a straightforward but ambitious idea: physical assets should have an engineering memory. Buildings produce vast amounts of information throughout their lifetimes, but much of that information remains scattered across photographs, reports, spreadsheets, service records, and the knowledge of individual people.

Geo sees an opportunity to change that.

CoreTherm combines radiometric thermal data, engineering intelligence, and artificial intelligence to create a deeper understanding of how physical assets change over time. The goal is not simply to collect more information, but to make that information useful to owners and operators before small problems turn into expensive capital events.

For someone who spent much of his career seeing these challenges firsthand, the idea is deeply connected to his own experience. Technology, in this case, is not being developed simply because it is new. It is being developed because Geo has seen a real problem from the ground level and believes there is a better way to address it.

But CoreTherm is only one part of his story.

His path to entrepreneurship has included mistakes, risks, failures, and rebuilding. There have been chapters he is proud of and others that brought lessons that no classroom could have provided. Rather than separating those experiences from his leadership journey, Geo sees them as part of what shaped the way he operates today.

That perspective has given him a practical view of leadership. He believes conviction matters, but so does speed. Accountability matters, but so does the willingness to challenge familiar ways of doing things. For him, entrepreneurship is not about accepting that something has always been done a certain way. It is about having the courage to ask whether it still needs to be done that way.

This mindset is particularly important in an industry where many processes have developed over decades. Buildings are long-term assets, and decisions made today can affect their performance and costs for years. Bringing better information into those decisions could change how owners think about maintenance, repairs, and capital planning.

At 47, Geo does not see himself as someone reaching the end of an entrepreneurial journey. Quite the opposite.

“I’m 47 years old, and I genuinely believe I am just getting started.”

That statement captures much of what defines his approach. He is not interested in building another company simply for the sake of calling it successful. His ambition is larger: to build something that can change the way an entire industry thinks about its physical assets.

Perhaps the most revealing part of his story is that he does not consider knowing everything to be his greatest strength. His advantage, he believes, came from something much simpler: curiosity.

“My greatest advantage was never that I knew everything.

It was that I was never afraid to ask why everyone else accepted it.”

That question sits at the heart of Geo Spooner’s journey. From construction sites and rooftops to building CoreTherm Aerial, his career has been shaped by looking closely at problems that others may have learned to overlook. Now, he is bringing that same mindset to the intersection of thermal data, engineering, and AI, with the ambition of helping the built environment become more intelligent, more proactive, and better prepared for what comes next.

Yves Marc Ouffoue | Building Africa’s Next Private Aviation Network

In private aviation, the journey begins long before an aircraft takes off. Finding the right aircraft, matching it to a client’s needs, coordinating with operators, and navigating the realities of different African markets all require experience and strong relationships. Yves Marc Ouffoue, known as Marc, has built nearly 15 years of that experience across the African aviation industry, and today he is using it to build a stronger network for private jet brokerage on the continent.

An Ivorian aviation entrepreneur and private jet brokerage expert, Marc has developed his expertise entirely within the African market. His career has involved working closely with operators across passenger aviation, cargo logistics, and specialised aviation support missions, including military-related operations in selected African countries.

That experience has given Marc a close view of how the African aviation market works and where there is room to improve the way private aviation services are connected and delivered. At 37, he is now taking that experience into entrepreneurship with a focus on strengthening the role of African brokers.

One of his key ventures is The Black Jet Brokers (BJB), a pan-African network created exclusively for jet brokers based on the continent. The idea behind BJB is to bring together the knowledge, connections, and reach of African brokers and turn them into a stronger collective force.

Marc’s vision is centred on supporting the growing mobility needs of Africa’s elite and institutional stakeholders. By creating a more connected brokerage community, he aims to help brokers improve service standards, respond more efficiently, and handle high-level travel requirements with greater ease.

The initiative also reflects his belief that African brokers should have a stronger role in shaping the continent’s private aviation market. Rather than relying entirely on networks outside Africa, BJB is designed around the people and businesses already operating within the continent.

Marc is also leading Empty Legs Africa, an initiative focused on promoting and monetising empty-leg flights across, to, and from Africa. These flights create an opportunity to make use of aircraft that would otherwise travel without passengers, potentially opening new revenue opportunities for both brokers and operators.

For Marc, the initiative is about finding value in an existing part of private aviation while improving access to aviation solutions across the continent. It adds another dimension to his work, connecting commercial opportunity with a more efficient use of available aircraft capacity.

Both ventures come from the same underlying idea: Africa’s private aviation industry has significant potential, but that potential can be strengthened through better connections, stronger local networks, and a deeper understanding of the continent’s unique requirements.

As he continues developing The Black Jet Brokers and Empty Legs Africa, his focus remains firmly on Africa. His ambition is to empower the continent’s brokers, create new opportunities for operators, and contribute to a private aviation ecosystem that is better connected and better equipped to serve the people and institutions driving Africa’s growth.

For Yves Marc Ouffoue, the future of private aviation in Africa is not simply about more aircraft in the sky. It is about building the relationships and networks on the ground that make those journeys possible.

Hanan Al-Shayeb | Leading Fintech Growth Across Markets

The financial world has evolved during the past two decades. Payments have moved online, digital banking has increased, and new types of financial technology have opened up previously inaccessible markets. Hanan Al-Shayeb has spent more than 25 years navigating these shifts, founding companies and directing teams in fintech, payments, digital assets, e-commerce, and regulated financial services.

As a C-level executive, Hanan has worked across MENA, Europe, Africa, and other international markets. Her experience combines business growth with the practical side of running financial services businesses, including regulation, partnerships, market expansion, and day-to-day execution.

Today, she serves as the DFSA-authorised CEO/SEO of Altery, where she brings together commercial goals and strong governance. Her experience in regulated financial services has given her a clear understanding of the care and responsibility required when building businesses in complex markets.

Before Altery, Hanan held senior leadership roles at companies including Paytiko, Bybit, OPay, JollyPay, Souq.com, and Bayt.com. Across these roles, she has led international teams, entered new markets, developed partnerships, and helped businesses achieve double- and triple-digit growth.

Her work covers a wide part of the financial technology sector, from payments and digital banking to cross-border financial solutions, acquiring and issuing, and digital asset infrastructure.

What stands out in Hanan’s career is her focus on turning plans into results. Growth, in her view, is not simply about having a good idea. It also requires the right people, strong partnerships, careful planning, and the ability to execute.

That approach has helped her build payment ecosystems and lead businesses through periods of change. Working across different regions has also given her experience with markets that have their own customers, regulations, business cultures, and challenges.

Her career has earned recognition through several awards, including Women Rising in Fintech – UAE 2025, Excellence in Women’s Leadership – FinTech 2026, and Visionary Fintech & Payments CEO of the Year – 2026.

Beyond her executive roles, Hanan is involved with organisations supporting women and the wider fintech community. She is a member of the MENA Fintech Association, WOMENCHOICE.ORG, and the Dubai Business Women Council (DBWC). She also gives back through mentorship as a Mentor at Ignyte.

Hanan believes that generating possibilities for individuals and businesses is intimately related to leadership. Her expertise in a variety of sectors and geographical areas has given her insight into the potential for significant change when technology, sound strategy, and capable leadership are combined.

Today, she continues to focus on fintech and the future of financial services. She continues to work on building responsible, adaptable and sustainable businesses that can grow from MENA to international markets.

Her journey is a career built around change. In a world of constant change, Hanan Alshayeb is determined to help shape what’s next in financial services through growth, innovation and hands-on leadership.

title: Residents of a Kibbutz Devastated by Hamas-Led Attacks on October 7 Struggle to Rebuild
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In the empty dining room of Kibbutz Nir Oz, which was once the vibrant center of a close-knit, 400-person Israeli settlement devastated by the Hamas-led onslaught on October 7, 2023, roosting birds now coo among the ceiling tiles.We used to visit and dine together. Dalit Ram Aharon, who is taking me around with her husband, Achi, recalls, “There were lots of activities here, also holidays to celebrate.” A startling reminder of what happened to the missing residents may be found by the glass entrance doors, which are peppered with gunshot holes. Following the attacks three years ago, stickers were placed on each household’s postbox: red ones show those who were slain, and black ones show those who were taken hostage. “”Kidnapped or murdered, that’s one out of four of us,” adds Dalit. “including infants and young children.” Residents of the kibbutz, which is located just a mile (1.6 km) from the Gaza border and was among the worst-hit areas, are going through another difficult period of reflection as Israel commemorates the third anniversary of its bloodiest day ever. At the Siman Tov family’s nearby burned-out home, where a wind chime hangs at the entrance, time seems to stop still. Tamar and Yonatan are pictured with their three kids: their two-year-old son, Omer, and their five-year-old twin girls, Shahar and Arbel. The parents were shot through the door of their bomb shelter, which was not intended to withstand gunfire but rather rockets fired from Gaza. title: After a Boy’s Hand was Blown off During Student Protests, France Stopped Using Stun Grenades

Over 500 schools were either completely or partially closed on Wednesday as the disruption persisted. Following complaints from various groups about police employing excessive force against youths, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has supported the police reaction. He denied that security officers had “orders to confront” the youths in a speech to the country on Wednesday nite. He stated that by the end of October, the government would provide a package of ideas, including building renovations to increase the number of teachers available, after looking into the demands made by students. He did not provide any more information. The alleged “anger of young people does not come from nowhere,” he stated. According to Education Minister Édouard Geffray, 24 schools have been “set alight or vandalised” to the point that they will be closed for several weeks, impacting 30,000 students. title: On October 7, Manila Celebrates Palestinian Heritage Day with a Demonstration and art Exhibit
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In honour of Palestinian Heritage Day, an art exhibition debuted in the Philippines this week. The University of the Philippines (UP)-College of Fine Arts (CFA) Art Gallery features a variety of images, crafts, and devotional items that depict the Palestinian way of life. The month-long exhibition, “Palestine: Living Heritage, Enduring Steadfastness,” was opened by UP President Angelo Jimenez and Palestinian ambassador to the Philippines Mounir Anastas. It provides visitors with a direct connection to the country’s ongoing cultural traditions. Images of Gaza’s historical landmarks before and after they were destroyed by Israeli occupation forces are contrasted with pictures of ancient sites throughout the West Bank. The exhibit’s first docent, Ambassador Anastas, described traditional Palestinian arts, including devotional objects, painting, and needlework. He thanked the CFA, the institution, and its Office of International Linkages for their dedication to international solidarity, education, and cultural preservation. The exhibit, according to CFA, offers evidence of a culture’s lasting beauty and vitality in the face of the deliberate destruction of Palestinian identity, communal memory, history, and territory. The exhibition, according to the top fine arts institution in the Philippines, presents “Palestinian visual culture to testify to the catastrophic loss of a people’s physical and cultural memory alongside the genocide happening across the Gaza Strip today.” The display spreads the message of solidarity and the need for social justice by highlighting both concrete and intangible cultural assets throughout this crisis, according to the institution. title: How China’s Imports Caused a Hazardous Addiction in India
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Enter an Indian toy store and, in addition to finding a child’s new favourite toy, you can learn more about the country’s struggle for improved commercial ties with its big neighbour, China. India increased tariffs on imported toys from 20% to 60% and finally to 70% six years ago in an effort to discourage local production and prevent inferior toys from entering its market. Retailers were furious, claiming that domestic companies could never compete with products manufactured abroad. However, the combination of stricter quality control requirements and increased customs fees was effective. Indian toy exports increased from approximately $129 million to $200 million during the same period, while imports decreased by a third from nearly $300 million (£227 million) in 2020 to $100 million this year. Additionally, the nation was able to significantly lessen its reliance on China, which controlled 70% of the regional toy market. In India’s usually fruitless attempts to correct an increasingly uneven trading relationship with its larger neighbor—which some experts claim is currently among the most asymmetric in the world—the industry stands out as a rare exception. Its trade deficit with Beijing has only increased, from $44 billion in 2020 to an astounding $112 billion this year, despite the fact that diplomatic relations between the two nations completely collapsed after the Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and Delhi announced a number of anti-dumping duties and a ban on Chinese apps like Tik Tok.Kevin Zongzhe Li, a Washington-based Fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute’s Center for China Analysis, told the BBC that while political, security, and investment ties were at their lowest point, India’s economic reliance on China continued to grow. title: Ahead Of the Midterm Elections, the US Labour Market is Sharply Slowing Down
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Employers added just 29,000 jobs in September, marking a significant downturn in the US labour market prior to the midterm elections. According to data from the Bureau of Labour Statistics (BLS), headcounts in key industries, including tech and retail, barely changed despite a sharp decline in hiring since August. Meanwhile, the unemployment rate rose slightly from 4.1% in August to 4.2% in September. According to experts, the numbers indicate a slowing US economy, which reduces the likelihood that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in the future. According to updated BLS data for the month, 29,000 jobs were created in September compared to 133,000 in August. title: Japan Increases Permanent Residency Fees by 20 Times
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Japan has increased payments for foreigners seeking permanent residency by 20 times, to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955). Applicants for permanent residency must also meet stringent income, pension, and Japanese language requirements. Long lineups formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants rushed to avoid the cost increases, with Tokyo’s main immigration agency reporting wait times of more than seven hours. When a business is owed money, it may hear several legal terms used during the recovery process, including debt collection, litigation, and enforcement.

These terms are connected, but they do not mean the same thing.

Understanding the difference can help businesses identify what stage they are dealing with and avoid taking the wrong approach when trying to recover an outstanding amount.

In simple terms, debt collection focuses on recovering an outstanding debt, litigation concerns resolving a legal dispute through the courts, and enforcement concerns executing an enforceable judgment or instrument.

The appropriate step depends on the circumstances of the individual matter.

What Is Debt Collection?

Debt collection generally refers to efforts to recover money that remains unpaid.

For a business, this may involve an overdue invoice, an unpaid commercial account, or another outstanding financial obligation.

The first stage may involve reviewing the agreement and supporting documents, contacting the debtor, requesting payment, and attempting to resolve the matter without immediately escalating it into a formal legal dispute.

The exact approach depends on the contractual relationship, the amount involved, the available documentation, and the reason for non-payment.

Debt collection is therefore not necessarily the same as going to court.

A business may be able to resolve an unpaid account through communication or an agreed payment arrangement without commencing litigation.

When Does Debt Collection Become More Complicated?

An unpaid amount becomes more complicated when the debtor disputes the obligation or refuses to resolve the matter despite repeated requests.

For example, a customer may claim that:

  • The invoice is incorrect
  • The goods or services were not delivered as agreed
  • The work was incomplete
  • The agreed price was different
  • The payment has already been made
  • The contract does not require the amount being claimed

In these circumstances, the business should examine the underlying agreement and evidence rather than treating the matter as a simple overdue payment.

The distinction between an undisputed debt and a genuine commercial dispute can influence what happens next.

What Is Litigation?

Litigation is the process of resolving a legal dispute through court proceedings.

A business may consider litigation when there is a dispute that cannot be resolved through other appropriate means and a formal legal determination is required.

Commercial litigation can involve disagreements concerning contracts, payments, obligations, or other business relationships.

The preparation for litigation can require careful review of:

  • Contracts
  • Invoices
  • Correspondence
  • Transaction records
  • Delivery or performance documents
  • Payment records
  • Other evidence relevant to the dispute

The precise requirements depend on the nature of the case.

Litigation should therefore not be viewed simply as another name for debt collection. A debt may be undisputed, while litigation generally becomes relevant when a legal dispute requires formal resolution.

Businesses dealing with a developing commercial dispute can consider the available litigation services in Saudi Arabia based on the circumstances of the matter.

What Is Enforcement?

Enforcement is different again.

If a party has obtained an enforceable judgment or another enforceable instrument, the issue may move from establishing or resolving the claim to taking steps to execute the enforceable obligation.

This distinction is particularly important for businesses that have already succeeded in obtaining a judgment.

Winning a dispute and actually obtaining payment are not necessarily the same stage.

The enforcement process is concerned with giving effect to an enforceable obligation in accordance with the applicable legal procedures.

Businesses seeking to understand this stage can review enforcement services in Saudi Arabia for more information about the relevant legal service.

Debt Collection vs. Litigation vs. Enforcement

The easiest way to understand the difference is to consider the main question at each stage.

Stage Main Question
Debt collection How can the outstanding amount be recovered?
Litigation Does a legal dispute need to be formally resolved?
Enforcement How can an enforceable judgment or instrument be executed?

These stages may sometimes connect, but they should not automatically be treated as one process.

For example, a business may have an unpaid invoice but no dispute. The initial issue may therefore concern debt recovery.

If the debtor challenges the underlying obligation and the matter cannot be resolved, litigation may become relevant.

If the business subsequently obtains an enforceable judgment, the focus may then move to enforcement.

Does Every Unpaid Debt Require Litigation?

No.

An overdue payment does not automatically mean that court proceedings are necessary.

Before considering litigation, a business should understand why payment has not been made and whether the issue can be resolved through appropriate communication or other available recovery steps.

The decision should take into account the amount involved, the contractual position, the available evidence, and the debtor’s response.

Unnecessary escalation can create additional cost, time, and commercial disruption.

At the same time, delaying action indefinitely can also create problems, particularly where the business has repeatedly attempted to recover an amount without success.

Does Winning a Case Automatically Mean the Money Has Been Recovered?

Not necessarily.

A judgment establishes an enforceable legal outcome, but the business may still need to take the appropriate enforcement steps to pursue the amount awarded.

This is why businesses should understand the difference between resolving a dispute and enforcing the resulting obligation.

The legal strategy should consider the entire situation rather than focusing only on the initial dispute.

What Should a Business Review Before Choosing the Next Step?

Before deciding whether to pursue collection, litigation, or enforcement, a business should organize the facts and documents surrounding the matter.

Important considerations may include:

1. Is the amount actually due?

Review the contract, invoice, payment terms, and relevant transaction records.

2. Does the debtor dispute the amount?

Identify whether there is a genuine disagreement concerning the contract, goods, services, or payment.

3. What evidence is available?

Organize contracts, invoices, correspondence, delivery records, payment records, and other relevant documents.

4. Has a judgment already been obtained?

If an enforceable judgment or instrument already exists, the issue may be different from an initial unpaid invoice.

5. What outcome does the business need?

The appropriate legal step should reflect the actual problem the business is trying to resolve.

Why Understanding the Difference Matters

Confusing debt collection, litigation, and enforcement can lead to unrealistic expectations.

For example, a business with an overdue invoice may assume that immediately starting court proceedings is always the best option. In another situation, a business may have already obtained a judgment but focus on the original dispute instead of understanding the enforcement stage.

A clearer understanding of the stages allows businesses to assess their position more logically.

It also helps them communicate more effectively with legal advisers and prepare the documents needed for the relevant process.

A Practical Example

Consider a company that supplied goods to another business under a written commercial agreement.

The customer receives the goods but does not pay the final invoice.

The supplier first reviews the agreement and invoice and contacts the customer regarding the outstanding amount.

If the customer accepts that the amount is owed and agrees to pay, the matter may remain at the debt-collection stage.

If the customer instead claims that the goods did not meet the contractual requirements and refuses payment, the matter may become a commercial dispute requiring further assessment.

If the dispute proceeds to court and the supplier obtains an enforceable judgment, the focus may then shift to enforcement.

The example demonstrates why the three terms should not be treated as interchangeable.

How Can Businesses Prepare for Debt Disputes?

Good preparation starts before a payment problem occurs.

Businesses should maintain clear commercial agreements, accurate invoices, transaction records, and written communications.

When a payment becomes overdue, records should be organized promptly rather than only after the matter has escalated.

A clear documentary record can help a business understand its position and determine what further action may be appropriate.

Final Thoughts

Debt collection, litigation, and enforcement are connected but distinct parts of dealing with unpaid commercial obligations and legal disputes.

Debt collection focuses on recovering an outstanding amount. Litigation concerns the formal resolution of a legal dispute. Enforcement concerns the execution of an enforceable judgment or instrument.

The correct approach depends on the facts, documentation, contractual relationship, and current legal position.

Businesses should therefore assess where the matter actually stands before deciding what action to take.
