2. Antonis Aristodemou | Making Cross-Border Business Simpler

“Good international tax planning isn’t just about compliance; it’s about helping businesses operate with clarity and confidence across borders.” That approach has shaped Antonis Aristodemou’s work throughout his career.

An FCCA-qualified international tax and financial reporting specialist, Antonis has spent more than a decade helping businesses, investors, and family offices navigate the practical challenges of operating across multiple jurisdictions. His experience covers international tax planning, financial reporting, corporate structuring, compliance, and business relocation, with a particular focus on Europe and the Middle East.

In June 2026, he established Willowserve Solutions Ltd as his full-time focus, creating a Cyprus-based advisory practice that supports clients expanding internationally or managing operations across borders. Through the firm, he works with entrepreneurs and organisations looking for practical guidance on tax, compliance, and corporate structures that align with their business goals.

Antonis has worked with clients across Greece, Cyprus, the Baltics including Lithuania and Estonia, and the United Arab Emirates. His work includes supporting businesses as they establish operations in new markets, manage international mobility, and navigate the tax and regulatory requirements that come with cross-border growth.

His expertise also extends to Golden Visa-related relocation and structuring matters in Greece and Cyprus, Cyprus IP Box regimes, non-domicile tax planning, transfer pricing, double taxation treaties, IFRS reporting, and the setup of legal entities and payroll structures for multinational teams.

What distinguishes Antonis’ approach is his focus on translating complex tax and regulatory requirements into practical solutions that clients can implement with confidence. Rather than offering one-size-fits-all advice, he works to develop frameworks that support businesses as they grow across different markets while remaining compliant with local requirements.

Fluent in both Greek and English, Antonis also contributes to the international tax community through industry events and thought leadership, sharing insights drawn from his experience working across multiple jurisdictions.

Today, through Willowserve Solutions, he continues to support businesses and investors navigating an increasingly international business environment, helping them build structures that are both practical and sustainable while simplifying the complexities of operating across borders.

3. Shairose Gulamani | Helping Leaders Turn Pressure into Their Greatest Strength

“Pressure doesn’t break leaders. It reveals them.”

Pressure is often treated as something to avoid, overcome, or simply endure. For Shairose Gulamani, it is something to understand and channel. Through a career spanning executive coaching, education, entrepreneurship, governance, and community leadership, she has developed a clear conviction: the true measure of a leader is not simply how much pressure they can withstand, but how intentionally and effectively they respond when it arrives.

That conviction led her to found PressurePoint: Channeling Pressure into Power Inc., where she works with executives, senior leaders, and organisations to strengthen their capacity to lead when the stakes are high. Instead of viewing resilience as simply pushing through adversity, Shairose helps leaders develop the self-awareness, emotional regulation, strategic clarity, and decision-making skills needed to perform under pressure without sacrificing their well-being.

Her perspective is grounded in both professional expertise and lived experience. Her career has taken her across education, entrepreneurship, governance, and community service, giving her first-hand insight into the complex realities leaders face. Before founding PressurePoint, she co-founded and helped build Vovito Cafés and Vovito Wholesale. These ventures deepened her understanding of business growth, operational responsibility, uncertainty, and the weight of making decisions that affect employees, customers, and communities.

Shairose’s understanding of resilience began much earlier. Born in Uganda, she came to Canada with her family after they were forced to leave their home country and rebuild their lives. That experience shaped her belief that even profound uncertainty can cultivate adaptability, courage, and the confidence to begin again.

Today, she brings these perspectives together in her work with organisations and leadership teams. Drawing on neuroscience, leadership psychology, and practical executive experience, she helps leaders navigate change, make sound decisions, and create sustainable high performance. At the heart of her approach is a powerful principle: before leaders can respond effectively to what is happening around them, they must understand what is happening within them.

Shairose’s impact extends beyond her coaching practice. She serves as Vice President of the Bellevue College Foundation Board and Chair of its Governance Committee. She has also contributed to international initiatives, including the Global Encounters Festival Dubai 2025, bringing her leadership experience to work that connects and serves communities across borders.

Her growing influence has earned external recognition. In May 2026, Shairose received the Rising Authority Award from The Authority Awards, recognising emerging leaders who are creating meaningful impact in their fields. She was subsequently nominated for a 2026 Women of Inspiration® Award, presented by the Universal Womens Network™, in recognition of her leadership and impact. She has also received the President’s Volunteer Service Award at the Gold level for her commitment to volunteer service.

An ICF Associate Certified Coach, Shairose is also a contributing author to Infinite Impact and Voices Across Borders: Becoming Here. Across her coaching, entrepreneurship, governance, writing, and community work, one purpose remains constant: helping people lead with greater clarity, intention, and humanity.

For Shairose, leadership is not about eliminating pressure or waiting for uncertainty to pass. It is about developing the inner capacity to meet difficult moments with clarity, courage, and purpose. Through PressurePoint, she helps leaders move beyond merely enduring pressure and learn to transform it into focused, meaningful action.

Pressure does not have to diminish a leader. When it is understood and channelled effectively, it can reveal the very qualities that make their leadership matter.

4. Suvrajit Ghosh | Three Decades of Building Businesses Across Borders

More than three decades in business have taken Suvrajit Ghosh across India, Uganda, Kenya, Dubai, and the Middle East. Different countries, different markets, and different challenges have shaped his career, but one thing has remained constant: his belief that lasting growth comes from strong execution, capable teams, and a willingness to adapt.

Today, Suvrajit serves as CEO and Group Head at Mount Meru Middle East. Before taking on his current role, he was CEO and Group Head at White Horse Commodities, adding to a leadership journey that has spanned sales, marketing, manufacturing, commercial operations, and business transformation across multiple international markets.

One of the most significant chapters of his career was with Bidco Uganda Limited, where he spent more than fifteen years progressing through several leadership positions before becoming General Manager and Unit Operations Head. During this time, the business strengthened its position across categories including oils, fats, soaps, and detergents, expanded its distribution network into West African markets, increased production capacity, and developed local employees into leadership roles.

His experience later took him to Capwell Industries in Kenya, where he led the Commercial and Research & Development functions, overseeing marketing, sales, product development, brand management, profitability, and team leadership. Each role added a different perspective, helping him understand not only how businesses grow but also how they respond to changing markets and customer needs.

Suvrajit’s professional journey began in sales with Marico Industries Limited and Cargill India Ltd. Those early years taught him the importance of understanding customers, building relationships, and staying connected to the market, lessons that have continued to influence his leadership style throughout his career.

Alongside his professional responsibilities, Suvrajit has continued to build his knowledge through management development programmes in sales, marketing, negotiation, consumer behaviour, brand management, media planning, and ERP in sales management. He holds both a Bachelor’s and a Master’s degree from Jabalpur University.

Looking back, Suvrajit’s career has never been defined by a single role or organisation. Instead, it reflects years of working across industries and countries, leading businesses through growth, change, and expansion. His approach has remained consistent throughout: build strong teams, understand the market, make thoughtful decisions, and create businesses that are prepared for the future.

LinkedIn |

5. Augusta Mirchandani | Building Trust in the World of Executive Recruitment

“The best career decisions don’t begin with a job description. They begin with understanding people.”

That belief has shaped the way Augusta Mirchandani has built her career and her business. As the Founder and CEO of AAA Global, she leads a recruitment firm specialising in quantitative finance and discretionary trading, helping hedge funds and financial institutions connect with professionals in one of the most competitive hiring markets.

For Augusta, recruitment has never been simply about filling vacancies. Long before launching AAA Global, she spent much of her early life adapting to new places and unfamiliar environments. Those experiences taught her the value of understanding people, recognising where they thrive, and appreciating that the right opportunity is about more than matching a résumé to a role.

That perspective became the foundation of AAA Global. Rather than measuring success by how quickly a position is filled, Augusta believes the best outcomes come from taking the time to understand both clients and candidates. In markets where many of the strongest professionals are not actively looking for a new role, she believes trust, relationships, and patience make all the difference.

The same philosophy shapes the way her team works. Each consultant at AAA Global focuses on a single market, allowing them to develop specialist knowledge and build lasting relationships within their area of expertise. Augusta has also fostered a culture that values collaboration, continuous learning, and maintaining high standards, creating an environment where the team grows together while delivering consistent results.

Over the years, this approach has helped AAA Global become a trusted recruitment partner for leading hedge funds and financial institutions around the world. Rather than relying on volume, the firm’s reputation has been built through consistency, reliability, and long-term relationships.

For Augusta, building a successful company has always gone hand in hand with building a workplace where people feel they belong. That belief continues to influence the way she leads, supports her team, and works with clients across the industry.

Today, Augusta continues to guide AAA Global with the same principle that inspired the business from the beginning: when people are understood, stronger teams, stronger businesses, and lasting professional relationships naturally follow.

LinkedIn | AAA Global

6. Otmane Yassine | Connecting Local Strengths with Global Opportunities

“Every country has something unique to offer. AKAL exists to connect those strengths to the world.”

That belief has shaped Otmane Yassine’s work from the beginning. Based in Geneva, he has focused on building partnerships that bring together local communities, institutions, businesses, and international organisations while encouraging cooperation that respects each country’s identity.

Otmane is the Founder of AKAL Brand®, Founder of AKAL INVEST, President of AKAL Développements, and President of IPPO Genève (International Patriotic Pact Organization). Across these initiatives, his work centres on economic cooperation, territorial development, investment, and sustainable partnerships.

The idea behind AKAL grew from a simple observation. Countries have their own resources, traditions, industries, and expertise, yet many struggle to gain international visibility while preserving what makes them unique. Rather than creating a single standard for every market, AKAL was designed as a platform where participating countries can present their own strengths while remaining connected through a shared international network coordinated from Geneva.

This approach has led to territorial initiatives such as SEN-AKAL in Senegal and AKAL-IVOIRE in Côte d’Ivoire. While each reflects the identity of its own country, they are part of a broader framework that encourages cooperation, knowledge sharing, and economic exchange.

Through AKAL INVEST, Otmane also supports investment initiatives that encourage the development of local industries, strengthen partnerships, and create opportunities for long-term economic growth. Alongside this work, he has placed importance on education by encouraging collaboration between universities, researchers, and international development projects. His aim is to create opportunities where academic knowledge can contribute to practical solutions.

Geneva remains at the centre of this vision, serving as the meeting point where governments, entrepreneurs, institutions, NGOs, investors, and international partners can come together to explore new opportunities for collaboration.

Much of Otmane’s work brings together economic development, international cooperation, territorial branding, and sustainable development. It is guided by the belief that countries do not need to lose their identity to participate in global opportunities. Instead, they can strengthen what already makes them unique while working alongside others.

His philosophy, “From Local to Global – Ubuntu,” reflects that perspective. For Otmane Yassine, cooperation is built not by making countries the same, but by creating opportunities that allow each one to grow while preserving its own identity.

LinkedIn | AKAL Brand

7. Kristin Bone | Choosing the Work That Matters Most

“Some people spend their careers following a single path. Kristin Bone built hers by saying yes to the work that mattered, even when it didn’t fit neatly into a title.”

That decision has taken her into places most people never experience. One day she’s leading a nursing team inside a psychiatric unit. Another day she’s on a film set helping bring an independent production to life. While the settings couldn’t be more different, Kristin sees a common thread running through all of them: people, pressure, and the responsibility that comes with both.

For more than a decade, Kristin has worked as a registered nurse and nursing supervisor in psychiatric units, correctional facilities, emergency departments, rehabilitation centres, and long-term care settings. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she stepped into travel nursing, moving between hospitals across the United States to support facilities facing severe staffing shortages. It was demanding work, but it also shaped the way she thinks about leadership, resilience, and showing up when people need you most.

Her academic background reflects that balance between healthcare and leadership. Kristin earned a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Washburn University before completing an MBA at the University of Saint Mary, bringing together clinical knowledge with a broader understanding of organisations and the systems that support them.

Outside healthcare, Kristin found another way to tell stories. As an actress and independent film producer, she works with Cinemaddict Films and Gaimchang3r Entertainment. Among the projects closest to her is Pony, a film exploring mental health, the fentanyl crisis, family, and female motorsports. The film is complete and is currently being submitted to film festivals around the world. A world premiere is in the works, but a date has not yet been set. Follow the Pony Movie Instagram page for updates and to learn how to support the film.

That same willingness to step into unfamiliar spaces has also shaped her work beyond nursing and film. Kristin serves on the Advisory Council for the Customer Experience Certificate Program at Seton Hall University’s Stillman School of Business and is a Global Advisory Board Member of the Fortuna Business Council.

Recognition has followed along the way. In 2025, she was named Transformational Leader of the Year by White Page International and honoured at the House of Lords in London. She has also been recognised among the Global 200 Women Power Leaders, the Brainz 500 Global list, received a CREA Global Award, and contributed as an Executive Contributor to Brainz Magazine.

Looking back, Kristin doesn’t describe her career as carefully planned. Instead, it has been shaped by opportunities to make a difference, whether that meant caring for patients, producing stories that reflect real life, or contributing to conversations about leadership and mental health. Across every role, one thing has remained constant: a willingness to step forward when the work matters most.

LinkedIn | Website | Instagram

8. Nayan Patel | Leading with Values, Purpose, and People

“A vision may start with one person, but it truly comes to life through teamwork.”

That belief has guided Nayan Patel throughout nearly three decades in the automotive manufacturing industry. Over 28 years, he has worked in Tier 1 manufacturing environments, partnering with leadership teams to strengthen operations while keeping people, culture, and accountability at the centre of every decision.

Nayan’s career has been shaped by operational leadership and organisational development. Working in director-level leadership roles within Piston Group, he has contributed to building operational discipline, supporting workforce engagement, and helping organisations align their long-term objectives with day-to-day execution. His experience also includes collaborating across supplier operations, strengthening executive communication, and encouraging cross-functional teamwork in complex manufacturing environments.

Alongside his operational expertise, Nayan has played a role in developing organisational culture and core values that support business growth. Rather than viewing culture as a separate initiative, he believes it should be reflected in the way leaders communicate, make decisions, and work with their teams.

Today, as a Certified FocalPoint Business & Executive Advisor, Nayan works with business leaders on operational leadership, organisational effectiveness, strategic growth, and leadership alignment. His approach combines years of manufacturing experience with practical business advisory, helping organisations strengthen performance while creating workplaces where people can contribute with confidence.

His professional background is supported by qualifications that include Six Sigma Black Belt, OSHA General Industry Trainer, and a degree from Lawrence Technological University. Together, they reflect his commitment to continuous learning and operational excellence.

Beyond his professional experience, Nayan is guided by a set of personal values that influence the way he leads and advises others. He believes in the importance of self-belief, lifelong learning, empowerment, integrity, diversity, and teamwork. For him, leadership is not about individual recognition but about creating an environment where others can grow, make informed decisions, and work towards shared goals.

Reflecting on his own journey, Nayan believes he found his purpose by leading with sincerity and authenticity. Inspired by the resilience and determination associated with Motown, he continues to encourage leaders to build organisations where strong values and ethical leadership remain at the heart of every decision.

Today, Nayan continues to support organizations facing complex operational challenges, helping leadership teams strengthen alignment, improve organizational effectiveness, and build cultures that support long-term success.

LinkedIn | Website

9. Simmone L. Bowe | Helping Leaders Build Stronger People and Stronger Organizations

“Real transformation begins with people.” That belief has shaped Simmone L. Bowe’s work as she helps organisations strengthen leadership, improve performance, and build healthier workplace cultures.

Over the years, Simmone has worked with small, medium, and large organisations, supporting leaders as they navigate change, develop their teams, and create environments where people can perform at their best. Her experience spans leadership development, cultural transformation, talent strategy, and executive coaching, bringing together practical business solutions with a people-first approach.

As the founder and lead consultant of Limitless Life, Simmone partners with organisations looking to strengthen leadership capability and organisational effectiveness. Her work includes facilitating executive retreats, helping leadership teams define their vision and strategy, designing leadership development programmes, and coaching executives as they grow into more effective leaders.

Culture has become another important focus of her work. Rather than addressing workplace challenges at the surface level, Simmone works with organisations to understand the factors influencing engagement, retention, morale, and performance. From there, she supports leaders in developing practical strategies that improve processes, strengthen collaboration, and create cultures aligned with an organisation’s long-term direction.

Alongside her consulting work, Simmone is also an accomplished speaker, certified corporate trainer, HR strategist, and personal development coach. Her career has included work as a consultant, leadership advisor, men’s empowerment advocate, educator, mentor, newspaper columnist, author, singer, and radio and television host. Each experience has contributed to her perspective on leadership and the role it plays in helping people realise their potential. Currently she is working as a Human Resources Director at Royal Caribbean Group Bahamas.

Her contributions have also been recognised beyond the workplace. Simmone was named one of the Caribbean Women to Watch in 2018 and was honoured as Mentor of the Year by Project Bahamas in 2022. She is also the author of seven books.

Academically, Simmone holds a BA in English, an MSc in Career and Human Resource Development, along with numerous professional certifications. Having worked across both the public and private sectors, she continues to bring together leadership, strategy, and personal development in ways that help organisations grow while empowering the people within them.

Today, through Limitless Life, Simmone continues to work with leaders who want to build organisations where performance and people develop together, believing that lasting success begins with investing in those who make it possible.

LinkedIn | Instagram | Facebook | Tiktok

10. Sridhar Kuppa | Helping Businesses Make Better Financial Decisions

“Finance should do more than explain what happened. It should help leaders make better decisions about what happens next.”

For Sridhar Kuppa, finance has never been just about reporting numbers or closing the books. Throughout a career spanning more than 25 years, he has worked with founders, executives, and growing businesses, helping them use financial information as a tool for better decision-making. Whether in public accounting, corporate finance, consulting, or strategic advisory, his focus has remained the same: turning financial complexity into practical insight that supports sustainable growth.

Sridhar’s professional journey began with Ernst & Young (EY) India, where he spent more than seven years in the Assurance practice. The experience gave him a strong grounding in financial reporting, governance, and audit while exposing him to the demands of large-scale business operations. During his time at EY, he received the EY Sparkle Award in recognition of his integrity and ethical leadership and contributed to a major IPO engagement.

As his career progressed, Sridhar took on finance leadership roles with organisations including Aurobindo Pharma, Amneal Pharmaceuticals, and Solomon Edwards. Across these roles, he worked on financial reporting, transaction advisory, ERP implementations, financial planning, cash flow management, and finance transformation. The variety of these experiences gave him a practical understanding of the financial decisions businesses face as they grow, evolve, and adapt to changing markets.

Today, Sridhar is the Co-Founder of Huntward Advisors, where he partners with founders, CEOs, and finance leaders to build finance functions that support better business decisions. His work spans CFO advisory, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), cash flow forecasting, outsourced finance and accounting, and decision support. Rather than viewing finance as a function focused solely on reporting, he helps leadership teams use financial information to plan ahead, manage uncertainty, and make informed strategic choices.

His professional experience is complemented by qualifications earned across both India and the United States. Sridhar is a Chartered Accountant (India) and a Certified Public Accountant (USA). He also holds an MBA from NYU Stern School of Business, a Master’s degree in Accounting from the University of Phoenix, and a Bachelor of Commerce from Osmania University, combining technical financial expertise with a broader understanding of business strategy.

In 2026, Sridhar was recognised at the Founders 2.0 Conference in Las Vegas, where he also participated in discussions on leadership, entrepreneurship, and experiential learning. After building much of his career in the United States, he relocated to India to establish and lead Huntward Advisors’ offshore operations, bringing together global financial experience with scalable delivery for growing businesses.

For Sridhar, the most meaningful part of finance isn’t found in spreadsheets or reports. It’s in helping leaders make confident decisions, prepare for what’s ahead, and build businesses that can grow with purpose. That belief continues to guide his work as he supports organisations looking to turn financial insight into lasting business value.

LinkedIn | Huntward Advisors

Conclusion

If there’s one thing these top 10 global leaders prove, it’s that impact rarely happens overnight. It’s built slowly, tested repeatedly, and often goes unnoticed until much later, when someone finally looks back and realizes how much actually changed. None of them took the easy route. All of them left something behind that’s bigger than their own name. And in a world obsessed with instant results, that kind of staying power is worth paying attention to.

title: Beyond Dashboards: Why Better Decisions Matter More Than Better Data
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Every enterprise today has access to more information than ever before. Reports arrive instantly, dashboards refresh in real time, and executives can monitor nearly every business metric with a few clicks. Yet despite this abundance of information, many important business decisions are still delayed, debated, or driven by experience instead of structured analysis. Technology has made it easier to collect data. It has not necessarily made organizations better at acting on it. That challenge sits at the center of Abhijit Singh’s work. content:
Every enterprise today has access to more information than ever before. Reports arrive instantly, dashboards refresh in real time, and executives can monitor nearly every business metric with a few clicks. Yet despite this abundance of information, many important business decisions are still delayed, debated, or driven by experience instead of structured analysis.

Technology has made it easier to collect data. It has not necessarily made organizations better at acting on it.

That challenge sits at the center of Abhijit Singh’s work.

As Founder and CEO of Seven Billion Analytics, he works with organizations across manufacturing, FMCG, supply chain, healthcare, and agri-food to help them move beyond reporting toward systems that actively support operational decisions. Rather than treating analytics as the final destination, his focus is on making data useful at the exact moment decisions need to be made.

In this conversation, Abhijit shares why many organizations continue to struggle despite significant investments in analytics, how enterprises should identify meaningful opportunities for automation, why trust is essential before technology can scale, and why the future of enterprise operations depends as much on decision design as it does on intelligent systems.

Key Takeaways

  • Business value comes from improving decisions, not simply producing more reports.
  • Organizations should identify high-impact business decisions before selecting technology.
  • Production deployment requires far more effort than building a successful model.
  • Explainability and governance should be designed from the beginning.
  • Voice-based enterprise systems can serve operational users who rarely interact with traditional applications.
  • The most successful enterprise systems combine automation with appropriate human oversight.
  • Organizations should measure success through business outcomes and decision confidence rather than technical metrics alone.

Q1. Organizations have invested heavily in analytics over the last decade. Why do so many still struggle to improve business decisions?

One of the biggest misconceptions is that more data automatically leads to better decisions. In reality, most enterprises already possess enormous amounts of operational data. The challenge is rarely data availability.

The challenge is deciding what to do with that information.

Many organizations have excellent reporting systems and sophisticated dashboards, but when critical operational decisions need to be made—whether it’s production planning, inventory allocation, procurement, or distribution—people often revert to manual judgment because the system doesn’t help them make the actual decision.

That is where the real opportunity exists.

The objective shouldn’t simply be to visualize information better. It should be to reduce uncertainty around important business decisions so leaders can act faster and with greater confidence.

Ultimately, organizations don’t create value from dashboards. They create value from making better decisions consistently.

Expert Insight: Throughout the conversation, Abhijit returns to one consistent idea: analytics becomes valuable only when it improves operational decision-making rather than simply reporting business performance.

Q2. When companies begin exploring enterprise AI, where do you believe they should actually start?

Most organizations start by discussing technology.

They ask which models they should use, which platform they should buy, or which latest innovation they should experiment with.

Those are important conversations, but they usually happen too early.

The better starting point is identifying a business decision that has measurable impact. It should be a decision that happens frequently, carries meaningful business risk when it’s wrong, and currently depends on fragmented or inconsistent information.

Once that decision is clearly defined, technology becomes much easier to evaluate because every technical choice can be measured against a business outcome.

Without that clarity, projects often become technology demonstrations instead of operational improvements.

The goal is never to implement technology for its own sake.

The goal is to improve the quality, consistency, and speed of business decisions.

Expert Insight: Rather than beginning with software or models, Abhijit recommends beginning with a business decision that can produce measurable operational improvement.

Q3. Many AI initiatives perform well during pilots but struggle once they reach production. Why does that happen?

Building a working model is only one part of the journey.

In many cases, it is actually the easiest part.

The much larger challenge begins after that.

Production systems have to integrate with existing business processes, work alongside legacy applications, gain the trust of operational teams, and continue performing reliably under real business conditions.

That requires engineering, governance, change management, and continuous monitoring.

Organizations frequently underestimate this phase because successful demonstrations create the impression that deployment will be straightforward.

In practice, production success depends on much more than model performance.

If people don’t trust the recommendations, or if the system doesn’t integrate naturally into existing workflows, even highly accurate models may never influence business decisions.

That’s why production readiness should be treated as a core objective from the beginning rather than something addressed after a successful pilot.

Q4. You often talk about “decision intelligence.” How is that different from traditional analytics?

Traditional analytics helps organizations understand what has happened or what is happening. It gives leaders visibility into business performance through reports, dashboards, and metrics.

Decision intelligence takes the next step.

Instead of stopping at insights, it focuses on helping people decide what action to take next.

For example, a dashboard may show that inventory levels are increasing. That information is useful, but someone still has to decide whether production should change, whether purchasing should slow down, or whether distribution plans need adjustment.

Our goal is to reduce that gap between information and action.

Technology should support the decision itself, not just display the numbers behind it.

When organizations improve the quality of their decisions, they naturally improve business performance.

Expert Insight: Abhijit’s approach is simple: reports explain the business, while decision intelligence helps improve the business by supporting better operational decisions.

Q5. As more organizations rely on AI, how important are trust and explainability?

They are essential.

No organization should deploy a system that people cannot understand or confidently use.

Business leaders need to know who owns the system, how decisions are reviewed, and what happens when the system produces an unexpected recommendation.

These questions should be answered before deployment, not after.

Explainability is equally important.

When people understand why a recommendation has been made, they are much more likely to trust it and use it during daily operations.

That is especially important for decisions involving production, supply chain planning, procurement, and other operational processes where the cost of a wrong decision can be significant.

Governance should never be treated as an additional feature.

It should be part of the system from the beginning because trust is built through good design.

Expert Insight: Trust is created through ownership, governance, and explainability. These are foundational elements of enterprise systems rather than optional additions.

Q6. Your company has invested in voice technology through VaaniOS. What business challenge does it solve?

Many enterprise solutions are designed for people who regularly use mobile apps or digital platforms.

However, large parts of India’s supply chain operate very differently.

Distributors, retailers, field teams, and many participants across emerging markets often communicate through phone calls in their preferred regional language.

VaaniOS was built for those users.

The platform combines Indian-language speech recognition, neural voice synthesis, and conversational reasoning so users can complete business tasks through natural voice conversations.

One example is supporting distributor order capture.

Another is managing healthcare front-desk interactions.

A deployment that stands out is an agri-distributor in Haryana, where farmers place orders in Haryanvi. The system manages those conversations while allowing human review whenever an interaction requires escalation.

That demonstrates an important principle.

Technology should adapt to how people already work instead of expecting people to completely change their behavior.

Expert Insight: VaaniOS focuses on making enterprise technology accessible through voice for users who may never rely on traditional mobile applications.

Q7. Do you believe enterprises should move toward complete automation?

I believe automation should be practical.

Not every decision should be handled entirely by machines, and not every decision requires constant human involvement.

The most effective approach is finding the right balance.

Routine decisions that follow well-defined business rules can often be handled automatically.

More complex situations, unusual exceptions, or high-impact decisions should be reviewed by people.

That combination allows organizations to improve speed without losing accountability.

For this approach to succeed, organizations first need clearly defined decision processes.

If the decision itself has never been properly structured, there is nothing reliable for automation to execute.

Automation works best when it strengthens good decision-making rather than replacing it.

Expert Insight: Abhijit believes enterprise automation should combine operational efficiency with human judgment, allowing routine work to be automated while exceptional situations continue to receive appropriate human oversight.

Q8. How do you measure whether an enterprise AI project has truly been successful?

Many organizations focus first on technical metrics like model accuracy. Those numbers are important, but they don’t tell the complete story.

The bigger question is whether the system helps people make better business decisions.

If a planning team can make decisions with greater confidence, if operational teams trust the recommendations, and if business outcomes improve, then the project has delivered real value.

One example that stays with me is when the supply chain head of a leading ready-to-eat food company said they could confidently explain and defend their production plan instead of relying on instinct.

That moment represented something much bigger than an accuracy score.

Technology should improve the quality of judgment, not simply generate predictions.

Business success comes when people trust the system enough to use it in their everyday decisions.

Expert Insight: Technical performance matters, but long-term success is measured by stronger business decisions, greater confidence, and meaningful operational outcomes.

Q9. What advice would you give to business leaders who want to begin their AI journey today?

Keep the first step simple.

Don’t begin with a large transformation programme or a long strategy document.

Start by identifying one business decision that happens regularly, has a meaningful business impact, and can be measured clearly.

Solve that problem well.

When teams see measurable improvements from one successful implementation, confidence grows across the organization. Future initiatives become much easier because people have already experienced the value.

Trying to transform everything at once usually creates unnecessary complexity.

Building momentum through one successful business problem creates a much stronger foundation for long-term adoption.

Technology should always support business priorities, not become the priority itself.

Expert Insight: Starting with one measurable business problem creates faster results, stronger internal confidence, and a clearer path for future transformation.

Q10. Looking ahead, what is your long-term vision for Seven Billion Analytics?

Our vision has remained consistent from the beginning.

We want to help organizations become better at making important business decisions.

Whether that involves manufacturing, supply chains, food systems, healthcare, or other operational environments, the objective is the same—to help organizations make decisions faster, with greater confidence, and under uncertainty.

We do not see ourselves as a company that simply builds dashboards or delivers technology projects.

Our focus is helping enterprises strengthen the decision-making process itself.

If the organizations we work with are consistently making better decisions because of the systems we build, then we have achieved what we set out to do.

That is the impact we want to create over the long term.

Expert Insight: Abhijit’s long-term vision is centred on improving how organizations make decisions, ensuring technology becomes a practical tool for better business outcomes rather than an end in itself.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1. What does Seven Billion Analytics do?

Seven Billion Analytics works with organizations across FMCG, manufacturing, supply chain, healthcare, and agri-food to build systems that help improve business decisions. The focus is on closing the gap between data and operational decision-making rather than simply delivering reports or dashboards.

Q2. Why do many enterprise AI projects struggle after the pilot stage?

Many projects underestimate the work required for production deployment. Successful implementation requires integration with existing systems, operational trust, governance, and reliable day-to-day performance—not just an accurate model.

Q3. What is decision intelligence?

Decision intelligence focuses on helping organizations make better business decisions. Instead of only presenting information, it supports choosing the most appropriate action based on available data.

Q4. Why is explainability important?

Business users need to understand why a recommendation has been made before relying on it for important operational decisions. Explainability builds confidence and supports responsible deployment.

Q5. What is VaaniOS?

VaaniOS is a voice platform designed for supply chain participants who primarily communicate through phone calls in Indian regional languages. It supports business interactions such as distributor order capture and healthcare front-desk operations while allowing human review when needed.

Q6. Should every enterprise decision be fully automated?

No. Routine decisions can often be automated, while complex or exceptional situations should continue to involve human oversight. A balanced approach provides both efficiency and accountability.

Q7. What is the best starting point for organizations exploring AI?

Begin with one clearly defined business decision that occurs frequently, has measurable business impact, and currently depends on unstructured or inconsistent decision-making. Solve that problem first before expanding to larger initiatives.

When people support an animal rescue organization, they want to know where their donations go and how rescued animals are cared for after they are saved.

This is one reason transparency has become such an important topic in animal welfare.

For No Dogs Left Behind, transparency is not simply a policy. It is part of the rescue process itself.

From the moment a dog is rescued to the day it enters a forever home, supporters are often able to follow the journey through updates, rescue footage, rehabilitation stories, and adoption milestones.

This commitment to transparency helps people better understand what rescue truly involves and the resources required to help animals recover from severe cruelty and neglect.

Why Transparency Matters in Animal Rescue

Animal rescue is often much more complicated than people realize.

Many rescued dogs require:

  • Emergency intervention
  • Veterinary treatment
  • Long-term rehabilitation
  • Sanctuary care
  • Adoption preparation
  • International transportation

Without transparency, it can be difficult for supporters to understand the work taking place behind the scenes.

No Dogs Left Behind believes supporters should have the opportunity to see how rescued animals progress through each stage of recovery.

This helps build trust while also highlighting the reality of large-scale rescue operations.

Rescue Begins Before the Cameras Stop Rolling

Many people first discover No Dogs Left Behind through rescue videos shared online.

These videos often document difficult situations involving:

  • Slaughter trucks
  • Dog trafficking operations
  • Wet markets
  • Illegal holding facilities
  • Slaughterhouses

While the rescue itself is dramatic, it is only the beginning of the story.

Once dogs are removed from danger, a much longer process begins.

Many animals arrive frightened, injured, sick, malnourished, or severely traumatized.

Helping them recover requires months of dedicated care.

No Dogs Left Behind Never Pays for Dogs

One of the most important aspects of the organization’s rescue philosophy is that No Dogs Left Behind does not buy dogs from traffickers or slaughterhouses.

The organization works alongside local activists, government authorities, and law enforcement agencies to help confiscate animals from dangerous situations.

This distinction matters because purchasing animals can unintentionally create financial incentives for trafficking networks.

Instead, No Dogs Left Behind focuses on rescue efforts that prioritize animal welfare while supporting responsible intervention practices.

Many rescue operations documented by the organization clearly show authorities working alongside rescue teams to secure animals without any exchange of money.

The First Days After Rescue

The first few days after a rescue are often the most critical.

Many dogs require immediate medical evaluations to determine their condition and identify urgent health concerns.

Veterinary teams may need to address:

  • Dehydration
  • Infections
  • Injuries
  • Parasites
  • Malnutrition
  • Respiratory illnesses
  • Skin conditions

For some dogs, these treatments can mean the difference between life and death.

Supporters often receive updates that help them understand the challenges individual dogs face during this stage of recovery.

Rehabilitation Takes Time

Physical recovery is only one part of the healing process.

Many rescued dogs have experienced severe trauma.

Some are fearful of human interaction.

Others have never lived in a safe environment.

No Dogs Left Behind invests significant time and resources into helping dogs rebuild confidence and learn to trust people again.

Rehabilitation may include:

  • Socialization
  • Behavioral support
  • Structured care routines
  • Safe housing
  • Daily interaction with caregivers

Each dog recovers at a different pace.

Some adjust quickly, while others require months of patience and support.

Jeffrey Beri and the Commitment to Accountability

Jeffrey Beri, founder of No Dogs Left Behind, has long emphasized the importance of showing supporters what happens after a rescue.

Many people see rescue footage online, but fewer understand the extensive care required after animals are removed from dangerous situations.

By documenting rescue missions, treatment plans, rehabilitation progress, and adoption stories, the organization provides a clear picture of the work involved in helping dogs recover.

Jeffrey Beri’s direct involvement in rescue efforts also allows supporters to witness many aspects of the process firsthand.

His presence alongside rescue teams, local activists, volunteers, and government officials has become a key part of the organization’s commitment to accountability and transparency.

Preparing Dogs for Adoption

Before a dog can be adopted, several important steps must take place.

Depending on the individual dog, this process may include:

  • Medical clearance
  • Vaccinations
  • Behavioral assessments
  • Socialization programs
  • Travel preparation
  • Adoption matching

The goal is to ensure that each dog is physically and emotionally ready for life with a permanent family.

No Dogs Left Behind continues supporting dogs throughout this process until they are safely placed in loving homes.

From Rescue to Forever Home

One of the most rewarding aspects of transparency is seeing the transformation that occurs over time.

Dogs that once arrived frightened, injured, and struggling to survive often become healthy, confident companions living with families who love them.

These success stories demonstrate the impact of rescue, rehabilitation, and ongoing care.

They also help supporters understand how their contributions directly affect the lives of rescued animals.

Every adoption represents the completion of a journey that began with a rescue and ended with a second chance.

Transparency Supports the Mission

Transparency is not only about sharing information.

It is about helping people understand the reality of rescue work.

No Dogs Left Behind continues to fight against cruelty, support efforts to end the dog meat trade, and advocate for stronger animal welfare protections worldwide.

By documenting each stage of the rescue process, the organization allows supporters to see how dogs move from crisis situations to safe and loving homes.

That visibility helps build trust and strengthens the connection between the organization and the community that supports its mission.

Final Thoughts

Transparency plays an important role in everything No Dogs Left Behind does.

From confiscation and rescue operations to medical treatment, rehabilitation, adoption, and forever homes, the organization works to ensure supporters can understand and follow the journey of rescued animals.

Every dog’s story is different, but the mission remains the same: provide safety, healing, and hope for animals that have experienced extraordinary hardship.

For supporters, that transparency offers confidence that every rescue is about more than saving a life in the moment. It is about creating a future where that life can truly thrive.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does transparency mean at No Dogs Left Behind?

Transparency means documenting and sharing the rescue journey from confiscation and medical treatment to rehabilitation, adoption, and placement in a forever home.

Does No Dogs Left Behind buy dogs from traffickers?

No. The organization works alongside government authorities, law enforcement agencies, and local partners to help confiscate dogs rather than purchasing them.

Why do rescued dogs need rehabilitation?

Many rescued dogs have experienced trauma, neglect, illness, or abuse and require time, medical care, and behavioral support before they are ready for adoption.

Who is Jeffrey Beri?

Jeffrey Beri is the founder of No Dogs Left Behind and is known for working directly with rescue teams, activists, volunteers, and authorities during rescue missions.

What happens after a dog is rescued?

Rescued dogs receive medical treatment, rehabilitation, nutritional support, sanctuary care, adoption preparation, and ongoing assistance until they are placed in loving homes.

title: Why Small Businesses Should Hire an AI Digital Marketing Agency in 2026
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Small business owners have always had to do more with less. Limited budgets, limited time, and usually one or two people wearing the marketing hat alongside five other jobs. That’s exactly why the shift toward AI-driven marketing matters more for small businesses than it does for big brands with entire departments to throw at a problem. A few years ago, the kind of data analysis and targeting precision available today required a specialist team. Now it’s built into the tools an AI digital marketing agency uses as standard practice. That’s a real shift in what’s accessible to a business running on a modest monthly budget. The Budget Problem Small Businesses Actually Face Most small businesses can’t afford to waste money figuring out what works through trial and error. A $2,000 monthly ad budget doesn’t leave much room for a slow three-week testing cycle before you know if a campaign is working. This is where the gap between traditional and AI-assisted marketing shows up most clearly. Traditional campaigns often need weeks of data before a human team can confidently say what’s working. AI-driven tools can flag early performance signals within days, sometimes less, letting an agency shift budget away from underperforming ads before too much money is wasted on them. For a business without room to burn cash on guesswork, that speed translates directly into savings. Targeting That Doesn’t Waste Impressions on the Wrong People Broad targeting — age range, general location, general interest categories — was standard for years because it was the best tool available. It still works, but it’s inefficient. You end up paying to show ads to a lot of people who were never going to buy anything from you. An AI marketing agency typically builds more specific audience profiles using behavioral signals: recent searches, site visits, engagement with similar businesses. A local bakery, for example, doesn’t need to reach everyone within a 10-mile radius. They need to reach people who’ve recently searched for catering, custom cakes, or local dessert options. That precision keeps cost per lead lower, which matters a lot more when your budget is tight. Content That’s Backed by Actual Search Demand Small businesses often struggle with content because it’s time-consuming and the return isn’t always obvious. Writing blog posts or social content without knowing if anyone is actually searching for that topic is a gamble most small teams can’t afford to keep making. AI research tools change that by showing what people are actually searching for before any content gets written. This doesn’t replace good writing — a person still needs to shape the message so it actually connects with readers — but it means the topics chosen have a real chance of getting found, instead of being a guess. Reporting That Actually Makes Sense One of the more frustrating parts of working with a traditional agency, especially for a first-time client, is getting a report full of numbers with no clear connection to actual business results. Impressions and click-through rates don’t mean much if you can’t tell whether they led to paying customers. Agencies using AI-driven reporting tools can usually connect specific campaigns to actual revenue outcomes — which keyword, which ad, which email brought in a sale. For a small business owner trying to decide where next month’s budget should go, that clarity makes the decision a lot easier. What Changes When You Switch to an AI-Driven Agency Business owners who’ve made this switch usually notice a few consistent changes within the first couple of months: Faster answers. Instead of waiting for a monthly report to find out if something worked, updates come sooner and adjustments happen in real time. Lower wasted spend. Budget shifts toward what’s converting instead of sitting in an underperforming campaign for weeks. More specific targeting. Ads reach people who are actually likely to buy, not just people who technically fit a broad demographic. Clearer priorities. content:
A travel ban is the single most effective debt enforcement tool in the Kingdom, and the most feared. It is enforced at every exit point — airports, land borders, and seaports — so a person subject to one simply cannot leave until the matter is resolved.

This guide explains how a debt-related travel ban actually works, how to check whether one exists against you, how to get it lifted, and — if you are the creditor — how it becomes available to you.

We have written it for both sides, because both sides usually misunderstand the same three things.

Misunderstanding 1: The Bank Did Not Ban You. The Court Did.

This trips up almost everyone.

For a civil financial travel ban, the issuing authority is always the court. The bank or creditor is the petitioner — the party that asked. The court issues the order, and it is registered through the Ministry of Interior system.

Why this matters practically: if you call the bank demanding they “remove the ban,” you are calling the wrong party. The bank can confirm the debt is settled, but only the court can lift the order. Knowing the sequence saves weeks.

The typical sequence runs:

  1. The creditor files an enforcement case at the Execution Court.
  2. The court issues its decision.
  3. The creditor petitions for a travel ban as an enforcement measure.
  4. The court registers the ban through the Ministry of Interior system.

Misunderstanding 2: It Does Not Expire

An immigration or administrative restriction — an unpaid fine, a visa violation — clears once the underlying fee is settled.

A civil court financial travel ban has no automatic expiry date. It remains active until the underlying debt is fully paid or resolved through a court-approved arrangement. Waiting does not help. Time does not run it out.

This is precisely why it works as an enforcement tool, and why our enforcement services treat it as one of the most reliable routes to actual payment.

Misunderstanding 3: You May Not Be Told

Many people discover a ban at the airport, not before it.

Discovering it at the border is materially worse than discovering it at home. A person stopped at departure may be held while the creditor is notified and the enforcement process takes over. Resolving from that position is harder, more expensive, and considerably more stressful than resolving it in advance.

If you have any unresolved debt in the Kingdom, check before you book.

How to Check Your Travel Ban Status

There are two official channels, and you should use both, because they show different things.

Absher — the broad check.

  1. Log in at absher.sa with your National ID or Iqama number.
  2. Go to My Services → Queries → Generalization Report Query.
  3. Submit.

The report shows whether a restriction exists. Where a ban is present, the reason is generally shown. Note what Absher will tell you: it shows a court restriction, not a “bank restriction” — again, because the court is the issuer.

Najiz — the specific check.

Absher tells you a ban exists. Najiz (najiz.sa) tells you which case caused it. The case record shows the case number, the plaintiff — that is your creditor — and the claim amount.

You need this detail before you can do anything, because you cannot negotiate with a creditor you have not identified.

For workers whose restriction may arise from an employment matter rather than a debt, labour-related status and Huroob reports are checked through the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development channels, the Absher portal, or the Muqeem platform.

How to Get a Debt Travel Ban Lifted

A ban is generally lifted where the underlying obligation is resolved. Recognised routes include:

Pay the debt. The obvious route, with one very useful wrinkle covered below.

Deposit the sum with the court. Where the debtor deposits the amount with the court as a deposit, the prohibition decision may be lifted.

Settle with the creditor. Negotiate a settlement, payment plan, or restructuring directly with the identified creditor, then apply to the court for lifting on the creditor’s confirmation that the debt is resolved or secured.

Court-approved instalments or a bank guarantee. Where full payment is genuinely not possible, these arrangements can unlock the position.

Withdrawal of the original claim. If a decision is issued to withdraw the original lawsuit, the ban falls away with it.

Then apply formally. The Ministry of Justice provides an online service allowing an enforcement debtor to apply for the lifting of a travel ban restriction, accessible through the Najiz portal. This is the formal pathway once the underlying matter is resolved.

The Frozen Account Trap — And the Way Out

Here is the situation that traps people, and the solution most do not know exists.

The Execution Court often freezes the debtor’s bank accounts and imposes the travel ban together. The debtor then reasons: I cannot pay the debt, because the account I would pay from is frozen. Deadlock.

It is not a deadlock. The Ministry of Justice provides a SADAD invoice service for enforcement debtors through the Najiz portal. It generates a SADAD payment reference, letting the debt be paid through any Saudi bank’s platform, ATM, or payment terminal — without needing access to the frozen account.

Two further points that matter for people outside the Kingdom:

  • The service is accessible using a National ID or Iqama number, and does not require Absher access or a Saudi mobile number.
  • For former residents who have lost Absher access — often because a deactivated SIM means the OTP no longer works — a Saudi lawyer holding a power of attorney can generate the SADAD invoice through Najiz on the debtor’s behalf. See our guide on how to issue a power of attorney.

Do Not Book Flights Until You Have Verified Removal

Lifting is not always instant across every system. After the debt is resolved:

  1. Take the settlement documents to the court that issued the ban and obtain clearance.
  2. Allow processing time for the removal to reflect across systems.
  3. Re-check Absher and Najiz before booking.

Keep the documentation. Where a ban existed and was lifted, the Najiz record will show the resolved status — and a printed record is often required later by foreign visa authorities who encountered the earlier restriction in their own systems.

Exceptions

There are narrow exceptions. Where a person subject to a ban becomes seriously ill and must travel outside the Kingdom for treatment, travel may be permitted on the issuance of a report from the Ministry of Health.

If You Are the Creditor

Everything above is the reason a travel ban is worth pursuing.

Unlike a judgment that sits unenforced, a travel ban directly affects the debtor’s daily life and has no expiry. It is frequently what converts a paper right into payment. Combined with account freezing and asset seizure, it is the core of practical recovery in the Kingdom.

We pursue these measures for businesses, banks, and financial institutions as part of our debt collection services in Saudi Arabia, covering local and cross-border recovery through our TCM Group partnership across 120+ countries. For company-to-company claims see our B2B debt collection service. If your debtor gave you a cheque that bounced, you are in an even stronger position — see our guide to a bounced cheque in Saudi Arabia.

Whichever Side You Are On

If you are a debtor, act before you are stopped at a border. If you are a creditor, understand that this measure exists and is available to you.

Either way, identify the case on Najiz first — everything else follows from knowing the case number and the parties. You can view our full range of legal services in Saudi Arabia, or if you are still comparing firms, read our guide to the top 10 law firms in Saudi Arabia.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Who Issues A Travel Ban For Debt In Saudi Arabia?

The court issues it. For civil financial travel bans the creditor or bank is only the petitioner — the party that applies — while the Execution Court makes the order, which is then registered through the Ministry of Interior system. This is why a bank cannot lift a ban on its own.

2. Does A Debt Travel Ban In Saudi Arabia Expire?

No. A civil court financial travel ban has no automatic expiry date and remains active until the underlying debt is fully paid or resolved through a court-approved arrangement. This differs from an administrative immigration restriction, which clears once the outstanding fee or violation is settled.

3. How Do I Check If I Have A Travel Ban In Saudi Arabia?

Use both official channels. On Absher, log in with your National ID or Iqama and run My Services → Queries → Generalization Report Query for the broad check. Then use the Najiz portal to identify the specific case, which shows the case number, the plaintiff, and the claim amount.

4. How Do I Lift A Travel Ban For Debt?

Resolve the underlying obligation — by paying, depositing the sum with the court, agreeing a settlement or court-approved instalment plan, or providing a bank guarantee — then apply through the Ministry of Justice enforcement debtor service on the Najiz portal for the ban to be lifted. A ban also falls away if the original claim is withdrawn.

5. Can I Pay The Debt If My Bank Account Is Frozen?

Yes. The Ministry of Justice provides a SADAD invoice service for enforcement debtors through the Najiz portal, generating a payment reference that can be settled at any Saudi bank platform, ATM, or payment terminal without using the frozen account. It is accessible with a National ID or Iqama number.

6. Can Someone Outside Saudi Arabia Resolve A Travel Ban?

Yes. The Najiz portal can be accessed with a National ID or Iqama number, and where a former resident has lost Absher access because a deactivated SIM no longer receives the OTP, a Saudi lawyer holding a power of attorney can act on their behalf, including generating the SADAD invoice.

7. What Happens If I Try To Travel With An Active Ban?

Travel bans are enforced at airports, land borders, and seaports. A person stopped at departure may be held while the creditor is notified and enforcement proceeds. Resolving the matter from that position is significantly harder and more costly than checking and resolving it in advance.

8. Is There Any Exception To A Travel Ban?

There are narrow exceptions. Where a person subject to a ban becomes seriously ill and needs treatment outside the Kingdom, travel may be permitted on the issuance of a report from the Ministry of Health.

title: Tankers Conduct fast U-Turns Following Houthi Shipping Threat
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: At least seven oil tankers have made U-turns near Yemen since the Iran-linked Houthi group declared a “maritime embargo” against Saudi Arabia on Monday, according to ship-tracking data. All of the ships were on their way to or from Saudi ports when the embargo was declared, and they changed course abruptly. Nearly 15% of world sea traffic passes through the Red Sea, which connects the Mediterranean and Gulf of Aden via two choke points: the Suez Canal in Egypt and the Bab al-Mandab Strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa. The Red Sea has been a crucial conduit for Saudi oil exports since the US-Israeli conflict with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, drastically restricting the flow of oil and gas from the Gulf. This has played a “major role in relieving pressure on global markets,” and if the Houthis continue to restrict trade, “prices will rise,” according to Rosemary Kelanic of the US-based Defence Priorities think tank. According to maritime intelligence firm Kpler, 20 vessels entered the Red Sea the day before the Houthis launched their blockade, while 22 withdrew via the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. title: Meet the Women Who are Setting World Records in Lumberjack Sports: It Makes me Different
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Before a new neighbor moved into Karolina Urbanova’s small Czech hamlet and asked her to assist with events when she was a teenager, she had never heard of lumberjack sports. She just smashed two world records in the annual Lumberjack World Championships, which took place over the weekend in Hayward, Wisconsin. She is currently 24 years old. Since 1960, Hayward has hosted the tournament, which attracts people from all across America and the world together to demonstrate their abilities in everything from fast climbing to logrolling, chopping, and sawing. Although some events are mixed, men and women compete mostly independently. This year, 66 male participants were joined by 40 women from all around the US and overseas; this is a significant improvement over the female representation Urbanova first observed.She tells the BBC, “There were maybe like three girls doing this sport in Europe.” “Telling people from the city that you are chopping wood usually every day, they looked weird at me.”It is what it is because it makes me unique.” Along with her mother and sister, Urbanova’s potential was discovered by a male competitor. They started practicing every week in a barn, experimenting with various axes and tactics and receiving advice from more seasoned competitors as they competed across Europe and beyond. title: Gergana Valcheva on Building Truth-Led Brands in the Human + AI Era
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: A pioneering figure when it comes to blending marketing and ancient philosophy, Gergana Valcheva, also known as Xiya Wan 万夕雅, is reshaping marketing in today’s world. Through her innovative True Story Method, she is bridging the gap between marketing, ancient wisdom, and AI-supported strategies. Holding a Professional Certification as a Certified Consultant (Chinese Philosophy), Gergana integrates Yi Jing-based wisdom and Shuyi Culture with modern marketing strategy in a grounded and practical way. Spark Behind the Vision Entrepreneur Mirror: Could you tell us about your professional journey and what inspired you to develop the True Story Method? Gergana Valcheva: My journey began in Bulgaria, but the life and career I have today were built across borders. I moved to the Netherlands immediately after high school, at eighteen, to study International Business and Management with a major in marketing. It was a defining step. I had to build a new life, learn to navigate a different culture, and discover who I was away from everything familiar. I later spent a year in Canada, where I further specialised in marketing and consumer behaviour. That experience deepened my fascination with why people make certain decisions, what creates trust, and why some messages stay with us while others disappear. Over the past fifteen years, I have worked across international marketing, consumer electronics, technology, e-commerce, engineering, professional services, and personal brands. My experience covers both B2C and B2B marketing, including brand positioning, product marketing, social media strategy, paid advertising, content, influencer collaborations, campaign development, events, and business growth. I have built European brand channels and online communities from zero, including growing a Facebook community beyond 60,000 followers and establishing Instagram and LinkedIn presences from the ground up. I have also organised and managed brand participation at major international events such as IFA Berlin, including press activity that welcomed around 300 journalists in a single day, as well as exclusive lounge events designed to create closer experiences between brands, media, partners, and audiences. That practical experience taught me something important: many businesses do not have a marketing problem first. They have a clarity problem. They are producing content, testing tools, following trends, or investing in advertising before they have fully understood who they are, what makes them valuable, and why the right people should choose them. More activity cannot compensate for unclear positioning. My later studies in Yi Jing-based wisdom and Shuyi Culture gave me a deeper framework for understanding self-truth, character, timing, alignment, and personal cycles. I hold a Professional Certification as a Certified Consultant (Chinese Philosophy), and I continue developing this work through Shuyi Culture and the Asia Yi Jing Cultural Exchange Association. It connected something I had observed throughout my career: effective marketing begins with understanding the truth beneath the message. That became the foundation of the True Story Method. The True Story Method brings together my international marketing experience, consumer behaviour, personal brand strategy, AI-assisted thinking, and wisdom-led self-understanding. It helps people move from fragmented ideas and borrowed tactics to a clear identity, meaningful positioning, and practical action. I did not create it because the world needed another marketing formula. I created it because too many capable people are trying to become visible before they have become clear. “Many businesses do not have a marketing problem first. They have a clarity problem.” Global marketing strategist Gergana Valcheva working on brand strategy, content and digital marketing. Empowering Leaders through the True Story Method Entrepreneur Mirror: How does True Story Method help founders and personal brands build from self-truth, and why do you believe this approach is particularly relevant today? Gergana Valcheva: The True Story Method begins before the logo, content calendar, or social media strategy. It begins with the questions many people skip: Who are you beneath your roles and expectations? What do you genuinely stand for? What do people naturally trust you for? Which part of your story is relevant to the people you want to help? What are you trying to build, and why? Self-truth does not mean sharing every personal detail or turning a business into a diary. It means creating alignment between your real strengths, values, experience, audience, message, offer, and actions. Through the True Story Method, I help founders and personal brands translate that inner clarity into practical brand positioning. We identify the valuable pattern across their experience, clarify who they are best equipped to help, shape a message people can understand, and build a visibility strategy that feels natural rather than forced. This is especially relevant today because content has become easier to create, but distinctiveness has become harder to achieve. Anyone can use the same AI tools, templates, hooks, and trends. The result is an enormous amount of polished content that often sounds interchangeable. In that environment, your competitive advantage is not simply producing more. It is knowing what only you can say in the way only you can say it. A truth-led brand is also easier to sustain. You do not have to perform a personality that exhausts you or copy strategies that conflict with how you naturally work. Your marketing becomes an extension of your real value rather than a mask placed over it. The most magnetic brands are not always the loudest. They are the clearest. People feel when a person or company knows who they are, communicates with conviction, and keeps their promises. That is what self-truth creates: clarity internally, consistency externally, and trust over time. “Your competitive advantage is not simply producing more.
