title: The Creator of the Contemporary American Economy, Alan Greenspan, Passes Away at the Age of 100
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Alan Greenspan, the former chair of the US Federal Reserve, passed away at the age of 100, according to his widow. In a statement sent by her workplace, NBC News correspondent Andrea Mitchell stated that her spouse had passed away due to Parkinson’s disease complications. Greenspan was described as “a giant of a man who helped shape the US economy for decades under presidents of both parties, but was always honest in acknowledging his mistakes” by Mitchell. Alan Greenspan was tasked with protecting the US economy and maintaining the stability of the dollar for almost two decades. He oversaw the greatest sustained run of US economic development in a generation while serving as chairman of the Federal Reserve from 1987 to 2006, a position regarded as the second most significant after the president. During his tenure at the Fed, Greenspan, dubbed the “God in the machine” of American finance, turned down every interview request.There was a sign in his office that read, “The buck starts here,” and the media and financial markets relied on his rare public remarks. However, some contend that an excessive dependence on easy credit contributed to both the 2008 sub-prime mortgage crisis and the dot-com bubble of the late 1990s. title: Aubrey Heldt on Shaping the Travel Sector through HTMC by Hariom Travels
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: We recently had the opportunity to have a conversation with Aubrey Heldt, about the evolution of the corporate travel industry over the years. As a senior leader, he has been constantly delivering exceptional services in the industry. Currently, as the Managing Director at HTMC by Hariom Travels, Aubrey fosters long-term client relationships and oversees the travel portfolio of the firm. He believes, “The travel experience can be elevated through innovation and operational excellence.” As we dive into the interview, we will learn more about Aubrey Heldt’s journey, challenges, and milestones throughout his career path. Spark Behind the Journey We started the interview by asking Aubrey Heldt to share the beginning of his professional career and the key moments that shaped his current position. Aubrey shared, “As I started my professional path in the travel industry with Kanoo Travel, the experience of working for such a well-established regional organization gave me invaluable exposure to the foundations of corporate travel and tourism. Initially, I focused more on understanding the operational side of the business, ranging from client servicing, travel management solutions, to daily mechanics that keep corporate travel running seamlessly. That hands-on experience shaped my approach to leadership and reinforced the importance of service excellence, strong relationships, and adaptability in an ever-evolving industry. This phase of my career proved to be a pivotal moment, as I learned to combine strategic leadership with customer-centric service on a global scale. Key moments in this period, like embracing digital transformation, leading through industry disruption, and building trusted partnerships, further strengthened my resilience, adaptability, and commitment to integrity. Today, I remain focused on elevating the travel experience through innovation, operational excellence, and lasting client relationships.” Leading HTMC by Hariom Travels Forward Interested to learn more about Aubrey Heldt’s current role and responsibilities, we asked him to share a glimpse of the same. He explained, “Currently, I lead as the Managing Director of HTMC by Hariom Travels, where I oversee the company’s overall strategy, operations, and growth initiatives. My role focuses on strengthening our corporate travel portfolio, building long-term client relationships, and ensuring service excellence across all touchpoints. From business development, financial performance, supplier partnerships, to team leadership, I work closely with our management team to drive efficiency, innovation, and sustainable growth. Additionally, a key part of my responsibility is positioning HTMC by Hariom Travels as a trusted travel management partner by combining personalized service with modern travel solutions and technology. In addition as a member of the Middle East and Africa Advisory Board of Uniglobe, our Global Travel Network Partner. I ensure to bridge local realities with global standards to deliver safer, compliant and cost effective travel and turn regional complexity into a competitive advantage for clients and the network.” Empowering Businesses With Bespoke Solutions We then asked, “What core services does your business provide that makes them unique?” “At HTMC by Hariom Travels, we go beyond booking travel; we deliver fully integrated travel management solutions tailored to each client’s needs. From corporate travel and MICE management to customized holidays and visa support, our focus is on efficiency, transparency, and seamless execution. With a client-centric approach, commitment to quality, and strong global partnerships, HTMC by Hariom Travels stands apart from the competition. By combining advanced reporting and cost-control tools with personalized attention, we ensure every journey is smooth, strategic, and value-driven. In a rapidly evolving travel landscape, our mission is clear: to be a trusted partner that empowers businesses and travelers with reliability, innovation, and peace of mind,” Aubrey shared. title: Apple Could Hike Pricing as the AI Boom Drives up Chip Costs
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Apple’s CEO has stated that the company intends to boost product prices due to the rising cost of memory chips. Tim Cook, Apple’s outgoing CEO, told the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that price rises were “unavoidable” since the situation with memory chips had become “unsustainable”. He did not specify when the prices would rise or which products would be affected. It’s also unclear whether the price increases will effect the iPhone 18, which is set to be released in September. Memory chips are crucial components in smart gadgets like mobile phones, but the surge in artificial intelligence (AI) has increased their pricing in recent months.Cook told the WSJ, “We’re doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed on to us. We’ve been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable. There’s less supply at a time when consumers want devices and the memory guys are passing on huge price increases,” said Cook, who will be replaced by John Ternus as Apple’s CEO in September after 15 years.We absolutely require memory pricing and supply to recover to normal levels for consumer products. title: The Iran Agreement Poses a political Nightmare for Netanyahu
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The US cease-fire agreement with Iran has presented Israel’s prime minister with a political nightmare, destroying the three pillars of Benjamin Netanyahu’s political career and trapping him in a new security predicament. How can the leader who made confronting Iran the centerpiece of Israel’s security strategy conclude the war with Iran’s regime in arguably stronger position? And how can his old, battered political image as Israel’s “Mr Security” withstand Washington and Tehran’s insistence that Israel stop striking Hezbollah in Lebanon, months before an Israeli general election? Netanyahu’s options right now are not good. They were summarized by opposition leader Yair Lapid in the Knesset on Monday as “either a direct and destructive confrontation with our greatest ally, or a submissive surrender of Israeli interests”. US President Donald Trump’s expletive-laden opinion that Netanyahu acted without judgment in authorizing an assault on Beirut on Sunday has been pounced on by his political challengers and media critics, who are already preoccupied with the election that must be held before the end of October. However, statements from Netanyahu’s own Likud party and far-right cabinet ministers in his governing coalition demonstrate the strain he faces from inside – most notably, Tehran’s demand that the ceasefire cover “military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon”.The US cease-fire agreement with Iran has presented Israel’s prime minister with a political nightmare, destroying the three pillars of Benjamin Netanyahu’s political career and trapping him in a new security predicament. In April 2026, Radwan led CarbonTech’s first major field validation deployment at the Al-Rujina Oil Distribution Company terminal in Sabha City, Libya, which is a Category A hazardous waste site that had accumulated decades of untreated industrial contamination across four distinct zones. Under his technical oversight, the deployment converted 4,200 grams of toxic slop-oil into 7,305 grams of commercial-grade multi-fuel product in just three days, with zero excavation, zero incineration, and zero regulatory violations. The operation transformed what would have cost an estimated $500,000 to $1 million under conventional remediation methods into a revenue-generating remediation event, successfully validating CarbonTech’s core investment thesis that industrial hazardous waste is not a sunk cost, but a high-value feedstock.

Radwan’s ability to lead CarbonTech with credibility and precision is rooted in more than three decades of executive-level experience directing multibillion-dollar engineering, procurement, and construction programs across the global energy sector. His prior career spans oil and gas, refining, petrochemical processing, offshore drilling, and heavy industrial infrastructure across five continents. 

Most recently, he served as a Technical Director and Project Director embedded with Saudi Aramco’s Project Management Team through the Wood Group, where he oversaw the full engineering and construction lifecycle for the Safaniyah and Manifa Crude Increment Development Program, a landmark expansion targeting an additional 1,000 MBCD of production capacity. Before that, he spent seven years as Project Director for KBR-AMCDE, providing senior project management consultancy for landmark Saudi Aramco developments including the Jizan Refinery and Zuluf water supply infrastructure. Earlier roles include directing a $1.2 billion gathering center for Kuwait Oil Company with DODSAL and managing large-scale chemical and fertilizer production complexes across North Africa with Jacobs Engineering.

His technical credentials were established at Oklahoma State University, where he earned both his Bachelor of Science in Civil/Structural Engineering and his Master of Science in Civil Engineering, followed by his Professional Engineering license from APEGA in Alberta, Canada. He spent the first two decades of his career progressing from structural engineer to lead project manager at Worley and the Ralph M. Parsons Company, executing projects ranging from Arctic drilling installations to facility rehabilitation programs in Iraq.

Recognized by the Korn Ferry Executive Leadership Assessment for demonstrated strategic foresight and organizational effectiveness, Radwan brings to CarbonTech a leadership philosophy built entirely on three principles: absolute accountability, disciplined risk governance, and an unwavering commitment to operational excellence. At CarbonTech Energy Solutions, those principles are not merely applied to project execution; they underpin every commercial decision, every technology deployment, and every investor commitment the company makes.

content:
For years, industrial flavor design has relied on standard chemical templates and synthetic shortcuts, but Juan José Thuemme focuses on how underlying molecular structure and clean chemistry work together. With an extensive background as a flavor chemist and industrial innovator, he helps manufacturers, dessert brands, and global food companies navigate major shifts in consumer taste demands. Today, he operates at the intersection of natural extract architecture, clean-label compliance, and scalable flavor infrastructure, running Etadar to help clients turn raw sensory ideas into protected, high-value flavor assets.

We sat down with Juan José to discuss his professional journey, the realities of clean flavor extraction, and how structured flavors are changing the game for the global food and beverage market.

“Could you start by telling us about your journey and work?”

“My journey has been very intense. I need to create more than 10 trendy and cozy flavors. Right now, I am duplicating all Dubai-style desserts, which are a very good flavor collection. I am also duplicating flavors and need to create a natural vanilla extract using an economical formula costing less than USD 5.”

“How has your company/work evolved since you started?”

“First, I introduced many new chemicals into the collection of raw materials. I created native flavors for Mexico, including: Bakery flavor collections, Tequila flavors, Mezcal flavors. I also started creating replacements for different restricted materials used in flavors, as well as flavor enhancers.”

“How does your work contribute to the ecosystem in your region?”

“My contribution is avoiding the use of toxic substances and hazardous or explosive materials whenever possible.”

“What three qualities do you believe are critical for success in your industry?”

“First, you must work with knowledgeable people who can understand technological demands. Second, you must possess the technical drive to spearhead innovation in flavor design. Third, you must maintain a strict focus on developing economical, high-performance formulations that can meet strict commercial yields.”

“What are your views on the current technological advancements in the business world?”

“I work with economical flavors based on reaction flavors or processed flavors. These include Maillard flavors, where chemicals are enhanced through ammoniation, maturation by heating, or recombination with other chemicals. I use local extracts to round out flavors and increase yields. I also develop flavors with the help of chefs who guide the creation of flavors for the new generation of desserts worldwide. A good example is the success of Dubai-style desserts, where basic flavors are combined with alternative flavors to create unique products.”

“How would you guide someone to navigate the key challenges you faced when establishing yourself in this industry?”

“My advice for overcoming challenges is to work with knowledgeable people who can understand technological demands and drive innovation in flavors. Some of the latest technologies I have developed include structured flavors, where flavors are designed to intensify and enhance taste profiles. These structured flavors help create stronger and more appealing flavor experiences.”

By anchoring industrial science in regional authenticity and eco-conscious engineering, Juan José Thuemme continues to re-engineer the foundational building blocks of taste. As consumer expectations shift toward clean, safe, and distinctively premium sensory experiences, his specialized research at Etadar bridges the critical gap between raw chemical execution and highly profitable food innovation. For enterprise operators looking to secure sustainable flavor alternatives or capture the world’s next viral dessert trend, the path forward relies entirely on this level of disciplined molecular architecture.

content:
Wałysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, Poland’s deputy prime minister and minister of defense, met with Kyrylo Budanov, the head of Ukraine’s presidential office, in Warsaw on Saturday to discuss Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s decision to name a military unit “Heroes of the UPA.”

“Poland and Ukraine are partners when it comes to security,” Deputy Prime Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz wrote in a post on X following the meeting. However, we have to be honest with one another about history.

“I outlined Poland’s expectations on the decision to name one of the military units after the UPA at a meeting today with General Kyrylo Budanov, head of President Zelenskyy’s office. The memory of Volhynia’s victims cannot be compromised. He wrote, “There are boundaries that must not be crossed.” Kyiv had not issued a statement on the negotiations at the time this article was published.

We have been progressively reestablishing productive communication for about two years. Exhumations and searches have been unblocked. We have reburied victims in various locations with respect and in accordance with Christian tradition,” the Ukrainian minister continued. Additionally, he emphasized that Ukrainian soldiers “did not have even the slightest anti-Polish intentions” when they decided to rename the unit “Heroes of the UPA.

Sarjan acts as Founder, Master Craftsman, and Lead Strategist. His leadership style demonstrates that analytical intelligence and creative excellence coexist, positioning him as a modern polymath. This duality forms the heartbeat of Haus Creative, an organisation built to challenge and inspire through humanistic, spiritual, and creative values rooted in authenticity and truth. Haus Creative functions as a creative think tank, creating a powerful network effect of inspiration. His writings on advertising, politics, society, arts, and human development serve as a source of inspiration for readers and collaborators alike, offering ideas that are adapted and translated.

The Philosophy of Unity Consciousness

At the center of everything Sarjan does is the Unity Consciousness giving model. This philosophy rests on one simple idea: creativity has to contribute to our collective progress as humans. The Lotus Leaf serves as the symbol for this framework. It represents a commitment to “giving while building.” Each leaf signifies a different path of benevolence, whether that is community, culture, or human development. In a world increasingly driven by speed and superficiality, the philosophy offers brands and institutions a rarer sense of authenticity, meaning, and cultural depth. The green shoots of Sarjan’s influence can now be seen emerging across industry verticals, tech, charities, international organisations, and the creative sectors garnering a distinguished and notable global following.

Where Strategy Meets Imagination

Sarjan isn’t just creative. He brings more than fifteen years of senior strategic leadership experience across global CPG and multiple industries, having managed multi-billion-dollar categories, performance strategy and transformations.

His deep corporate executive expertise, combined with lifelong intellectual and creative pursuits, has been recognized, resulting in trailblazing work for those seeking originality and depth. While Beach Haus Creative focuses on multidisciplinary consultancy, Beach Haus Boutique, the award-winning gallery-led property platform, is where he curated more than 30 artists, including talent connected to the Tate Modern and Saatchi Gallery, bringing a fine art vision to life through immersive guest experiences.

Bridging British Heritage and Future Innovation

As an Englishman with Golden Punjab roots he bridges classic heritage with trailblazing modern creativity, architecting a unique creative ecosystem, to champion UK creativity on the global stage. British Institutions including Creative UK, Freemasonry, Quatuor Coronati, Crafts Council, Decimus Burton Society, Royal Society of St George,  William Morris Society, and the Guild of Pastoral Psychology amongst others.

Through Satya, the consulting wing of his firm, Sarjan supports the British creative economy directly. He advises on enterprise transformation and innovation that looks toward the future.   By combining British craft with global trends and subcultural insight, Sarjan has created a genuine reflection of his worldview, a natural expression of who he is.

Impact and Recognition

Sarjan’s work has earned him Fellowships at the Royal Society of Arts, the Royal Asiatic Society, and the Royal Historical Society. He is a Freeman of the City of London and a Freeman of the Worshipful Company of Marketors. His recent wins speak for themselves, including Creative Consultancy Firm of the Year and Art Gallery of the Year for 2026 through 2027. The most recent recognition, awarded in May 2026, was Managing Director of the Year in Strategic Advisory and Creative Consultancy from UK Enterprise.

In this era of relentless technological transformation, Sarjan Ram represents a different kind of leadership. He is someone who can harmonize business and culture to find a more meaningful, connected future.

2. Saša Pejić, MSc | Building Resilience through the Art of Financial Architecture

Saša Pejić didn’t learn about financial risk from a textbook alone. Growing up in Southeast Europe during the 1990s meant living through a masterclass in economic instability. Watching a world change overnight left a mark on him, and it is exactly why he spends his life today helping others build foundations that won’t crumble when the wind changes.

As the founder of Pannon Group NS, Saša acts as a professional “financial architect.” He doesn’t just look at market movements. Instead, he focuses on the bones of a person’s wealth. His core belief is that long term safety depends on the quality of the structure you build around your capital, not the noise of the daily news cycle.

Why the Structure Matters

With over 3,000 reports and expert analyses under his belt for banks and courts, Saša knows exactly where the cracks usually appear. He helps entrepreneurs and professionals stop worrying about inflation or sudden liquidity gaps by creating a plan that is actually durable. He uses modern tech and AI to model different scenarios, but he is quick to tell his clients that data is useless if it doesn’t lead to a clear, confident decision.

For Saša, this is a personal mission. It is about taking the complex, sometimes scary world of macroeconomics and turning it into something manageable. He wants his clients to have more than just money. He wants them to have certainty.

A Voice for the Long Term

You might recognize Saša from the business platforms where he shares his thoughts on the psychology of money and global trends. He has built a massive community of over 50,000 followers, and his insights have been viewed more than 20 million times. This isn’t just about “content,” it is about making financial education accessible to everyone.

Through his collaborations with international fintech firms and a global network of wealth advisors, Saša has turned his local expertise into a worldwide perspective. His guiding principle is one that anyone can get behind. In the long run, you don’t need to have the world’s most brilliant idea. You just need a solid structure that allows your good choices to stack up and grow over time.

3. Daniel A. MacKenzie | Human Focused, Global Business Leader, Entrepreneur, and Impact Strategist

“Great people come to us to make even greater people possible.” – Emerson

Daniel A. MacKenzie is a global executive with extensive international experience and the founder of GENALYTIX, an enterprise dedicated to building value across high-impact sectors, including AI, Collaborative Healthcare, Agri-Tech, Sustainable EnergySolutions, andEntertainment& Media.

Operating with a borderless mindset, Daniel has spent his career at the forefront of global technology integration. He is recognized for a leadership style driven by an engaging, positive attitude, an inclusive approach to co-authorship, and a passion for creating mutually beneficial outcomes that enable teams to cross the finish line together.

GENALYTIX is structured around five core pillars: being human-focused, climate-conscious, environmentally aware, academically integrated, and community-connected. Daniel’s beliefs drive sensible business expansion and fair-trade practices. His strategic thought leadership ensures long-term paradigm shifts in global marketplaces, blending financial success with ethically driven, sustainable development.

He firmly believes that business is personal first and that making progress must also include making a difference. The best technology matters only when it is backed by real human connection. Rather than being constrained by traditional workplace boundaries, he focuses on mentoring the next generation of successful professionals.

He encourages individuals and organizations to rise above mediocrity and strive for excellence. He fosters an environment where teams feel comfortable trying new ideas and learning as much from failure as success. For Daniel, success is not only about growth in business but also about contributing to the benefit of society, doing more than most for the many, and achieving a positive impacton people’s lives and the communities served.

4. Simon Villaflor Hague | Creating Leadership Impact Through Courage and Connection

Simon Villaflor Hague didn’t learn leadership from a textbook. He learned it in the busy kitchens of northern England. Growing up in Derbyshire, in the Peak District, Simon began his career at a stately home and a Michelin-rated restaurant. These intense settings taught him that success relies on trust, communication, and respect, no matter the hierarchy. 

Today, Simon is a well-known business leader in the global food and beverage industry. He also strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). His career path has been intentionally varied, covering different roles in culinary, research and development, marketing, and commercial leadership. He has worked in many places around the world, including the UK, Europe, Asia (Hong Kong, Singapore, the Philippines), and North America. This broad international experience has influenced his focus on understanding cultures, showing humility, and recognizing the importance of local consumer insights.

As a commercial leader, Simon believes that business growth, innovation, and social impact go hand in hand. In the foodservice sector, he aims to help customers prepare for the future by grounding innovation in sustainable nutrition, functional benefits, and transparency. 

By focusing on solutions that provide real value to customers, communities, and the planet, Simon shows that sustainability and commercial success support each other. His approach involves careful listening and engaging with customers to make sure that global strategies have local relevance. 

Alongside his commercial duties, Simon acts as the LGBTQI Global Transformation Lead at Kerry. Based on his own experiences of feeling like an outsider, he promotes inclusion not just as a set of policy statements but as an essential leadership skill.

Simon advocates for closing the gap between corporate intention and everyday impact, ensuring that inclusion is measured by accountability, equitable promotion, and psychological safety. Under his leadership, Kerry’s PRYSM employee network has flourished as a space for education and allyship. His impactful advocacy and grassroots leadership earned him the Inspiring People Award for Courage in 2023, and he was named one of Yahoo Finance’s 100 Future Leaders in 2021.

Simon is an active public speaker and thought leader, utilizing platforms like LinkedIn to demonstrate that business success and humanity are deeply connected. He champions storytelling as a vital tool for building organizational trust, frequently sharing personal milestones, detours, and moments of doubt to normalize authenticity in executive roles.

Looking toward the future of corporate health, Simon is committed to leaving a legacy where every individual feels seen, valued, and empowered to bring their whole self to work.

5. Catherine Tondelli | Global Entrepreneur, Corporate Meeting and Event Strategist, and Champion for Women’s Empowerment

Catherine Tondelli is a successful business owner and international leader. For over 30 years, she has helped companies grow in advertising, publishing, hotels, events and business communications. As the Founder and CEO of Meeting Angels, a Rome-based boutique agency specializing in venue sourcing, meeting and event strategy, Catherine helps international corporations, associations, and organizations across the US, Europe, the UK, and the Middle East optimize their operations, save time and money in their meeting and event planning and maximize their visibility. 

Her agency is proudly woman-certified through WEConnect International, featuring an all-women team dedicated to being a true “guardian angel” for clients from venue finding, contract negotiation to a flawless execution.

“True leadership isn’t just about delegation; it’s about working side by side, encouraging individuality, and lifting others as you grow.”

Beyond her agency, Catherine is a deeply committed institutional leader. She serves as the President of the Professional Women’s Association (PWA) of Rome, where she leads an eight-person board and a thriving community of over 150 members, an organization she successfully led with her board to grow by triple in numbers. Through target initiatives in mentorship, networking, workshops and education, she aims to support women at every stage of their professional development. 

Her global activism is supported by her role as G100 Italy Country Chair for Hospitality and Tourism, where she promotes women’s leadership worldwide.

Catherine grew up believing that financial independence is the best form of empowerment. She sees entrepreneurship as the most dependable path to economic freedom for women. This core belief comes from her mother, who worked until she was 85 and is her greatest inspiration. In practice, Catherine leads with empathy and a mindset for change. She focuses on active listening and creating environments where everyone has the chance to thrive.\

Her journey from San Diego to Rome, with an important stop in London, is described in her memoir, Three Coins in the Fountain (available on Amazon). The book highlights the humor and resilience needed to navigate those significant cultural shifts. Today, whether she is consulting for global executives, mentoring students, playing music, or caring for stray cats, Catherine approaches life with genuine optimism. For her, every unexpected turn is just another
opportunity to step up, inspire, and make a real impact.

6. Founder & Chairman – EFG-HUB Technologies

He is a Cameroonian entrepreneur, business strategist, and visionary founder of EFG-HUB Technologies, a global ecosystem connecting Africa, the Gulf, and international markets through technology, trade, logistics, media, and innovation.

With more than 15 years of experience across Africa, Europe, and the Middle East, he has dedicated his work to helping African businesses, entrepreneurs, and young innovators access global opportunities through digital transformation and cross-border collaboration.

Under his leadership, EFG-HUB Technologies has expanded into a multi-division ecosystem covering B2B trade, corporate services, logistics, AI & cybersecurity, media, branding, and professional training.

One of his flagship initiatives is the EFG Afro Market Portal, a B2B platform designed to connect African suppliers, producers, and exporters with verified international buyers worldwide.

Through EFG Vision, the media and branding division of the ecosystem, Ambe also promotes African entrepreneurship, innovation, and digital storytelling through podcasts, branding solutions, and global media engagement.

Driven by a strong belief in ethical leadership, innovation, and youth empowerment, Ambe Fidelis Ndang continues to advocate for sustainable business growth, digital inclusion, and Africa’s integration into the future global economy.

“Connecting Africa to the Future Through Innovation, Trade & Technology.”

7. Natanya Wachtel | Behavioral Science-Powered Marketing, Healthcare Strategist, and Advocate for Purpose-Driven Wellness

Natanya Wachtel is a behavioral psychology-based healthcare leader and show host who changes how people approach mental health and personal wellness. For over 20 years, she has combined consumer psychology and data analytics to help wellness and healthcare brands connect with people more authentically.

As the founder of New Solutions Network, Natanya leads a specialized collective of companies that, in part, uses behavioral science to design compassionate, effective commercialization strategies, health education programs, and media. Founded in 2008, the network has grown into a multi-division ecosystem spanning behavioral science consulting, media production, wellness innovation, life sciences, and ethical technology. On the consulting side, it advises Fortune 500 companies and mission-driven organizations on how people actually think, decide, and change.

Its media division, The Natanya Experience, produces original programming including Psych + Hip Hop and Game Mindset — that carries mental health conversations into high-pressure worlds like sports, entertainment, and law enforcement. Its wellness arm builds the tools to match: identity-mapping frameworks, applications, and immersive technology for the nervous system’s conventional systems are slow to reach. The throughline across every division is a single conviction, that people do their best work, and their best healing, when they are met as whole human beings rather than the version that fits the org chart.

Her network partners exclusively with organizations that prioritize health and public benefit, ethical innovation, and community support over corporate profit.

“I don’t teach the way out from a mountaintop. I teach it from inside the climb, because that is the only place I have ever stood.” 

Natanya is deeply involved in building modern mental health tools. She was the co-founder of evrmore.io, an empathy-driven artificial intelligence platform designed to help young people build emotional resilience and navigate social challenges. Starting in June 2026, she will host the Hear Me Now! podcast, filmed at the United Nations in partnership with Montessori Model United Nations (MMUN).

Natanya grew up traveling the world alongside her mother, an immigrant who became a global corporate executive. Witnessing severe wealth and healthcare disparities at a young age inspired her lifelong commitment to giving back. Today, she translates that commitment into direct community action. She has donated numerous university scholarships and served as Board Chair for Women Who Create, a New York City nonprofit that mentors and provides scholarships to young women of color.

Her professional standing is matched by a personal resilience that few of her peers have been tested by. A mother of five and a young widow who later remarried, Natanya has rebuilt her life and her company not once but twice. In 2015, a spinal injury left her temporarily paralyzed and bedridden for a year; she relearned how to walk and rebuilt her health and her business from the ground up. A decade later, in 2025, she fell from a former product partner’s stage at an industry event, sustaining a traumatic brain injury, a broken arm, and months in a neck brace. She rebuilt a brain, a voice, and a company at the same time — choosing meditation, non-invasive neurostimulation, and integrative protocols over the multiple surgeries she was advised to have, and exceeding every recovery marker her doctors set.

That lived experience is not a sidebar to her work; it is the operating system beneath it. Building a company devoted to human flourishing while privately fighting her way back from collapse forced a reckoning most wellness leaders never face: what it means to sell healing while still doing the work yourself. It is the reason New Solutions Network is built for real nervous systems shaped under pressure, not for ideal conditions that almost no one actually has.

Her work has been recognized widely. She serves on the Fast Company and Harvard Business Review Executive Boards, has been featured in Forbes, Psychology Today, TEDx, and across more than thirty-five publications, and has received the Marquis Who’s Who Humanitarian Award, the HEaL Brilliance in Healthcare honor, a World’s Leaders Magazine cover, and recognition on the INNOVATE100 and Dreamers & Doers Women to Watch lists. She writes openly about leadership, identity, and healing for outlets including Fast Company. Whether she is advising healthtech founders, mentoring the next generation, or rebuilding herself again, Natanya leads with radical honesty, proof that the most durable leadership is forged, not credentialed.

8. Dr. Karen Figueiredo | Legal Leader with Vast Experience in Social Security Expert and Institutional Strategist

“Women in law do not ask for permission. They build, transform, and lead with excellence.” 

Dr. Karen Figueiredo is a lawyer who believes the legal system should protect real people. She started her own firm, Karen Figueiredo Advocacia, to defend social rights and assist everyday citizens. Karen focuses on Social Security Law, helping people with retirement planning, disability claims, and public pensions. She is known for combining strong legal skills with kindness, ensuring her clients achieve financial security and peace of mind.

Beyond her office, Karen is a committed leader in the legal community. She made history by becoming the first woman elected and then re-elected to preside over the 35th subsection of OABRJ. During her leadership, she worked to support local lawyers, ensuring that professionals outside the big cities felt valued, connected, and heard.

Today, she helps shape the future of her profession through several key roles. She serves as the Vice Director of Social Security Affairs for OAB/RJ and collaborates directly with the National Social Security Law Commission. She is also an active member of the Brazilian Association of Women in Legal Careers, where she advocates for fellow female professionals.

For Karen, traditional legal values and modern thinking go hand in hand. She respects the foundations of law but understands that today’s world needs quick problem-solving and clear communication. She does not let old workplace barriers hold her back. Instead, she uses her position to open doors for other women, mentoring the next generation of lawyers and demonstrating that true leadership involves lifting others as you grow.

Website | Instagram | LinkedIn

9. Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu | A Thoughtful Approach to Care, Research, and Human Connection 

Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu has built a career that reflects both discipline and curiosity. Trained as a family physician, she completed her medical studies at the University of Iași in Romania and later pursued research in family medicine at Maastricht University in the Netherlands. Early on, she showed a clear interest in understanding not just disease, but the many factors that shape a person’s health.

Over the years, her work has taken her far beyond the clinic. She has presented her research at more than 140 international conferences and has published over 60 articles in well-regarded medical journals. Her role within the academic community is equally active. She is a member of the Academy for Professionalism in Healthcare, contributes to The Journal of Patient Experience as part of its editorial review board, and serves as an Associate Editor for Primera Scientific Publication. These roles reflect her ongoing commitment to improving both medical knowledge and patient care.

One of the most defining aspects of her journey is her decision to build a private practice based on a medical home model. For more than a decade, she has worked directly with patients in their own environments. This shift has allowed her to observe details that are often missed in traditional consultations. Daily routines, family dynamics, access to resources, and even subtle patterns of communication all play a role. Through this approach, she has gained a deeper understanding of how health is influenced by more than just clinical symptoms.

Dr. Bistriceanu often speaks about the importance of communication. In her view, the way people interact can shape both mental and physical well-being. Simple qualities such as respect, honesty, and kindness are not abstract ideals. They are practical elements that affect how people feel and function. She believes that no one exists in isolation, and that everyday exchanges, whether personal or professional, leave a lasting impact on health.

Her approach to medicine also focuses on looking beneath the surface. Rather than treating isolated symptoms, she works to understand the root of imbalance. This perspective often leads to better outcomes, not only in terms of treatment but also in patient satisfaction and long-term stability. It is a method that requires patience, attention, and a willingness to listen.

Alongside her medical and academic work, Dr. Bistriceanu is also a published poet. She has authored seven volumes, offering a different lens through which she explores human experience. This creative side adds another layer to her work, one that values reflection as much as precision.

In many ways, her journey brings together science and sensitivity. She continues to contribute to healthcare with a steady focus on people, not just processes. Her work serves as a reminder that good medicine is not only about knowledge, but also about understanding the lives behind each patient.

10. Günter Loibl on Reshaping Music Production and Distribution

Leaders like Günter Loibl are shaping the music industry with their passion for music and new technologies. As a founder and CEO of multiple successful music business companies, his vision is to bridge music production, digital distribution, and emerging audio technologies.

Starting his entrepreneurial endeavours with Rebeat, Günter established it as a physical distribution for CDs and DVDs. Eventually, adapting to technological advancements, he founded Rebeat Digital, contributing his part to the rise of digital music. Currently, Rebeat Digital has become a leading name in the field, with its in-house developed Music Enterprise Software (MES) at the core. From digital music distribution to sales analyses, the MES integrates everything into a single system, empowering easy music distribution from around the globe. 

Additionally, Loibl bought the majority of Preiser Records in 2013, one of Austria’s oldest and most established classic labels, which currently comprises over 30,000 titles. Moreover, he is the co-founder of Legitary, built along with Nermina Mumic, a PhD graduate from the Technical University of Vienna. The startup’s mission is clear: to improve transparency in music streaming data for stores, labels, and artists while reducing errors and preventing fraud in royalty accounting. The venture even won the MIDEM Lab award in Cannes in 2019, reflecting the recognition it earned in the music startup industry. 

With a strong vision to promote vinyl culture, Loibl co-founded the Vinyl Alliance, a global organisation that strengthens the vinyl record business. His contribution to bringing innovative solutions in the field of music has resulted in Loibl building a Dolby Atmos recording studio at Rebeat’s headquarters. Envisioning to channel his passion for music in the right direction, Loibl reflects, “I have recently returned more actively to hands-on recording and mixing, releasing several records with Viennese pop-rapper Syko.” 

Known for building artist-focused platforms, Loibl launched Gimme Beat, and Yeebra in 2025, a next-generation physical music distribution platform designed for independent artists and smaller labels. By making production and distribution easily accessible to all, he empowers artists to reach a wide audience without the need for traditional labels.

Aligning his passion for music with his business endeavours, Günter Loibl is reimagining music through innovation and artist-centred developments.

Over the last ten years, he has built a personal investing track record averaging 22.5% per annum across global public markets, spanning Wall Street, London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Singapore, and the ASX. His investment approach has been grounded in disciplined position sizing, macro-aware sector rotation, options strategy, and a deliberate move into concentrated private opportunities.

That experience has given Brendon more than performance. It has given him a practical understanding of how capital moves across cycles, markets, and asset classes, and where opportunity tends to emerge before it becomes widely recognised.

This perspective has been reinforced by direct operating experience.

Brendon was an early backer of a private Australian fintech, supporting the business with both capital and strategic input as it scaled. That early conviction has since grown into an estimated 30x return on invested capital and remains one of the defining outcomes in his private market track record.

Alongside investing, Brendon is also the Founder and CEO of Gybe Sailing Charters, a premium experiential business operating across Sydney Harbour and Australia’s east coast. There, he has built a reputation for operational discipline, brand clarity, and turning a lifestyle-led business into a scalable, cash-generative platform.

Together, these experiences shape the investment philosophy behind his current venture strategy.

His focus is clear: concentrated, high-conviction capital deployed into category-defining founders building across fintech, wealthtech, proptech, and the broader productivity and automation stack, with a differentiated focus on the Asia, Australia, and Africa corridor.

For Brendon, this is not simply a geographic thesis. It is a structural one.

As digital infrastructure expands and demographic growth accelerates, some of the most compelling opportunities are emerging in markets where financial systems are being rebuilt, SME ecosystems are digitising quickly, and mobile-first infrastructure is transforming access and scale.

This is where Brendon sees a clear edge.

Through long-standing relationships, trusted partners, and years of exposure across Asian and African business networks, he brings founders more than capital. He offers access to markets and strategic corridors that remain overlooked by many traditional investors, but are increasingly shaping the next generation of high-growth economies.

From cross-border payments and embedded finance to SME credit infrastructure, agritech, and mobile-led financial systems, Brendon’s focus is on businesses solving structural problems in markets where adoption is rising fast and legacy systems remain open to reinvention.

What sets this approach apart is not just reach, but capital fluency.

Brendon’s experience across public equities, options, private markets, and multi-asset allocation has built a practical understanding of how liquidity, credit, and macro cycles shape value long before they become consensus. In a market where capital efficiency matters more than capital abundance, that perspective is increasingly valuable.

It is this combination of market discipline, operator instinct, and frontier-market access that defines his investment lens.

For Brendon, the opportunity is clear. The next era of venture will not be defined only by where capital has historically concentrated, but by where it can move with the greatest conviction next.

LinkedIn | Website 

3. Kelly Marie Mackinnon | From Potential to Precision in Business Growth

“Stay focused on yourself, your goals, and your vision; the rest will fall into place.”

For Kelly Marie Mackinnon, entrepreneurship is not just about building businesses. It is about building people, ideas, and long-term impact. With over 15 years of experience across industries, she has positioned herself as a driving force behind brands that aim to grow with clarity and purpose.

Based in Dubai since 2008, Kelly Marie is the Founder and CEO of KMM Dubai, a company that brings together business mentoring, events, and brand management under one strategic vision. Her work focuses on helping businesses move beyond potential and into execution, creating structures that support sustainable growth.

Through KMM Dubai, she has built a strong reputation in the events and promotions space, delivering large-scale, high-impact projects. The company’s portfolio includes globally recognised platforms such as The Amazing Race, Global Soccer Awards, Dubai World Cup, and Abu Dhabi Formula One. These collaborations reflect not only operational excellence but also an ability to navigate complex, high-visibility environments.

At the core of her work is mentorship. Kelly partners with entrepreneurs across different industries and growth stages, helping them align their vision with actionable strategies. Her approach is practical and results-driven, focused on turning ideas into structured, scalable businesses rather than short-term wins.

Beyond mentoring and events, she continues to expand her footprint as an investor. She is actively involved with Gym Clothing Co., a homegrown brand that combines performance, style, and accessibility. Her involvement reflects a strong belief in supporting emerging businesses that bring both innovation and value to the market.

Her growth mindset extends internationally as well. Kelly is currently leading the expansion of KMM Dubai into the UK, working with clients such as Caffe Monza while introducing business masterclasses designed to equip entrepreneurs with practical tools and insights.

Kelly’s journey is deeply personal. She has spoken about overcoming early life challenges that shaped her independence and resilience. These experiences continue to influence her perspective on success, reinforcing her belief that mindset plays a defining role in what individuals can achieve.

For her, success is not measured in milestones alone. It is reflected in the ability to create opportunities for others, to support growth, and to contribute to a larger ecosystem where businesses and individuals rise together.

Her philosophy remains clear. Stay focused, stay consistent, and build something that lasts.

LinkedIn | Website

4. Irina Lazar-Visu | Reimagining Professional Learning for a Changing World

“Professional training should not be a checkbox. It should be a catalyst for growth, clarity, and transformation.”

For Irina Lazar-Visu, professional education is not simply about acquiring new skills. It is about creating the conditions for people and businesses to evolve with confidence, relevance, and resilience. As Co-Founder and CEO of I-Grow, Irina is building a professional training ecosystem designed to make learning more accessible, practical, and aligned with the real needs of modern professionals and organisations.

Irina’s path to founding I-Grow is shaped by a career that bridges technical expertise, corporate leadership, and international governance. With an academic foundation in chemical engineering from the Polytechnic University in Bucharest, she later expanded her expertise through studies in banking, business administration, and executive leadership, earning qualifications from Spiru Haret University, the Romanian Banking Institute, and ESSEC Business School in France.

Over the course of 20 years in banking and financial services, including 15 years in risk management and controlling, Irina built a career at the intersection of governance, compliance, leadership, and operational excellence. From Credit Analyst and HR Manager to Director of Operational Risk and Permanent Controls, she held senior positions across Société Générale Group and Orange Bank – Orange Group in both Romania and France. Her work placed her at the center of decision-making, where she designed governance models, strengthened risk and compliance frameworks, and led multicultural teams across Europe, Russia and West Africa.

This experience shaped more than her expertise. It revealed a critical gap in how professional learning is often delivered.

Too often, training remains fragmented, generic, and disconnected from the realities professionals face in fast-changing business environments. Irina recognized that while organizations are investing in learning, many still struggle to access the right expertise, compare relevant programmes, and translate training into measurable impact. That insight became the foundation for I-Grow.

Launched in 2026, I-Grow was created with a clear mission: to make professional development more intelligent, more transparent, and more meaningful. I-Grow is built around two main pillars: a technical solution which is an aggregation, comparison and intermediation platform gathering and providing professional training offers existing on the French market and a human centered solution consisting in tailor-made training programs developed by freelance expert trainers.  As a professional training aggregation, comparison, and intermediation platform, I-Grow helps organizations and professionals identify the right learning opportunities, connect with trusted experts, and access training that is relevant, practical, and built for real business outcomes.

At its core, I-Grow is designed to simplify and strengthen the learning journey. By bringing together expert-led programs, curated learning pathways, and a more transparent approach to training discovery, the company aims to solve a growing challenge in professional education: not the lack of training, but the difficulty of finding the right training that creates lasting value.

For Irina, this is where the future of learning is headed.

She sees professional training evolving from static, one-size-fits-all instruction into a more dynamic and strategic business function. As industries transform under the pressure of digital acceleration, regulatory complexity, AI adoption, and global market shifts, learning must become more agile, personalized, and directly tied to business performance. The organizations that will lead in the future are those that treat learning not as an isolated HR initiative, but as a core lever of growth, adaptability, and competitive advantage.

This belief is central to I-Grow’s value proposition.

The company is built on the idea that effective training should do more than inform. It should enable better decisions, stronger leadership, sharper execution, and more resilient organizations. Through I-Grow, Irina and her co-founder Iouri Goloubtzoff aim to create a platform and training programs where learning is not reduced to content delivery but elevated into a strategic tool for transformation.

What distinguishes I-Grow is not only its model, but also the values it is built on.

Irina believes meaningful learning must be rooted in clarity, trust, and relevance. Training should be practical, not performative. It should empower people with tools they can apply, not just theories they can repeat. It should create space for reflection, challenge assumptions, and support long-term capability building rather than short-term knowledge transfer.

These same principles shape how I-Grow approaches partnerships and ways of working. The company promotes collaboration over hierarchy, curiosity over rigidity, and substance over surface. It is committed to building learning environments that are rigorous, human-centered, and grounded in real-world application. For Irina, professional growth happens best in spaces where expertise is shared generously, critical thinking is encouraged, and development is approached as a continuous process rather than a one-time intervention.

A recognized conference speaker and trusted advisor, Irina brings to this work a rare ability to translate complex regulatory and business realities into practical executive learning. Her strength lies not only in understanding systems, but in helping others navigate them with greater confidence and competence.

Through I-Grow, she is now channeling that experience into a larger mission: helping professionals learn better, helping organizations grow stronger, and helping education evolve into a more strategic force for business and human development.

For Irina, the goal is clear. Learning should not only keep pace with change. It should help shape what comes next.

LinkedIn | Website 

5. Ramzy Maher | Bringing Egypt’s Stories to the Modern World

Growing up surrounded by Egypt’s incredible history, Ramzy Maher has always known that the best way to see the country is through the stories it tells. Today, he uses his 50-year legacy at Emeco Travel and Gray Line Egypt to help the rest of the world discover those stories.

Ramzy acts as a bridge between Egypt’s ancient wonders and the modern digital world. He spends his days working with global travel platforms and tech companies to ensure that when someone dreams of visiting Egypt, they find high-quality, seamless, and unique experiences waiting for them.

He is especially most passionate about moving beyond standard sightseeing. Whether he is designing special trips for women or crafting deep tours for solo travelers, his goal is to make travel feel personal and premium. For Ramzy, it isn’t just about getting people to a destination; it’s about making sure Egypt stays connected, innovative, and unforgettable for every person who visits.

For Ramzy, this work is more than a job, it is a personal mission to share the authentic heart of his country. He keeps creating new opportunities for explorers by fusing his strong industry background with a modern, forward-thinking viewpoint, making sure that the enchantment of Bile and beyond is always just a few clicks away. 

LinkedIn | Website

6. Alf Hellström | Building Stronger Leaders, Teams, and Organizations

“Leadership is not tested when things are easy. It is revealed when pressure rises, the pace quickens, and people are asked to perform beyond the familiar.”

For Alf Hellström, leadership has never been a theoretical exercise. It has always been shaped in real environments, under real pressure, where behaviour matters more than intention and culture is defined by what people do, not what they say.

With a background as an officer, Alf developed an early understanding of leadership in its most practical form. He saw firsthand what happens when expectations rise, decisions carry weight, and teams are required to perform under pressure. That experience shaped his enduring interest in people, behaviour, and the conditions that allow teams to function at their best.

Today, as Founder of KEY Leadership & Transformation, Alf helps leaders, teams, and organisations strengthen leadership, build healthier cultures, and navigate transformation with greater clarity and trust.

His work is grounded in a simple belief: sustainable results are created by people, and people perform at their best when they experience meaning, clarity, and trust.

Rather than relying on fixed frameworks or one-size-fits-all models, Alf works from the understanding that every organisation is different. Every team carries its own dynamics. Every individual brings their own history, behaviours, and motivations. His role is to help organisations understand those patterns, work with them more effectively, and create the conditions for long-term growth.

His work is centred around three connected levels of transformation.

The Self focuses on helping leaders and employees better understand themselves, their behaviours, and the impact they have on others.

The Team focuses on building safe, high-performing teams with stronger trust, clearer expectations, and healthier ways of working together.

The Company focuses on shaping the structural and cultural behaviours where purpose, values, and direction become visible in everyday work.

Across industries ranging from manufacturing and energy to service-led and founder-driven businesses, Alf has worked with leaders through growth, change, and transformation. Whether the organisation is large or small, his core principle remains the same: lasting performance is built through human clarity, not organisational complexity.

What defines Alf’s work is not just his focus on leadership, but his focus on behaviour.

He believes transformation becomes meaningful only when it is lived in practice. Not in strategy decks. Not in leadership slogans. But in how people communicate, make decisions, handle pressure, and work together every day.

That is where culture is built. And that is where transformation succeeds or fails.

Alf is driven by helping people lead with greater self-awareness, helping teams perform with greater trust, and helping organisations turn intention into behaviour.

Outside of work, physical and mental training remain a central part of his life. He sees a clear connection between body, mind, and performance, and brings that same discipline into the way he approaches leadership, growth, and transformation.

LinkedIn | Website | Personal 

7. Peter Sundara Swamickannu | Leading with Purpose in Global Logistics

Peter Sundara Swamickannu is Medov Logistics’ Managing Director in Asia-Pacific. In simple words, he is in charge of ensuring that products arrive at their intended destination on time. 

Peter focuses on ensuring that these difficult journeys run smoothly and efficiently, whether he is working in the building and maintenance of massive cruise ships or delivering cargo over the ocean. He spends his days establishing teams capable of surviving whatever challenges the contemporary world throws at them, as well as looking for ways to expand the company with new technologies.

He has over 25 years of experience in the shipping and freight industry, so he has seen it all. He has led major advancements in the use of digital tools by organisations and managed massive budgets. The people and the idea are more significant than the ships or the numbers for Peter. He thinks that a company is only as strong as its employees, therefore he spends a lot of time teaching, mentoring, and helping the next generation of logistics experts find their footing. 

His experience has propelled him to the position of industry authority. He routinely speaks at large international conferences and shares what he has learned about staying adaptable in a fast changing world. He even helped create a leadership book to help others navigate difficult corporate environments.

When he is not managing global supply chains, he is most likely sharing his leadership and grit ideas, constantly looking for new ways to make the complex world of global trade a little more human and much more connected. 

LinkedIn 

8. Monsef Idrissi | Connecting the World of Sports Beyond the Field

“The future of sports will not be decided only on the field, but in how its ecosystems are connected, structured, and empowered.”

Monsef Idrissi believes that the future of sports happens where talent meets opportunity. Based in Madrid, Monsef is an entrepreneur working at the busy intersection of sports, law, and technology. As the founder of CarrerUp, he is building a digital home where athletes, clubs, agents, and fans can finally connect in one organized and high-performance space.

Monsef’s journey is inspired by one simple goal: making the sports world easier to navigate. While earning his Master’s in International Sports Law at the Real Madrid Graduate School, he saw firsthand how disorganized the industry could be. He decided to fix this by building a bridge that connects talent with global opportunities in a stable, professional way.

His work combines big dreams with real-world action. Whether he is improving the sports industry through CarrerUp or growing his coffee shop businesses, he stays focused on what is important. For Monsef, it is all about building companies that truly help people and create long-term success.

At the heart of what he does is the conviction that, while games are won on the pitch, the industry thrives through stronger links and greater administration. Monsef is committed to ensuring that the future generation of sports is more structured, transparent, and full of opportunities for all participants. 

LinkedIn | Website | Twitter | Instagram  

9. Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu | A Life Dedicated to Care, Knowledge, and Expression

For Dr. Sofica Bistriceanu, healthcare has never been limited to diagnosis or treatment. It has always been about understanding people. Her journey as a family physician reflects this belief. She focuses on the human side of medicine just as much as the clinical side.

She graduated from Iași University in Romania and later pursued family medicine research at Maastricht University. Over the years, she has built a strong presence in the medical field. She has delivered more than 137 international presentations and published over 60 articles in respected journals. Each contribution reflects her commitment to learning and sharing knowledge.

Dr. Bistriceanu is also closely involved in academic and professional circles. She is a member of the Academy for Professionalism in Healthcare. In addition, she serves on the Editorial Review Board for The Journal of Patient Experience and contributes to other medical publications. Her work as an Associate Editor with Primera Scientific Publication further highlights her role in shaping medical research.

One of her most distinctive contributions is her medical home model. Instead of limiting care to a clinic, she focuses on treating patients in their own environments. This allows her to observe factors that are often missed in traditional settings. She pays close attention to communication, family dynamics, and daily habits. According to her, these elements play a major role in overall health.

Beyond medicine, Dr. Bistriceanu has also built a name in the literary world. She has authored seven volumes of poetry. Her writing reflects a thoughtful and reflective mind, one that looks beyond science into emotion and experience.

Her work continues to influence both healthcare and research. She brings a clear message. To treat a person well, one must first understand the life they live.

LinkedIn

10. Dr. Karen Wendt | Guiding the Future of Sustainable Finance

Dr. Karen Wendt has spent her career at the point where finance meets long-term impact. She began in investment banking, working on acquisition strategies and project finance for leading institutions. Over time, her focus shifted. She moved toward sustainability, not as a trend, but as a necessary direction for the financial world.

Her work today reflects that shift. Dr. Wendt believes that real impact often comes from new ideas and new companies entering the market. To understand where finance is heading, she looks closely at areas like decentralized systems, tokenization, and new forms of asset ownership. For her, these are not distant concepts. They are already shaping how capital moves and how value is created.

With a PhD focused on impact investing and institutional clients, she combines research with real-world application. She also serves as President of SwissFinTechLadies, where she supports greater participation of women in finance and emerging financial systems. This is an area she speaks about often. She believes the future of finance must be inclusive, not limited.

As the CEO of Eccos Impact GmbH, Dr. Wendt works directly with investors and organizations. She helps them build strategies that align financial returns with measurable impact. Her work includes portfolio design, risk understanding, and the development of structured approaches to sustainable investment. She focuses on making these ideas practical and usable.

Beyond her advisory work, she is also an active voice in the field. She edits a Sustainable Finance science series, has written several books in both German and English, and regularly speaks at global forums. Her sessions are known for being clear and grounded, often linking complex ideas back to real decisions.

Dr. Karen Wendt continues to work with a clear sense of direction. She supports investors who want to do more than follow the market. She helps them understand where it is going and how to be part of that change.

Conclusion

The global leaders featured in this article are not just building successful ventures, they are pioneers of transformation in the current times. Their journey of dedication and relentless efforts is proof that with a strong vision, leaders can not only change industries, but they can also empower an entire generation.

title: Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini  | Transforming an Overlooked Industry Through Purpose and Leadership
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: In this exclusive interview, Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reflects on her journey from chemical engineering to entrepreneurship, and how she built Emakheni Group into a purpose-led facilities management company. From navigating a male-dominated industry to transforming an overlooked sector, she shares how resilience, leadership, and vision continue to shape her path. From Engineering to Purpose To understand the foundation of her journey, we asked, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“I was raised by my grandparents in the rural village of eMpendle, near Pietermaritzburg, while my mother pursued a teaching qualification. My upbringing instilled resilience, discipline, and a deep respect for education, which was further strengthened through my boarding school experience. I went on to build a career in chemical engineering, working with organisations such as Sappi, Sasol, and Unilever. Despite the stability and prestige, I found myself searching for deeper purpose. In male-dominated industrial environments, I often felt unseen, which led me to reflect on where I could create more meaningful impact. That search led me to the cleaning industry, where I identified both a challenge and an opportunity — a workforce that was undervalued, yet full of untapped potential. This insight became the foundation of Emakheni. I founded the business in 2013, and the early years were extremely challenging. I had to learn how to navigate a competitive, compliance-driven industry while also developing business acumen and leadership under pressure. With the support of mentors and a clear sense of purpose, I was able to build a strong foundation for the business.” Building Emakheni To understand how this vision translated into reality, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“Today, Emakheni Group is a 100% Black-owned, ISO 9001-certified facilities management company serving clients such as Unilever, SA Home Loans, and NCS Resins. We provide specialised industrial cleaning, including high-pressure, high-level, and chemical cleaning, alongside integrated hygiene, contract cleaning, pest control, and landscaping services. Backed by my technical background, we operate in environments where safety, compliance, and efficiency are critical. Our purpose, “Transforming Lives While Cleaning Excellently,” guides everything we do. We invest in training, promote from within, and integrate sustainability with social impact. Looking ahead, we are expanding beyond KwaZulu-Natal, with plans for national growth, AI-driven operational improvements, and the establishment of an NPO to further professionalise the sector.” Impact on the Ecosystem To explore the company’s broader role, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?” “We contribute by creating employment opportunities in the communities where we operate, which is especially important in the current economic climate. We also contribute economically by being a compliant business and paying our taxes responsibly.” Defining Success in the Industry As the conversation shifted to industry insights, we asked, “What three qualities are critical for success in your industry?” “Resilience is essential, because this industry requires you to persist despite challenges. An inquisitive mindset is also important, as you need a strong desire to learn, understand your market, and identify how to bring value. Leadership is equally critical, particularly the ability to manage yourself and lead teams to consistently deliver results.” Adapting to Technology To see how the business is evolving with changing times, we asked, “How has your organisation adapted to technological changes?” Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply – “We are currently upgrading a number of our systems to improve efficiency across multiple sites. We have also integrated Artificial Intelligence into key processes to enhance operational performance and enable smarter service delivery.” Advice for the Next Generation Finally, looking ahead, we asked, “What advice would you give to someone entering this industry?” “You need a clear vision and a strong sense of purpose. You must have the desire and hunger to learn, and to understand both your industry and the clients you want to serve. Most importantly, you need to embody a spirit of excellence and be willing to go above and beyond expectations.” Connect with Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini on LinkedIn. Learn more about Emakheni Group and its work through their official channels. content:
In this exclusive interview, Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reflects on her journey from chemical engineering to entrepreneurship, and how she built Emakheni Group into a purpose-led facilities management company. From navigating a male-dominated industry to transforming an overlooked sector, she shares how resilience, leadership, and vision continue to shape her path.

From Engineering to Purpose

To understand the foundation of her journey, we asked, “Could you share a bit about your early background, education, and the key experiences that shaped your career journey?”

Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“I was raised by my grandparents in the rural village of eMpendle, near Pietermaritzburg, while my mother pursued a teaching qualification. My upbringing instilled resilience, discipline, and a deep respect for education, which was further strengthened through my boarding school experience.

I went on to build a career in chemical engineering, working with organisations such as Sappi, Sasol, and Unilever. Despite the stability and prestige, I found myself searching for deeper purpose. In male-dominated industrial environments, I often felt unseen, which led me to reflect on where I could create more meaningful impact.

That search led me to the cleaning industry, where I identified both a challenge and an opportunity — a workforce that was undervalued, yet full of untapped potential. This insight became the foundation of Emakheni.

I founded the business in 2013, and the early years were extremely challenging. I had to learn how to navigate a competitive, compliance-driven industry while also developing business acumen and leadership under pressure. With the support of mentors and a clear sense of purpose, I was able to build a strong foundation for the business.”

Building Emakheni

To understand how this vision translated into reality, we asked, “How has your company evolved since its inception?”

Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply -“Today, Emakheni Group is a 100% Black-owned, ISO 9001-certified facilities management company serving clients such as Unilever, SA Home Loans, and NCS Resins.

We provide specialised industrial cleaning, including high-pressure, high-level, and chemical cleaning, alongside integrated hygiene, contract cleaning, pest control, and landscaping services. Backed by my technical background, we operate in environments where safety, compliance, and efficiency are critical.

Our purpose, “Transforming Lives While Cleaning Excellently,” guides everything we do. We invest in training, promote from within, and integrate sustainability with social impact.

Looking ahead, we are expanding beyond KwaZulu-Natal, with plans for national growth, AI-driven operational improvements, and the establishment of an NPO to further professionalise the sector.”

Impact on the Ecosystem

To explore the company’s broader role, we asked, “How does your business contribute to the ecosystem in your region?”

“We contribute by creating employment opportunities in the communities where we operate, which is especially important in the current economic climate.

We also contribute economically by being a compliant business and paying our taxes responsibly.”

Defining Success in the Industry

As the conversation shifted to industry insights, we asked, “What three qualities are critical for success in your industry?”

“Resilience is essential, because this industry requires you to persist despite challenges.

An inquisitive mindset is also important, as you need a strong desire to learn, understand your market, and identify how to bring value.

Leadership is equally critical, particularly the ability to manage yourself and lead teams to consistently deliver results.”

Adapting to Technology

To see how the business is evolving with changing times, we asked, “How has your organisation adapted to technological changes?”

Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini reply – “We are currently upgrading a number of our systems to improve efficiency across multiple sites. We have also integrated Artificial Intelligence into key processes to enhance operational performance and enable smarter service delivery.”

Advice for the Next Generation

Finally, looking ahead, we asked, “What advice would you give to someone entering this industry?”

“You need a clear vision and a strong sense of purpose.

You must have the desire and hunger to learn, and to understand both your industry and the clients you want to serve.

Most importantly, you need to embody a spirit of excellence and be willing to go above and beyond expectations.”

Connect with Portio Nkosithandile Dlamini on LinkedIn. Learn more about Emakheni Group and its work through their official channels.
