The top 10 global women in business are shaping the future of industries in ways that were once unimaginable. Across sectors, they are leading companies, driving innovation, and creating opportunities that impact economies worldwide. From technology and finance to sustainability and healthcare, their work is transforming the way we live and do business.

As we celebrate Women’s Day, we take a moment to recognize ten women who are making a lasting impact in their fields. Each of them has built something remarkable—whether it’s a groundbreaking startup, a successful corporation, or a movement that challenges the status quo. Their journeys are different, but they all share a common thread: perseverance, vision, and a commitment to change. The top 10 global women in business are not just thriving in their respective fields; they are redefining leadership on a global scale.

Top 10 Global Women in Business Impacting the Business Landscape in 2025

This women’s day, let’s talk about the women leaders who are shaping the business landscape in their own unique ways. Let’s get to the top 10 global women in business below:

1. Dr. Tina D. Lewis | The BottomLine Queen – A Global Visionary Business Leader

Dr. Tina, affectionately known as “The BottomLine Queen,” is a visionary business leader with a network and meetings with global icons, including Richard Branson, Oprah Winfrey and Donald Trump, the President of the United States of America. As the driving force behind The 6-Figure Incubator, she empowers entrepreneurs to achieve financial freedom through dynamic coaching and mentorship. Dr. Tina’s dynamic coaching and mentorship empowers ambitious minds to break barriers and achieve financial freedom. Her journey from earning the first six figures in record-breaking time to receiving awards for top recruiting and income producing is a living testament to her extraordinary business insight and leadership.

As an International Certified Global Speaker, Dr. Tina captivates audiences worldwide with her powerful, transformational messages. Moreover, as the creator and host of GLOBALcon, an international conference designed to inspire and equip women leaders from all walks of life, her voice resonates with entrepreneurs, executives, and visionaries alike, making her a sought-after keynote speaker.

Driven by her passion for empowering women, Dr. Tina founded Global Women Speakers, a professional organization dedicated to positioning women on global stages, enabling them to share their message, sell their products worldwide, and travel internationally. Her leadership has catapulted countless women into influential roles, helping them amplify their voices and achieve global recognition. But Dr. Tina’s commitment to impact and women empowerment doesn’t stop there. As a teenage mom turned entrepreneurial icon, she often declares, “Entrepreneurship saved my life.” Her journey fuels her mission to uplift the next generation, leading to the creation of the Her Business Matters Foundation, a non-profit organization empowering young girls aged 9 -19 in mastering S.E.L.F – STEM/AI, Entrepreneurship, Leadership, and Financial Literacy.

Her mantra, “If it’s to be, it’s up to me—but not just for me,” reflects her belief in leadership through service and global impact. For Dr. Tina, entrepreneurship is more than a career—it’s a transformative journey of empowerment, influence and simply just in her DNA. This philosophy has earned her international acclaim in countries, including the United Arab Emirates. Dr. Tina was awarded the Middle East Summit of Excellence Award, and honored as “Woman of the Year!”

According to Dr. Tina, Women’s Month is a celebration of strength, resilience, and progress. It honors the trailblazers who paved the way and inspires future generations to dream without limits. Dr. Tina reflects, “To me, it’s a powerful reminder that we are the architects of change, united by purpose, and destined to redefine unlimited possibilities.”

As a strategic philanthropist, Dr. Tina continues to give back, contributing to educational initiatives, entrepreneurial training, and community development programs worldwide. She believes in creating a legacy of leadership, influence, and impact that inspires generations. Dr. Tina D. Lewis is not just a business leader—she is a global phenomenon. Her story of resilience, vision, and empowerment continues to inspire entrepreneurs, leaders, and change-makers worldwide. She is proof that with determination and purpose, greatness is achievable.

LinkedIn | Instagram

2. Dina Tahboub | Results-Driven Wealth  Management Professional

Dina Tahboub, a passionate Wealth Manager, specializes in managing the wealth and investment portfolios of high-net-worth individuals. Her commitment to excellence in this field has shaped her unique journey from Jordan in the Middle East to Switzerland. With more than two decades of extensive experience in private banking and investment across top global banks, she has earned recognition as a “strong and significant asset in the wealth management industry.”

Dina has always been passionate about wealth management, finance, entrepreneurship, business, and women’s leadership and empowerment. She began her professional journey at global banks in Jordan and steadily climbed the ranks in this field with passion and enthusiasm. She reflects, “Success doesn’t come from what you do occasionally; it comes from what you do consistently.”

In 2018, Dina moved to Geneva to join the Global Wealth Management division at UBS Bank; the largest asset manager in Switzerland. During her time at UBS, she was certified as a Wealth Management Advisor by the SAQ Swiss Association for Quality. She was also nominated by UBS Bank’s management as a financial ambassador to the Middle East, a role in which she led and empowered women in finance.

As a UBS Ambassador, Dina played a crucial role in women’s empowerment in finance, helping women enhance their financial confidence and decision-making. She also worked on educating women in the Middle East on managing their assets, investing wisely, diversifying their portfolios, and optimizing asset allocation to meet their financial needs.

After a successful and fulfilling tenure at UBS Switzerland, Dina transitioned into entrepreneurship, joining Woodman Asset Management as an external asset manager. Woodman is recognized as one of the top 50 wealth managers in Switzerland. As a wealth management entrepreneur, Dina continues to work with determination and dedication toward her clients’ and company’s goals.

As a visionary leader in the industry, Dina promotes portfolio diversity, sustainable investing, and strategic wealth planning. She also encourages the younger generation to take charge of their financial decisions. Additionally, she is an active member of the Women-to-Women International organization, where she finds inspiration in the stories and experiences of other women.

Beyond her professional pursuits, Dina enjoys reading, traveling, and has a deep passion for the arts, music, and education. She firmly believes that every young girl should dream big, have confidence in their abilities, and commit to lifelong learning. “Independent women know their own worth and pave their own path,” she adds. Committed to supporting women’s and children’s issues globally, Dina continues to pave a path of positive change, inspiring women everywhere to pursue their dreams.

LinkedIn | Instagram

3. Katrina Michelle | Curated Food Experience For Every Event

Katrina Michelle, the Founder of K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering, has over 29 years of experience in the hospitality sector and has been a seasoned independent business owner for the last 14 years. Driven by the encouragement of her friends and starting her culinary journey in childhood, Katrina started K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering back in 2020.

As a culinary professional, Katrina has an impressive 4-year track record, in catering to esteemed clients, including Soulja Boy, Offset, and Cardi B, along with renowned entities like Disney Pixar, LA Department of Mental Health, Arizona State University, LACC, and more. Well-known for specializing in weddings, student groups, and corporate events, K Michelle’s presence extends to major events with multi-year attendance in events like Taste of Soul, Rolling Loud, Taste of Inglewood, 1500 or nothin Day, Hot Water Cornbread, Black on the Block, South LA Pride, Frat Games, and beyond.

With K Michelle’s Kitchen Catering, Katrina offers the best catering services by creating unique menus to accommodate every special event with sustainably sourced ingredients. From casual in-home brunches and office lunches to elegant weddings and glamorous events, her catering services are perfect for any occasion and are customized to fit the client’s budget. As a testament to Katrina’s diverse and successful catering portfolio, she has been featured on KTLA morning news and Voyages LA. With an enduring passion and commitment to excellence for her services, Katrina navigates and thrives in the diverse landscape of the industry. “Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement. Nothing can be done without hope and confidence.” — Kartina Michelle quotes Helen Keller

Women’s Day celebrates the strength, resilience, and ambition of urban women, empowering them to thrive in business and leadership.

Website | Instagram

4. Patricia M. Montesinos | Fostering Gender-Diversity And Role Of Women Entrepreneurs

Patricia M. Montesinos is a serial entrepreneur, business angel, startup coach, and jury member in the Swiss startup ecosystem. She is the Founder and President of FE+MALE Think Tank, a non-profit international association dedicated to gender diversity in entrepreneurship. Her work focuses on addressing the challenges women face in business and creating initiatives that drive meaningful change.

She holds a professional degree in Social and Cultural Integration, an Executive Master’s in Commercial and Marketing Management, and an MBA in Entrepreneurship. Patricia started her career as a Sales Director in a women’s footwear company before moving into roles as Commercial Director in the publishing sector in Madrid and Chief Administrator Officer in an architecture firm in Copenhagen.

With women entrepreneurs navigating various challenges such as funding and business growth, FE+MALE Think Tank conducts research to develop initiatives that support female entrepreneurs. “The numbers don’t lie—despite progress, female entrepreneurs still receive only 2% of total funds raised in Europe, with all-women teams securing just 0.4% of venture capital. Yet, data shows that diverse teams drive higher returns and greater innovation. Investors who prioritize gender diversity are unlocking untapped potential and outperforming the market,” Patricia states.

Through initiatives like the Beat Funding Bias Initiative, supported by the Bern Economic Development Agency, Gebert Rüf Foundation, and Ernst Göhner Foundation, FE+MALE Think Tank equips investors and entrepreneurs with resources to close the gender funding gap. Patricia works to turn research into practical solutions that foster an environment where diversity is recognized and valued.

While FE+MALE Think Tank is her primary focus, Patricia is also the Founder of Women Change-makers, an initiative that provides support for women in entrepreneurship. Though less active, it remains part of her broader mission to create opportunities for women in business.

She is also committed to supporting young women through education, with 5% of Women Change-makers’ net income donated to initiatives that encourage entrepreneurship and career development.

LinkedIn | Website

5. Amy Koford | Transforming Lives Through Hypnosis

Amy Koford, The Happy Hypnotist, is a highly acclaimed clinical hypnotist, author, speaker, and performer who excels in empowering individuals to overcome depression and anxiety, heal from past traumas, conquer their fears, and unlock their fullest potential. She is also the Founder and a Certified Hypnotherapist at Results Hypnotherapy.

With accreditation from leading trainers and organizations worldwide, Amy has enriched her expertise by attending international hypnosis conferences and learning from the foremost hypnotists in the field. Her impactful work has garnered attention across various media platforms, including television shows, publications, and podcasts. Her book about how to rise to unnecessary fear so that it is no longer holding you back and causing you suffering is coming out in a few months.

Amy’s commitment to excellence has taken her around the globe to attend the top hypnosis conferences, receiving training from top experts in this field. Specializing in happiness and peace, Amy helps people with various techniques that are effective in resolving and letting go of the past and changing their center to become positive, confident, empowered individuals who know their amazing abilities to live their best lives.

As a top-rated specialist in hypnosis techniques, public speaker, author, and performer of comedy hypnosis shows, she is even a coach with guaranteed results. Amy reflects, “I am accredited by the leading trainers and organizations in the world today. Always professional, I am an exact fit for corporate-friendly presentations, events, training, and coaching!”

LinkedIn | Website

6. Dr. Gabi Kratochwil | Connecting People And Bridging Cultures

Dr. Gabi Kratochwil, Cultural Diversity Management Expert, Speaker, Networker, CEO of CrossCultures and Chairwoman of the German-Arab Women Business Leaders, brings over 25 years of experience in connecting people and empowering women globally. Dr. Kratochwil studied Middle Eastern Studies, Politics, and Public Law at the University of Bonn and at the American University in Cairo, Egypt, forming the base of her career path.

As a passionate high-profile change maker and multi-award winning female leader, she represents Germany at many international conferences and round tables as a keynote speaker, moderator, and facilitator and has been initiating and chairing many high-ranking events bringing together global excellence, including the German-Arab Women Business Leaders Summit (GAWBL-Summit), in 2018 in Munich, Germany.

Dr. Kratochwil is a renowned name in Cultural Diversity Management counting a large number of the world’s leading international enterprises and organizations on the client list. With her company CrossCultures, she provides workshops & events around the world supporting her customers to work better globally.

She mentions, “I firmly believe in the power of connecting people globally and growing together through exchange, networking, and partnerships. Let us be open to new ideas, be bold, and learn from each other. Because only together can we pave the way forward for future generations.”

Furthermore, Dr. Kratochwil is teaching at the University of Freiburg, mentors young female entrepreneurs and coaches individuals on career development, personal goal setting, and resilience.

Her intercultural business handbook on the Arab World has been listed as number 5 of the top management books by The Financial Times, her book on successful Arab women leaders was featured in FORBES.

As a member of the Board of Directors of the Arab-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Ghorfa) since 2006, a member of the German Middle East Studies Association for Contemporary Research and Documentation (DAVO) and the Society for Intercultural Training and Research (SIETAR), she is strongly committed to contribute.

Dr. Kratochwil’s exceptional support and work have earned her several recognitions, including the Global Diversity Leadership Award, in 2017, and the World Women Leadership Achievement Award, in 2015.

LinkedIn | Website

7. Christina Ioannou | Driving PR And Brand Positioning For Growth

A Senior PR strategist with over a decade of experience in planning, leading, executing, and evaluating international communications and PR campaigns with great success, Christina Ioannou has a demonstrated history of delivering large and complex international PR campaigns. Being passionate about PR and communications, she has a proven track record in running and implementing communication strategies focusing on storytelling, branding, and profile raising. Currently, as the Director & Campaign Lead at CCIcomms, Christina looks after the communication services, strategic partnerships, and networking opportunities for the organization.

With a keen eye for detail and a solution-oriented approach, Christina follows a strong work ethic and stays updated with the latest developments in the PR sector, ensuring efficient solutions for clients. Over her career path, she has achieved more than 8K pieces of impactful press coverage for her clients and has helped numerous leaders and founders become authorities in their fields and get positioned in the press.

Christina is also a Member of the Board of Directors at Union Dance, advising on communication strategy and implementation, and a contributor to Entrepreneur Magazine. As a Goldsmiths University Graduate, she has also served as a student mentor for the ICCE department students, supporting them with their professional journey.

Regarding her upcoming plans, Christina reflects, “Supporting startups has been my focus lately, as I am keen to support young teams and their innovative solutions. The technology and AI space is fascinating for me and I look forward to seeing more startups flourish in Switzerland and beyond!” As a seasoned leader, Christina’s dedication to staying at the forefront of this industry and her commitment to excellence make her a perfect match for organizations seeking expert guidance on PR and communication strategies.

LinkedIn | CCIcomms | Instagram

8. Tlhonepo Modisane | A Seasoned Executive And Coach

Tlhonepo Modisane is a Senior HR Executive, currently a People & Communications Business Partner at KONE for the Africa Region where she is responsible for the development and implementation of Human Capital strategies in South Africa, Morocco, Tunisia, Kenya, and Uganda countries. She serves as an Executive Director for KONE South Africa and as the Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Lead for the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa Region. KONE is an innovative leader in the elevator and escalator industry with a footprint in more than 60 countries worldwide.

Tlhonepo holds an Honours Degree in Industrial & Organisational Psychology amongst other accolades. She transitioned from a finance background and moved into the Human Resources field and has spent the past 11 years in Senior HR roles in multiple organizations within the Elevator/Escalators, Mining Engineering, Manufacturing, and ICT industries within multinational organizations such as KONE and Metso as well as local South African private organizations.

Committed and passionate about driving positive organizational cultures, Tlhonepo empowers individuals within organizations, particularly in taking accountability, and ownership for their personal development and growth by creating and leveraging opportunities for self-improvement and growth. As a public speaker and coach, her passion for the empowerment of others is also seen in her involvement in non-profit organizations where she imparts her knowledge, skills, and time by coaching and empowering others through her involvement as a Board member and in other capacities in organizations that encompass servant leadership principles and focus on the upliftment of others.

Being a coach, Tlhonepo helps individuals and businesses develop strategies and structures for improvement, change and goal attainment. She assists individuals to set goals and aim to live the lives that they desire and assists businesses in strategic transformation. For those struggling to find their purpose in life, Tlhonepo is a beacon of hope, offering her guidance and assisting them to find their own solutions.

LinkedIn | Website

9. Deniz Erkuş | Conscious Leadership For Regenerative Living

Deniz Erkuş is an impact investing catalyst and change maker for holistic sustainability. She is the Managing Partner and Founder of Sidemi Business Consulting. As a former corporate warrior with over 28 years of solid international experience, she aims to build powerful bridges connecting finance and investment with a growth mindset, regeneration, and action. Regarding regeneration, Deniz shares, “Make a daily habit of doing one valuable action a day to positively impact the planet and people’s lives.”

With a vision to empower purpose-driven businesses to generate a net positive impact, Deniz is raising awareness among investors and stakeholders for a green circular economy that creates a carbon-neutral world. She believes in the principle of the Quadruple Bottom line and regenerative framework, for sustainable prosperity by involving future generations in addition to people, planet, and profits. Deniz is a C-level executive at HealthSum Holding AS, a pioneering Norwegian firm, with a vision to revolutionize the healthcare industry through innovative solutions and powerful partnerships.

Her vision is to mobilize and channel private and public capital towards impact investing while supporting innovation with disruptive business models and aims to support such businesses as an Impact Advisor/Board member with collaboration and partnerships, applying regenerative practices. To do this, Deniz organizes training sessions, workshops, and retreats to merge consciousness and regeneration with the investment and finance community, as the first step, to moving forward with collaboration, partnerships, and action-taking.

As an international speaker and a UNDP international consultant, she contributed and spoke at various events in Türkiye, Luxembourg, Switzerland (including the World Economic Forum in Davos), Azerbaijan, Tanzania, Uganda, the UAE, and Brazil, regarding climate financing, circular economy, AI and impact, Impact Measurement and Management, SDG-anchored investing, Innovative Finance, Conscious Leadership for Regenerative Living and Generating Change. As a passionate presenter, Deniz’s teaching sessions and workshops include sustainable and innovative finance to channel capital to global impact, ESG framework, and conscious leadership for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), inspiring her audience to generate change and propel transformation forward.

LinkedIn

10. Dr. Marika Crohns: Transforming Healthcare Through Leadership and Innovation

With over three decades in healthcare, Dr. Marika Crohns, MD, PhD, has built a career defined by leadership, expertise, and a drive for meaningful change. Her impact goes beyond medical practice, as she has played a key role in shaping healthcare policies and improving patient outcomes through strategic innovation.

Throughout her career, Dr. Crohns has focused on identifying inefficiencies in healthcare systems and implementing solutions that enhance both patient care and operational effectiveness. She has been instrumental in integrating emerging technologies like AI and telemedicine to make healthcare more accessible and efficient.

Beyond her professional achievements, Dr. Crohns is deeply committed to mentorship. She actively supports and guides future healthcare leaders, helping them develop the skills and confidence needed to navigate an evolving industry. Her approach ensures that innovation and leadership continue to thrive in the next generation of professionals.

Dr. Crohns also places strong emphasis on patient-centered care. She believes that while healthcare systems advance, they must always keep the patient experience at the core. Her dedication to balancing technological progress with compassionate care has earned her a reputation as a leader who drives meaningful, lasting improvements in the field.

LinkedIn

Conclusion

The women featured in this list represent just a fraction of the talent and leadership driving the business world forward. Their success is not just about personal achievement; it’s about paving the way for others and creating spaces where more women can thrive. The top 10 global women in business serve as an inspiration, demonstrating that success is not limited by background or industry.

As we move into 2025, their influence will continue to grow, inspiring the next generation of leaders to take bold steps and redefine what is possible. This Women’s Day, we celebrate their work, their impact, and the future they are helping to build.

As the founder of SYNNEVE GOODE ATELIER, she fuses avant-garde creativity with strategic vision, proving that innovation is not just about newness – but depth, feeling, and impact.

With two decades in Paris and the global luxury sphere, Synneve has worked with Chanel, Agent Provocateur, LVMH executives and leading trend forecasting bureaus. She is the co-founder of the renowned tailored clothing brand, Husbands Paris, pioneering new ways of thinking and creating. Now, through Sensorial Dressing®, she is introducing a radical shift – one that reimagines how we engage with clothing, brand experiences, and innovation itself.

“Sensorial Dressing® is not just an evolution in fashion—it’s an invitation to go deeper, to explore new dimensions within ourselves and our surroundings. It is about redefining our boundaries and how we experience creativity and innovation. The future belongs to those who dare to feel, think, and create differently. This is just the beginning.”

More than fashion, Sensorial Dressing® is a tool for transformation – a strategic approach that pushes boundaries, heightens emotional connection, and unlocks new innovation potential. Through immersive experiences, workshops, and made-to-order designs, Synneve enables both individuals and companies to engage the senses, break away from conventional models, and create something entirely new.

Associated with reputed universities in the UAE over these years in key leadership positions, Dr. Mariam has been actively working with aspiring students looking to pursue higher education. Currently, as the CEO and Founder of MS Education Consultants, she continues to lead with passion and purpose, making an indelible impact on students and communities globally.

Driven by her passion for quality education, Dr. Mariam’s career path commenced with the establishment of a nursery school, eventually making a transformative shift into the higher education sector which marked a pivotal moment in her professional journey. She has played a key role in establishing some of the most reputed foreign University Branch campuses in UAE such as the University of New Brunswick in Dubai Knowledge Village, which was the first of her pioneering efforts to encourage foreign Universities to set up their campuses in Dubai.

Dr. Mariam also attends numerous conferences as a keynote speaker and has media appearances, sharing her vision for world-class educational facilities. Recognizing her untiring efforts to establish Dubai as a leading educational hub and her position as a leading woman entrepreneur, Dr. Mariam has been entitled to several titles and awards, including the Global Excellence in Education Award, the GCC Woman Leadership Award, and the Educator of the Year 2023.

Apart from her professional endeavors, Dr. Mariam strongly advocates for women’s empowerment and entrepreneurship through the Global Women Entrepreneurs Group in Dubai, where she promotes collaboration in Education and Professional Development. Her mission includes supporting and empowering women in the mainstream economy through skill development, entrepreneurial projects, and improving young women’s access to mentors and new venture incubators. Furthermore, with MS Education Consultants, she has created job opportunities for graduates and developed programs for refugee students, reflecting her deep compassion and commitment to community service.

Dr. Mariam Shaikh’s journey from a small nursery school to becoming a global educational leader reflects her vision, resilience, and dedication to education and women empowerment. Her work continues to inspire, making her a beacon of hope and a role model for aspiring educators and entrepreneurs worldwide.

title: The peaceful Massachusetts Communities that Fueled the Revolution
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: On April 19, 2025, Lexington, Concord, and two other towns north-west of Boston will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the frigid spring day in 1775 when Massachusetts militias clashed with British forces in a battle that set the United States on the path to independence. The disastrous die was cast when Paul Revere rode on horseback in the little farming village of Lexington to warn leaders that British soldiers were marching from Boston to take colonial military supplies kept in Concord, just a few miles away. When the British came, they discovered a small band of local militiamen, Minutemen, waiting in the morning light. Nobody knows who fired the first shot, but eight Minutemen and one British soldier were killed by the end of the fight. The British marched on to Concord, where they encountered many Minutemen near the North Bridge. After intense battle and substantial losses on both sides, the British withdrew. Returning to Boston, British troops faced a running conflict as the towns of Lincoln, Lexington, and Menotomy (now Arlington) organized militias to resist. Every year on April 19, these little Massachusetts communities celebrate with historical reenactments and other special events. However, with additional celebrations planned in honour of the 250th anniversary, organizers expect this year’s festivities will lure more travellers than ever before to what many call “the birthplace of American liberty. title: North Korea is Off-Limits to US Tourists. In Order to Visit There, this American Paid six Figures for a Second Passport
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The gloomy days of COVID-19 seem like a faraway past to the majority of people on the planet. But not in North Korea, said Justin Martell, who recently made history as the first American to enter the closed country since the pandemic began more than five years ago. Due to persistent concerns about virus transmission, major tourist destinations, such as local markets, are still off-limits, and strict health precautions, including mask-wearing and temperature checks, are still standard. According to Martell, pandemic paranoia is still pervasive in North Korea, officially known as the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK). He even came across strange hypotheses on the genesis of the virus. “There is a rumour that COVID-19 entered the country through a balloon that was sent from South Korea,” said Martell, a filmmaker from Connecticut who created Pioneer Media, a company that specialises in capturing unusual and challenging-to-reach places. Last week, he was a member of a small group of tour operators who travelled to North Korea to establish plans for future travel. They returned to China on Monday via the icy Tumen River Bridge after five days in North Korea, where they laid the foundation for the limited resumption of Western travel. title: Sharjah is Named Guest of Honour at the Book Fair in Rabat
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Sharjah: The Kingdom of Morocco has designated the emirate as the official Guest of Honour at the 30th Rabat International Book Fair (RIBF) in honour of His Highness Dr. Sheikh Sultan Bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah’s cultural project, as well as Sharjah’s standing as a global knowledge capital. The Moroccan Ministry of Youth, Culture, and Communication is organising RIBF 2025, which will be held at the renowned OLM Souissi from April 17 to April 27. Khoula Al Mujaini, Director of Events and Marketing at the Sharjah Book Authority (SBA), and Latifa Moftaqir, General Coordinator of RIBF and Director of the Moroccan Archives Foundation, signed the agreement during the ceremony where the news was made. Enhancing Arab cultural interchange and strengthening relationships between intellectuals and literary luminaries from the United Arab Emirates and Morocco are two important goals of this statement. The program will celebrate the richness of Emirati heritage and the cultural values it shares with Morocco, promoting greater understanding and cooperation. Sharjah, as the Guest of Honour, will also present a varied cultural agenda that highlights the UAE’s historical and contemporary literary and artistic accomplishments. title: Dubai Presents an Airborne Taxi Prototype
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: A prototype of the airborne taxi created by Joby Aviation has been unveiled at the Museum of the Future in collaboration with Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA). The prototype, which is on display on the museum’s “Tomorrow, Today floor,” demonstrates Dubai’s dedication to the Dubai Self-Driving Strategy and its progressive vision for intelligent, sustainable mobility. One of Dubai’s main initiatives to revolutionise transport is the aerial taxi program, which aims to have 25% of trips driven by self-driving cars by 2030. The project, which uses cutting-edge electric technology, intends to lower carbon emissions and promote global sustainability goals. We are honoured to present the aerial taxi model at the Museum of the Future, which highlights Dubai’s ambition and forward-thinking approach to redefining mobility in this vibrant city,” stated Khaled Al Awadhi, Director of Transportation Systems at RTA’s Public Transport Agency. Dubai will be the first city in the world to introduce the aerial taxi project, which is expected to start in the first quarter of 2026 and signal the start of a revolutionary age in urban mobility. In addition to adhering to the strictest safety and security regulations to guarantee the welfare of its passengers, the aerial taxi is notable for its vertical takeoff and landing capabilities. title: Dubai Intends to Provide fire Safety Training to one Billion People Worldwide
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The “1 Billion Readiness” campaign was introduced by the Dubai Civil Defence under the sponsorship and in the presence of Sheikh Mansoor Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairman of Dubai’s Supreme Committee of Crisis and Disaster Management. The ground-breaking global effort, the biggest of its kind in safety and fire hazard avoidance, is to educate and train 1 billion individuals globally on prevention methods between 2025 and 2027. This innovative endeavour, spearheaded by the United Arab Emirates, is a global partnership of 34 nations and 18 significant firefighting organisations. It emphasises how the UAE is in the forefront of improving safety and security measures globally. Through extensive awareness campaigns, this initiative will increase global awareness about fire prevention and the significance of safety procedures,” said Lieutenant General Expert Rashid Thani Al Matrooshi. Specialised digital platforms that are available globally in several languages will complement these efforts. After completing the course, participants will also receive official electronic certificates from the Dubai Civil Defence Readiness Program and the Global Wildfire Monitoring Centre. Al Matrooshi added that in order to reach as many people as possible, the project would run massive awareness efforts at the local level that will target all facets of society, including people, government agencies, the commercial sector, and educational institutions. title: Over 120 People are Killed by a Powerful Earthquake in Tibet
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: At least 126 people were killed and hundreds of dwellings were flattened Tuesday when a powerful earthquake slammed the foothills of the Himalayas close to one of Tibet’s holiest cities, according to Chinese officials. The epicentre of the magnitude 6.8 earthquake was located roughly 80 kilometers (50 miles) north of the highest mountain in the world, Mount Everest. Buildings in neighboring Bhutan, India, and Nepal were also shaken by the tremors. 800,000 people live in the Shigatse district of Tibet, which was affected. Shigatse City, the traditional residence of the Panchen Lama, one of the most significant personalities in Tibetan Buddhism, serves as the administrative centre for the area. According to footage supplied by Tibet Fire and Rescue, several homes in Shigatse city were reduced to rubble. Early December saw a sharp increase in norovirus cases, sometimes known as the stomach flu, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). According to the CDC, more than twice as many cases reported between 2021 and 2024 occurred during the week of December 5. According to a news statement from the Minnesota Department of Health, the state saw twice as many instances of stomach flu in December than usual.

Gastroenteritis is brought on by the highly contagious norovirus, which inflames the stomach and intestines. Often called the “stomach flu,” it has nothing to do with influenza. A major source of foodborne illness worldwide, norovirus can afflict individuals of all ages. This page discusses norovirus causes, symptoms, and prevention measures.

Causes

Norovirus spreads primarily through:

  • Food or water contamination: Eating or drinking anything that has been tainted by the virus.
  • Person-to-person contact: Shaking hands or sharing utensils with an infected person are examples of close contact.
  • Contaminated surfaces: Contacting the mouth, nose, or eyes after coming into contact with surfaces or objects that have been contaminated with the virus.
  • Particles inhaled by an infected person’s vomit or faeces are known as aerosolized particles.

Signs

Symptoms typically appear 12–48 hours after exposure and include:

  • Nausea
  • Vomiting
  • Diarrhoea
  • Stomach cramps
  • Fever or chills
  • Muscle aches
  • Fatigue

Dehydration (dry mouth, dizziness, reduced urination)These symptoms typically last one to three days, but in small children, the elderly, or those with compromised immune systems, they may be more severe.

title: Taxable Persons are Advised by the FTA to Follow the Deadlines
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: The Federal Tax Authority (FTA) encourages residents who hold licenses issued in October or November, regardless of the year of issuance, to swiftly submit their application for corporate tax registration by November 30, 2024. For the purposes of Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 on the Taxation of Corporations and Businesses and its amendments, which went into effect on March 1, 2024, the FTA advised Taxable Persons in a press release today to follow the deadlines outlined in FTA Decision No. 3 of 2024 on the Timeline specified for Registration of Taxable Persons for Corporate Tax. The FTA Decision specifies the due dates for submitting corporate tax registration applications for each type of taxable persons liable to corporate tax. Additionally, the FTA clarified that the FTA Decision applies to both resident and non-resident natural persons and juristic persons. It stated that resident persons who were incorporated, otherwise established, or recognised prior to March 1, 2024, must file their corporate tax registration application using the month in which their licence was issued, regardless of the year of issuance. The license with the earliest issuing date determines the deadline for Taxable Persons with multiple licenses as of March 1, 2024. The registration deadline is still determined by the month the licence was issued, even if a Taxable Person has an expired licence as of March 1, 2024. title: In Severe Weather, a Giant Moon Facsimile on a Historic River in the UK Deflates
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Storm Ashley’s “extreme” gusts caused a big moon facsimile that was placed on a historic river in a Somerset town to deflate. According to Bridgwater Town Council, Bristol-based artist Luke Jerram’s “Fallen Moon” installation has “captivated” and attracted over 10,000 visitors to Bridgwater Docks since its Tuesday unveiling. However, on Sunday, the council bemoaned that the installation might have ended prematurely after having “clearly brought joy and astonishment to so many” in the days since it opened. In a statement, the council said: “We regret to notify the public that due to an unexpected and tough electrical and technical breakdown, which is now made worse by the strong weather, especially winds, Luke Jerram’s ‘Fallen Moon’ exhibit. We must be realistic about the difficulties of this installation, and even if we will look at various options over the course of the next 48 hours, it [may be that] the project is finished in its current form. As further information becomes available, it will be shared. The illuminated sculpture, a “technically challenging” duplicate that is 350,000 times smaller than the actual moon and has a diameter of 10 meters, was made using NASA data. The lunar landscape is represented by 3.5 km per centimetre. title: The Discovery of microRNA Wins the Nobel Prize in Medicine
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: They found that microRNA is a component of messenger RNA, the backbone of DNA that houses the genomic code of all living things, including humans and other larger animals as well as fruit flies. Through their research, Ambros and Rukvun demonstrated how microRNA controls the process of cell differentiation in multicellular organisms, leading to the same genome code being encoded in the chromosomes and becoming the intestinal, muscle, nerve, and many other cells that make up a large organism like a human. Cancer cells and other defective components in the human body and other creatures may also result if the microRNA misdirects this act of cell differentiation. Our chromosomes contain information that can be compared to an instruction manual for every cell in our body. Since all cells have the same chromosomes, every cell has identical genes and precisely the same set of instructions. However, the properties of various cell types—such as muscle and nerve cells—vary greatly. What causes these variations? Gene regulation provides the solution by enabling each cell to choose only the pertinent instructions. This guarantees that only the appropriate genes are active in each cell type. As the Global Flavorist and Creative Center Leader at Etadar by Deiman, Thuemme’s innovative approach is revolutionizing the flavor industry, particularly through his groundbreaking work on “Native Flavors.” This unique flavor class celebrates the traditional pre-Hispanic Mexican ingredients and customs that have faded from contemporary cuisine. By resurrecting these ancient flavors, Thuemme ensures that the world can once again taste the essence of Mexico’s past.

Since joining Deiman in 2014 after a distinguished tenure with international flavor houses, Thuemme has been instrumental in transforming Deiman into a global leader in flavor innovation. His expertise, honed over the creation of more than 50,000 flavors, has positioned the company as a competitive force in the international market. Thuemme’s dedication to flavor research is unparalleled; he is currently developing a Flavorists School in Mexico to train future professionals, passing on his extensive knowledge and passion for the craft.

One of Thuemme’s most remarkable contributions is the creation of flavors that embody the spirit of Mexican independence, celebrated each September. Among his notable creations are the Tres Leches flavor, a tequila with citrus undertones enhanced by exotic fruits like cactus and nanches, and a tepache flavor that brings a traditional fermented pineapple beverage to the global stage. He has also innovated by reclaiming the residues of vanilla beans through reactions with amino acids, reviving the authentic aroma of vanilla and creating derivative flavors that pay homage to Mexico’s rich culinary history.

title: India and the US are Expected to Finalise a deal on Vital Minerals
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: According to two Indian government officials, India and the US are expected to sign a preliminary agreement for cooperation on vital minerals this week as they work to strengthen commercial relations in spite of diplomatic setbacks. During Indian Trade Minister Piyush Goyal’s visit to Washington, they are anticipated to sign an agreement to collaborate and partner in the field of vital minerals, according to the sources. Weeks before the White House begins preparing for a leadership transition following the presidential election later this year, one of the sources states that Goyal is expected to visit the US this week to discuss strategies for strengthening overall bilateral trade ties. Prior to this month, President Joe Biden and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a one-on-one meeting in Delaware as part of the Quad grouping, which also consists of the leaders of Australia and Japan. According to the first official, the first agreement on vital minerals will foster cooperation between Indian and American companies operating in the industry by assisting in developing supply chains and exchanging technical know-how. The US embassy and the federal trade ministry of India did not immediately respond to Reuters’ email seeking comment. title: The President of the UAE Commands $100 Million in Immediate Aid for Lebanon
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: An immediate $100 million aid package for the people of Lebanon has been ordered by UAE President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan. This gesture demonstrates the UAE’s steadfast commitment to helping the Lebanese people and is a part of the country’s ongoing efforts to support Lebanon through its current challenges. The necessity for an immediate ceasefire and de-escalation along Lebanon’s southern borders, as well as for protecting people, showing caution, and stopping the violence from spreading farther in the region, was highlighted today by the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). In a statement, GCC Secretary-General Jassim Mohammed Al-Budaiwi reiterated the GCC’s unwavering support for Lebanon’s sovereignty, security, and stability as well as its continuous solidarity with the Lebanese people. He also emphasised the GCC States’ ministerial declaration, which demanded that UN Security Council Resolution 1701 be fully implemented. In line with pertinent Security Council resolutions and the Taif Agreement, the resolution highlights the necessity for Israel to respect Lebanon’s borders and for the Lebanese government to exercise jurisdiction over all of its territory in order for Lebanon to maintain complete sovereignty over its regions. title: Selling Sand to an Arab: Dubai’s Genius in Turning the Impossible into the Inevitable
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Imagine selling snow to an Eskimo. Now, imagine selling sand to an Arab. In a city where sand surrounds every corner, Dubai has turned even this seemingly limitless resource into a valuable commodity. Here, all the sand belongs to the government, and you can’t touch a grain of it without their consent. Just like swans belong to the Queen of England and pandas are the sole property of the Chinese government, Dubai’s sand is not free for the taking. Not all sand is created equal in this dazzling desert metropolis. There are two distinct types of sand in Dubai, and each is treated very differently. First, there’s the ubiquitous desert sand—rough, gritty, and golden. This sand is used for construction projects, either dumped after excavation or refilled to level out the land. Even this common desert sand is heavily regulated. You can’t move or use it without paying the government, making it a clear example of “selling sand to an Arab.” Every truckload is accounted for, and every movement of sand comes with a price tag. Image Credit Then, there’s the real treasure—Dubai’s white beach sand. Soft, luxurious, and as valuable as gold, this premium sand lines the shores of the city’s world-famous beaches and high-end resorts. This isn’t just any sand; it’s a symbol of the city’s opulence and exclusivity. Reserved for the most luxurious properties, Dubai’s white sand is treated like a rare treasure, reinforcing the city’s image as a place where even the simplest things are elevated to extraordinary heights. Dubai’s ability to transform sand into a valuable resource mirrors a global trend where seemingly common commodities are turned into luxurious, highly regulated assets. Consider Venice, a city built on water, yet fresh water is a rare commodity. The Venetians rely on water piped in from the mainland, despite being surrounded by the very element they need. In a city where water is everywhere, they’ve managed to “sell water to Venetians,” proving that scarcity can be created where none seems to exist. Image Credit In Switzerland, the country’s famed mountain air has been transformed into a luxury product. Visitors from polluted cities can purchase bottled Swiss air to take home, a literal example of “selling air to the world.” The Swiss have mastered the art of turning their natural environment into a valuable commodity, much like Dubai has with its sand. Image Credit The Dutch have done something similar with tulips, flowers that are as common in the Netherlands as sand is in Dubai. Yet, the Netherlands has managed to create an entire economy around these vibrant blooms, with tourists and locals alike paying premium prices for tulips. It’s another case of turning something abundant into a luxury—“selling tulips to the Dutch” in a land full of flowers. Image Credit Canada’s maple syrup industry operates in much the same way. Despite producing 70% of the world’s supply, the syrup is tightly controlled and sold at high prices, even to Canadians themselves. The government ensures that the syrup, much like Dubai’s sand, is a valuable commodity by managing its production and pricing. It’s a sweet example of “selling syrup to Canadians,” even in a land where maple trees are everywhere. Image Credit In Colombia, some of the world’s best coffee beans are grown, but most of the premium product is exported to other countries. Locals often drink lower-grade coffee, as the finest beans are reserved for international markets. It’s a perfect example of “selling coffee to Colombians,” where the very people who grow the product don’t always get to enjoy the best of it. Image Credit Japan takes the concept even further by turning something as simple as a watermelon into a luxury item. Square watermelons, meticulously grown and sold for hundreds of dollars, are often given as gifts, proving that even the most ordinary things can be transformed into high-end commodities. In Japan, they’ve managed to “sell watermelons to the Japanese” by reimagining an everyday fruit as a status symbol. Image Credit France’s Brittany region is home to another example of turning the ordinary into the extraordinary. Salt harvested from the Atlantic coast, known as “white gold,” is sold at premium prices around the world, despite being as abundant as the sea itself. This artisanal salt has been elevated to a luxury good, showing that even the simplest resources can be turned into treasures with the right narrative. Image Credit In Greece, olive oil, a staple of the Mediterranean diet, has become a prized export. The finest olive oil is often reserved for international markets, while locals consume lower-grade versions. It’s yet another example of “selling olive oil to Greeks,” where a common resource is transformed into a valuable product for those who can afford it. In every one of these examples, from Venice’s water to Canada’s syrup, the story is the same: abundant resources turned into precious commodities. And Dubai, with its mastery of sand, leads the way. By transforming both desert and beach sand into valuable resources, the city has proven that even the most ordinary materials can be reimagined into something extraordinary. Whether it’s “selling sand to an Arab” or creating value out of air, the future belongs to those who can turn the ordinary into the extraordinary. And in Dubai, even sand—whether it’s the rough desert variety or the silky white beach sand—is priceless. About the Author Hamzah Abu Zannad is an industry veteran and the co-founder and managing director of Axiom Prime Real Estate Development. With over two decades of experience in the dynamic Dubai real estate market, Hamzah has played a pivotal role in introducing forward-thinking and sustainable living solutions to the region. Axiom Prime Real Estate Development, renowned for its Dutch-inspired, luxurious developments, focuses on community-driven designs and cutting-edge technology. Their flagship projects in Jumeirah Village Triangle and Jumeirah Garden City (Satwa) exemplify their vision of creating spaces that promote a sense of belonging while unlocking growth potential. For more information, visit axiomprime.ae. Also Read: 2030 Renewable Energy Targets

title: Dubai’s Evolving Skyline: A Guide to Urban Growth
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Dubai, like any major city, is constantly evolving. Many end users and investors often find that the views they were promised with their properties are disrupted by new developments. My response to this is simple: if your view is that important to you, do your homework. Get the master plan for your community or, at the very least, review the block around your future property. If the plots around you are undeveloped, it’s only a matter of time before something will be built. Take, for example, the residents of Palma Villas who are upset about Como Tower. Did they really think that the empty plot next door would stay vacant forever for them to use as a litter box for their pets? And then there are the people in JBR, who assumed that the first-row waterfront plots, temporarily used as parking lots, would remain open spaces for their cars to bask in the sun. Unfortunately, that’s not how urban development works. A perfect illustration of Dubai’s dynamic nature is the case of Cayan Tower, formerly known as Infinity Tower. When the RTA moved the bridge connecting to the marina island, a new premium plot of land was freed up. And what came next? The world’s tallest hotel, Ciel Tower, was built right there. It’s a prime example of how, in Dubai, undeveloped land doesn’t stay that way for long—and when it’s used, it’s often for something remarkable. This isn’t unique to Dubai. Major cities worldwide face similar situations. In New York, for example, the construction of 432 Park Avenue—one of the tallest residential buildings in the world—disrupted the iconic views for many residents in Midtown Manhattan and the Upper East Side. People who had long enjoyed unobstructed views of Central Park suddenly found themselves looking at a new luxury tower instead. Billionaire’s Row along 57th Street in New York saw the rise of towers like One57, Central Park Tower, and 111 West 57th Street, forever changing the skyline and blocking the park views for many older buildings in the area. In cities like New York, rapid development is just part of life. London has seen its fair share of skyline changes too. The Shard, the tallest building in the UK, transformed the city’s skyline and altered views across Southwark and central London. Many properties that once had panoramic views of Tower Bridge now see a very different landscape with the completion of The Shard. Back in Dubai, the same applies to residents on The Palm, who once had clear views of the Marina and the Al-Sufouh skyscraper block, but are now facing the new Dubai Harbour community. While the Marina skyline was impressive, the Dubai Harbour development offers something equally appealing, with the bonus of cruise ships docking nearby. It may not be what they originally expected, but it’s still a world-class view, enhanced if anything. At least in Dubai, the process is handled with vision and purpose. Other cities, like Hong Kong, have faced similar disruptions. In the West Kowloon Cultural District, new developments have impacted the views of residents in Yau Ma Tei and Tsim Sha Tsui, who previously enjoyed sweeping vistas across the harbor toward Hong Kong Island. These new high-rise developments have completely altered the cityscape. Ultimately, whether it’s Dubai, New York, London, or Hong Kong, rapid urban growth and changing skylines are inevitable in world-class cities. In Dubai, these changes come with a certain agility, often transforming the city for the better. It’s all part of the evolving landscape of major cities worldwide. title: Land is Scarce, Repurpose: Unlocking Dubai’s Urban Potential
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As Dubai continues to grow and evolve, the strategic utilization of its scarce land resources within prime areas has become more crucial than ever. The city has undergone transformative projects where underutilized or misaligned plots of land were repurposed to unlock their highest potential. These efforts reflect the visionary approach of the government and master developers, driven by the understanding that certain plots are too valuable to remain in their current state. One such project exemplifying this forward-thinking strategy is the reshaping of the Safa Park area. The government strategically acquired surrounding villas and properties, even repurposing part of the park itself, to carve out a new channel for the Dubai Canal. This move transformed the connectivity of the city, linking the Arabian Gulf from Ras Al Khor through Business Bay and Safa Park, effectively turning key parts of Deira and Bur Dubai into an island. This monumental infrastructure project not only elevated the city’s landscape but also unleashed untapped value from previously static land, making way for super high-end projects on the canal. A similar initiative is the Jumeirah Garden City. In this case, Meraas undertook the ambitious task of acquiring and demolishing old villas in the Satwa area, clearing the way for a new community that serves as a vibrant bridge between City Walk, Sheikh Zayed Road, and Downtown Dubai. By reclaiming and revitalizing the area, Meraas created a dynamic, modern development that complements the surrounding regions and adds immense value to the overall urban fabric. These examples of bold interventions in urban planning and development are models that must continue to be replicated. There are many areas, particularly along Sheikh Zayed Road, that are grossly underutilized despite their prime locations. For instance, several villa communities along this major artery of the city occupy massive, strategically important plots that remain dormant or misaligned with the city’s broader vision. To fully capitalize on the value of these plots, they either need to be reclaimed by the government or rezoned to serve more fitting purposes, unlocking their potential as commercial, residential, or mixed-use developments. Al Quoz is another critical area that demands reevaluation. Currently, it houses a mix of residential, commercial, and industrial zones that are out of sync with its true potential. Relocating the industrial component of Al Quoz to specialized zones such as Dubai Industrial City (DIC), Dubai Investments Park (DIP), or IMPZ, would free up substantial land, which could then be repurposed for more valuable, community-oriented uses. This move could reinvigorate the area, bringing new life and economic activity while allowing industrial operations to thrive in dedicated hubs. Similarly, the Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC) should be reconsidered. Moving it to Expo City, with its expansive infrastructure and post-Expo legacy, provides a ready-made destination for events and trade shows, allowing DWTC to be relocated and freeing up valuable central land. Repurposing this area into a large-scale, vibrant community would not only create significant land availability but also drive further traffic and energy toward Expo City, fulfilling its potential as a long-term commercial and residential hub. One of the more glaring misuses of land lies in the Jumeirah Lakes Towers (JLT) area. A notable portion of JLT includes labor accommodations and industrial zones that are no longer the highest and best use for such prime real estate. Reclaiming this land under the authority of the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) would allow it to be integrated into the broader JLT community. These plots could be transformed into valuable residential, commercial, or retail spaces that would significantly enhance the area’s vibrancy and utility. With that brief in mind, perhaps the most absurd example of wasted land is on Palm Jumeirah. The spectacle of Palm West and Palm East—two low-rise, low-density studio buildings sitting on the most prime waterfront plots of the “eighth wonder of the world.” Taking some of the most coveted land on the planet and turning it into a suburban-style parking lot. Instead of incorporating parking into the building’s structure, the developer graciously sacrificed two more invaluable plots to create open-air parking bays. So now, studio tenants park their cars on these super premium dirt patches—where the land alone is worth a huge fortune. In fact, those parking bays are likely worth more than the entire studio building as a whole. It’s almost unimaginable to be pulling into what could easily be the most expensive piece of land your car will ever touch. Image credit These buildings and their open-air parking lots are sitting on some of the most coveted waterfront land in Dubai, falling short of the grandeur that should define this location. It’s not just a missed opportunity, it’s a downright lost treasure and misuse of ultra-prime real estate. These plots should be repurchased at any cost and repurposed into something that actually deserves to stand on Palm Jumeirah—developments that make full use of the unparalleled views and prestige that come with this world-famous destination. In conclusion, the development strategies employed in Dubai must continue to focus on maximizing the value of scarce land resources. Whether through government intervention or private enterprise, every underutilized plot represents an opportunity to recapture its value. With smart zoning, repurchasing, and repurposing strategies, Dubai can continue its trajectory as one of the world’s most innovative and forward-thinking cities. title: The Hidden Potential of Abandoned Projects: From Failure to World-Class Triumphs
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: Is there a sight more depressing than an abandoned project in the heart of a bustling city? Standing as a testament to failure, a silent witness to the unrealized dreams and aspirations it was meant to embody. However, there are times when such a depressing sight is, in fact, a blessing in disguise. Across the globe, and particularly in Dubai, there are countless examples of abandoned or stalled developments that have been revived, repurposed, and transformed into iconic landmarks—sometimes even breaking world records in the process. Dubai, known for its resilience and creativity, has seen several such transformations. One notable example is the Marina Yacht Club. Initially a two-story building that was underperforming on a rare and valuable plot, it was redeveloped into a towering skyscraper by Vida Emaar, along with a massive new yacht club. This redevelopment has made it one of the most sought-after residential locations in Dubai Marina, where finding new plots is nearly impossible. Another example is the Meydan Beach Club on Jumeirah Beach Residence (JBR), one of the best beach plots in JBR. It was repurposed into the gigantic, luxurious Five Hotel and Residences. Building on this success, Sensoria at Five, another luxury skyscraper, is currently under construction on the same plot, further cementing the value of once-failed projects. Among Dubai’s most iconic unfinished developments is the Dubai Pearl, a massive 7-million-square-foot plot at the base of Palm Jumeirah. Although it remains incomplete, its sheer size and iconic location make it an incredibly valuable asset. Once revived, it would be nearly impossible to put a price tag on such prime real estate, and it will potentially redefine the city’s skyline. One of the most remarkable revivals in recent times is the Pentominium Tower by Trident, once an abandoned vision. It is now being transformed into the Six Senses Tower, which will claim the title of the world’s tallest residential building. With lush, super high-end finishes and unparalleled designs, this project is set to redefine luxury living. Similarly, just a few plots down, Al Qabda Holding’s stalled project was picked up by London Gate in collaboration with the renowned watchmaker Franck Muller. The development will feature a state-of-the-art mechanical clock, set to be the tallest in the world, adding a new landmark to Dubai’s list of record-breaking achievements. These projects highlight the resilience and innovation that characterize Dubai’s approach to development. What were once considered failures or eyesores are now setting new global standards, proving that with the right vision, any project can be transformed into a world-class success. Globally, similar success stories can be found. In New York, the Hudson Yards development transformed an underutilized industrial area into one of the largest and most expensive private real estate projects in U.S. history. In London, the Battersea Power Station, long abandoned, has been revitalized into a thriving hub of residential, retail, and office spaces, with major companies like Apple choosing it as their headquarters. Both in Dubai and across the world, these examples show that even the most challenging projects can become iconic successes. What might appear as setbacks are often just opportunities waiting to be realized, proving that vision and determination can turn failure into a record-breaking triumph. title: The Rise of Private Master Developers in Dubai: A Developer’s Perspective
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: As a Dubai-based developer, I’ve witnessed firsthand the challenges and disappointments that come with investing in numerous promising communities. Time and again, master developers have promised the moon but ended up delivering a terrain that resembles it instead. It has become clear that investing and developing within certain master developments is akin to tossing the dice at a casino. However, private master developers have stepped in and delivered truly exceptional communities. Majid Al Futtaim’s Tilal Al Ghaf, for instance, stands out as perhaps the most astounding community delivered in Dubai at its price point. The quality of materials and craftsmanship surpasses most others. Had they been granted the luxury of choosing the most prime locations, they would have undoubtedly topped any other community by far. Reflecting on this, it’s evident that private master developers are outperforming their semi-government counterparts—though Emaar remains a notable exception. Emaar has consistently demonstrated that they operate more like a private entity, without relying on government grants or favors. This sets them apart from others who, despite having vast land banks and the ability to pick prime spots, have left them severely underdeveloped. Examples include Dubai Science Park, Studio City, Healthcare City 2, and many others. Looking back, when District One was managed by Sobha, it was a trailblazing community, the first of its kind. However, after Meydan took over the remaining development, we struggled to achieve any solid profits. We were among just 5 of 50 plots that were actually built. Delving deeper, the entire Dubai-land area, initially managed by Dubai Properties, was eventually sold to private master developers like Damac, who transformed it into the successful Damac Hills community. Similarly, what was once Golf City, another project by Dubai Properties, was reimagined as Damac Lagoons by Damac. Tilal Al Ghaf, another example, was picked up from Dubai Properties and developed into a paradise community. title: The Saudi Industry Ministry Expands its Offerings to the Non-Profit Sector
author: Entrepreneur Mirror
excerpt: RIYADH: New electronic services and a thorough operational plan for 2024 have helped Saudi Arabia better position the non-profit sector in its mining and industrial sectors. The new project was unveiled by the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, which highlighted six main goals to increase the nonprofit sector’s contribution. According to an official release, these objectives include raising domestic investments, developing non-oil industrial exports, enhancing workforce skills, and offering various supportive services. Under its Vision 2030 framework, the Kingdom is actively pursuing a broad industrial and economic transformation to diversify its economy from relying on oil. A key component of this transition is the National Industrial Strategy, which was introduced in 2022 and focusses on developing industrial capabilities, boosting domestic production, and promoting sustainable economic growth. The ministry’s website provides information on the new electronic services, which include applications for forming non-profit organisations and asking for the transfer of technical oversight to these organisations. Currently, the ministry oversees five significant non-profit organisations, including the Industrial Exporters Association, the Supply Chain and Procurement Society, and the Pharmaceutical Industry Association. Additionally, it is in charge of the Automotive Manufacturers Association and the Industrial Loss Prevention and Risk Mitigation Association.
